PART I—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, thg High Court, Government 
Treasury, etc. 
GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND FAMILY PLANNING 
Public Mealtb 
NOTIFICATION 


/2R-15/73.—lst January 1974.—Jn exercise of the power 
gonferred Ay section 30 of the West ‘Bengal Vaccination Act, 1973 (West 
ct XXXVII of 1973), the Governor is pleased hereby to make the 
followhg rules, namely:— 


RULES 


1. Short title——-These rules may be called the West Bengal Vaccination 
Rules, 1974. 


2. Definitions.—In these rules, unless there is anything repugnant in the 
subject or context,— 


(a) “Act”, means the West Bengal Vaccination Act, 1973. 


(b) “Assistant Superintendent of Vaccination” meane an officer appointed 
as Assistant Superintendent of Vaccination by the Stafe Govern- 
ment under sub-section (3) of section 11 of the Act. 


(c) “Inspector of Vaccination” means an officer appointed by the Stafe 
Government as Inspector of Vaccination under sub-section (3) of 
section 11 of the Act. 


(d) “Superintendent of Vaccination” means an officer appointed by State 
Government as Superintendent of Vaccination under clause (i) of 
section 2 of the Act. 


3. Qualifications required for appointment as Superintendent of Vaccima- 


tion—A Superintendent of Vaccination shall possess the following 
qualifications, namely: 


(a) the qualification of a medical practitioner specified in clause (e) of 
Section 2 of the Act, and 


4(1) 


4(2) 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, JANUARY |, 1974 


[Parr 1 


পা পিপি পরার, ھے‎ 
পাস্তা: যারা ০ سس ھ۔ےتت .سس ہہ سپٹ‎ — 


(b) a University Diploma in Public Health and/or Diploma of the Faculty 
of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene, West Bengal: 


Provided that the State Government may in exceptional circumstances 
relax the requirement of the qualification referred to in clause (b). 


4. Vaccination hours at a vaccination centre——Vaccination at a vaccina- 
tion centre shall be performed within the office hours prevailing in the district 
or area under the local authority in which the vaccinating centre is situated. 


5. Attendance for ascertaining result of vaccination—The direction 
referred to in section 6 of the Act shall be given in Form | to the guardian of 
the child and in Form 2 to the person concerned. 


6. Certificate of successful vaccination—The certificate of successful 
vaccination referred to in sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Act shall be in 
Form 3 


7. Repetition of vaccination.—Direction referred to in sub-section (2) of 
section 7 shall be given in Form 4 to the guardian of a child and in Form 5, to 
the person concerned. 


8. Certificates for insusceptibility to successful vaccination.—(1) The 
certificate for temporary insusceptibility to ‘vaccination referred to in sub- 
section (1) of section 8 of the Act shall be issued in Form 6. 


(2) The certificate for permanent insusceptibility to vaccination as referred 
to in sub-section (2) of section 8 of the Act shall be issued in Form 7. 


9. Manner of vaccination and _ revaccination.—The vaccine shall be 
introduced into the skin at a single site preferably over the outer aspect of the 
upper arm after reasonable cleansing by multiple puncture of ten to fifteen 
perpendicular strokes with a sterile bifurcated needle. 


10. Measures in the event of an outbreak of smallpox.—The direction 
referred to in sub-section (1) of section 10 of the Act shall be given in Form 8 
by the Superintendent of Vaccination to the guardian of any child or any 
person within his jurisdiction as the case may be. 


11. Notice for vaccination, under section 11.—A notice referred to in 
sub-section (1) of section 11 of the Act shall be in Form 9. 


12. Duties and functions of a Superintendent of Vaccination.—(l) The 
Superintendent of Vaccination shall be responsible for carrying out the 
provisions of the Act and the rules in the area within his jurisdiction. 


(2) The Superintendent of Vaccination shall keep himself informed about 
the presence of unprotected children and persons and shall take steps for their 
portection against smallpox by successful vaccination. For this purpose he 
Shall visit different areas and localities within his jurisdiction, as frequently 
as the occasion may require. 


(3) The Superintendent of Vaccination shall enquire into and ascertain the 
source of infection and distribution of any incidence of smallpox in the area 
within his jurisdiction. 


(4) On receiving the information of an outbreak of smallpox in the area 
within his jurisdiction, the Superintendent of Vaccination shall visit without 
delay the locality where the outbreak has occurred and_ shall take such 
measures for preventing the spread of the disease. He shall also forthwith 
report the particulars of every such outbreak, simultaneously to the Deputy 
Director of Health Services (Public Health), West Bengal, and Assistant 
Director of Health Services (Smallpox), West Bengal. An intimation by 
telegram/rediogram should also be sent to the Director-General of Health 
Services, Government of India, when smallpox is noted for the first time in 
the area within his jurisdiction as also when the epidemic condition subsides. 


(5) In the course of his inspection of the vaccination work the Superintend- 
ent of Vaccination shall carefully ascertain, with due reference to the 
proportion of population, the number already protected by vaccination, the 
quality of vaccinations performed by the vaccinator, quality of vaccine lymph 


ene used and the merit of the work performed by subordinate inspecting 
Staff.

(6) The Sup2rintendent of Vaccination shal! carefully examine the registers 
maintained by the vaccinators as also those maintained by hospitals, health 
centres, maternity centres, nursing homes and other medical institutions in the 
area within his jurisdiction including those registers for recording left out 
unprotected children and persons in the course of his inspection tours. 


(7) At the close of each calendar year, the Superintendent of Vaccination 
shall, in Form 10, make an annual report of vaccination done in the area 
within his jurisdiction during the calendar year and submit it to the Deputy 
Director of Health Services (Public Health), West Bengal, with copies to the 
Director, State Bureau of Health Intelligence, and Assistant Director of Health 
Services (Smallpox), West Bengal, by the 15th of January next year. 


(8) The Superintendent of Vaccination shall furnish the Deputy Director of 
Health Services (Public Health), West Bengal, as also the Assistant Director 
of Health Services (Smallpox), West Bengal, with periodical reports and 


Statistical returns as may be directed from time to time by the Director of 
Health Services. 


(9) The Superintendent of Vaccination shall inform of any outbreak of 
smallpox in the area within his jurisdiction to the Superintendent of 
Vaccination in the adjacent areas. 


13. Qualification required for appointment as Assistant Superintendent of 
Vaccination.—An Assistant Superintendent of Vaccination shall possess the 
following qualifications, namely: 


(a) the qualification of a medical practitioner specified in clause (e) of 
section 2 of the Act, and 


(b) a University Diploma in Public Health and/or Diploma of the Faculty 
of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene, West Bengal: 


Provided that the State Government may in exceptional circumstances 
relax the requirements of the qualification referred to in clause (b). 


14. Qualifications required for the appointment of Inspector of Vaccina- 


eee Inspector of Vaccination shall possess the following qualifications, 
namely: 


(a) he must have passed the School Final Examination or its equivalent; 


(b) he must have passed an examination for the training of Sanitary 
Inspector as recognised by the State Government; 


(c) he shall possess knowledge of the working and operation of the Act 
and the maintenance of register, returns, forms and_ certificates 
required to be maintained under the Act; 


(d) he shall possess an adequate knowledge of the technique of 
vaccination, including— 


(i) approved method of performing vaccination; 

(ii) ability to recognise a satisfactory vesicle, pustule and a typical 
vaccination scar and remedial steps neccssary in the case of 
complication; 

(111) phenomena of smallpox; 


(e) he shall be able to ride a cycle over long distances. 


15. Records of vaccination to be maintained in hospital, health centre, 
etc.—The Superintendent of every hospital, Medical Officer in charge of every 
health centre, maternity centre or any other medical institution and the medical 


authority of every nursing home shall maintain the following ‘records and 
registers, namely: 


(1) Register of new-born along with their vaccination status in Form 11. 
(2) Register of ail patients admitted and treated in the institution showing 
vaccination status in Form 12. 


16. Notice for inspection and detection of unprotected child and person.— 
A notice referred to in section 15 of the Act shall be in Form 13.

17. Application for issue of duplicate certificate—An application referred 
to in section 29 of the Act shall be in Form 14. 


18. Qualifications required for appointment 85 vaccinator.—{1) Any 
person shall not be qualified for appointment as a vaccinator unless he— 


(a) is a medical practitioner, or, 


(b) has passed School Final Examination or its equivalent and possesses 
a certificate of competency granted in Form 15 after oral and 
practical examination by one of the following officers, namely: 


(i) District Health Officer, 

(ii) Municipal Health Officer, 

(iii) Subdivisional Health Officer, 

(iv) Military Medical Officer of a Cantonment, 
(v) Health Officer of a Mines Board of Health: 


Provided that a person who is employed under the Government of West Bengal 
or any local authority on the date of coming into force of the Act for 
administration of vaccination against smallpox may continue to hold office as 
such subject to the terms and conditions of service applicable to him even 
though he does not fulfil the qualifications laid down in clauses (a) and (b). 


(2) Every person who desires to present himself/herself for the examina- 
tions referred to in clause (b) of sub-rule (1) shall, if he/she had not attended 
a vaccination class in a recognised Medical School in India and obtained a 
certificate of competency from the Superintendent thereof, submit evidence to 
the satisfaction of certifying authority referred to in the said clause prior to 
his examination that he— 


(a) has been engaged in vaccination work, in the capacity of an apprentice 
or assistant, for a period of at least six months, and 


(b) possesses— 


(i) knowledge of approved method of performing vaccination and 
ability to read results thereof; 


(ii) knowledge of provisions of the West Bengal Vaccination Act, 1973, 
and rules framed thereunder; and 


(iii) knowledge of the registers, returns, forms and certificate required 
to be maintained under the Act and rules framed thereunder. 


19. Duties of vaccinators—In addition to the duties imposed upon him 
under the Act and rules framed thereunder and also by any other laws for the 
time being in force regarding vaccination, a vaccinator shall perform the 
following duties, namely: 


(a) to visit by rotation every village/ward in his/her allotted jurisdiction 
for which purpose he/she should prepare an advance tour 
programme and get it approved by his Inspector of Vaccination-in- 
charge without whose knowledge no alteration of the programme 
can be made; 


(b) to maintain a diary for recording day-to-day work including tours ; 


(c) to operate the approved method of vaccination in one point with a 
bifurcated needle using only vaccine of standard potency; 


(d) to note the batch number and date of expiry of the vaccine and 
against each vaccination performed in his/her record to facilitate 
issue of certificate later on as indicated in section 7 of the Act; 


(6) to attend regularly vaccination centres, if any, opened in his/her 
jurisdiction; 


(f) to report immediately any incidence of smallpox within his/her area 
to the Inspector-in-charge; 


(g) to remain responsible for due care and preservation of equipments, 
vaccine, records and register supplied to him/her and maintained 
by him/her for the discharge of his/her duties; 


(h) whenever it shall come to the notice of a vaccinator that any child 
required to be vaccinated according to the provision of 
the Act, is still unprotected, he/she shall request the parents or 
guardians of such child to have the child vaccinated forthwith and

(j) he/she shall maintain a register of all children and persons in his/her

their lifetime in Form 17 


20. Power of Director of Health Services, West Bengal.—(1) The Director 
of Health Services, West Bengal, may notify from time to time the nature, 


type and potency of the therapeutic substance to be administered as vaccine 
against smallpox. 


(2) Subject to the provisions of the Act or the rules the Director of Health 
Services, West Bengal, may from time to time issue to the officers appointed 
under the Act such directives as are considered necessary for the 
administration of the Act.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
HOME DEPARTMENT 
Transport 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 111-WT/6R-14/73.—4th January 1974.—The following draft of amend- 
ment which, in exercise of the power conferred by section 68 of the Motor 
Vihicles Act, 1939 (Act 4 of 1939), the Governor proposes to make in the 
Bengal Motor Vehicles Rules, 1940, published with notification No. 1930-P.L., 
dated the 215. September 1940, at pages 2655-2829 of Part 1 of the “Calcutta 
Gazette” of the 10th October 1940, as subsequently amended (hereinafter 
referred to as the said rules), is hereby published, as required by sub-section (1) 
of section 133 of the said Act, for the information of persons likely to be 
affected thereby. 


2. The draft will be taken into consideration om or after the 25th January 
1974, and any objection or suggestion with respect thereto, which may be 
received by the undersigned before that date, shall ba cofisidered. 


Draft amendments 
In the said rules,— 


(1) in rule 2, after clause (n), insert the following clauses, namely:— 


400) ‘composite permit’ means a permit issued under section 56 of the 
Act, in respect of a public carrier goods vehicle for operation on 
National Highways and State Highways passing through, or 
terminating in, the State of West Bengal and other States and 
Union Territories in pursuance of a Special Reciprocal Agreement 
entered into by the State of West Bengal with other States and 
Union Territories; 


(p) ‘Special Reciprocal Agreement’ means an agreement entered into by 
the State of West Bengal with other States and Union Territories 
for the purpose of issuing composite permits under section 56 of 
the Act by the State Transport Authority or a Regional Transport 


19 


20 THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, JANUARY 4, 1974 (PART | 
সলিল ee te ہے‎ ee en ene 


Authority of any of the signatory States to promote long distance 
and inter-State transport of goods by road between those States 
and Union Territories; 


(q) ‘signatory State’ means a State or a Union Territory which is a party 
to a Special Reciprocal Agreement”; 


(2) after rule 63, insert the following rule, namely:— 


“63A. Grant of Composite Permits.—(1) The State Transport Authority, 
West Bengal, shall be the competent authority to issue composite 
permits.; 


(2) A composite permit issued by the State Transport Authority or a 
Regional Transport Authority of any of the signatory States other 
than the State of West Bengal shall be valid in the State of West 
Bengal without countersignature of the Regional Transport 
۳ھ"‎ or the State Transport Authority of the State of West 
Bengal; 


(3) A composite permit shall be granted only in relation to 38 public 
carrier goods vehicle, 


(a) which at the time of grant is not more than two years old reckoned 
from the date of its first registration as new; and 


(b) which has a registered laden weight of not less than 10,000 Kgs.; 


(4) An authorisation under a Special Reciprocal Agreement in the Form 
SRA-AUTH 91811 be granted to every public carrier goods 
vehicle, in respect of which a composite permit is issued under 
the signature and seal of the competent authority of the State of 
West Bengal on an application made in writing in the Form SRA- 


7 
(5) The following shall be the conditions of every composite permit:— 


(a) While operating in any area outside the State of West Bengal, 
goods shall not be picked up or set down between any two 
points lying 0ٌ within, the jurisdiction of the reciprocating 
States, 1.5. in such cases, the vehicle shall be prohibited from 
carrying any intra-State business. 


(b) The vehicle shall be painted in the colour specified by the State 
Transport Authority, West Bengal, at the time of issuing the 
permit and shall carry special markings to 093 1 
specified. A board showing the following inscription shall be 
carried prominently in front of the vehicle at the top above 
the “PUBLIC CARRIER” board, the colour of the letters and 
the background being specified by the State Transport Autho- 
rity, West Bengal, at the time of issuing the permit: 


Inscription 


—_—_—— —— = —— 


COMPOSITE PERMIT 
(Under Special Reciprocal Agreement) 
করি: ا سی دا سکس اھ سا‎ 


(**Hero, write the names of the States and Union 
Territories applicable), 
(c) Each vehicle covered by a composite permit shall have two drivers. 

The vehicle shall be provided with a seat across the full width 
of the vehicle, behind the driver’s seat, providing facility for 
the spare driver to stretch himself and sleep. 


(d) The vehicle shall at all times carry Bill/Bills of Lading in Form 
SRA-LAD. The goods conveyed shall be in conformity with 
the declaration in the Bill/Bills of Lading.

(6) Quarterly returns in Form SRA-QLY shall be submitted by the 
permit-holder to the Secretary, State Transport Authority, West 
Bengal, with as many copies as may be specified at the time 
issuing the permit by the State Transport Authority, to reach 
him not later than the 30th day of the month succeeding the 
quarter concerned. 


(f) The vehicle shall conform to, and comply with, all the provisions 
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, as well as the provisions of 
the Bengal Motor Vehicles Rules, 1940, subject to such restric- 
tions as may be imposed by the State Governments from time 
to time under the provisions of the Act. 


(g) The vehicle shall be subject to the load and other restrictions as 
may be imposed by the Government of the signatory State in 
the area of which the vehicle is plying for the time being. 


(h) The vehicle shall at all times carry a valid certificate of fitness, 
a certificate of insurance, the certificate of registration, the 
composite permit and the authorisation issued in pursuance of 
a Special Reciprocal Agreement. 


(i) The holder of the composite permit shall pay the Motor Vehicles 
tax in West Bengal and shall also pay such amounts in lieu of 
taxes due to the other signatory States in respect of the 
vehicle, as may be stipulated under a Special Reciprocal 
Agreement. 


(j) The vehicle, as soon as it becomes seven years old reckoned from 
the date of its first registration as new, shall be replaced by a 
later model vehicle with the previous approval of the State 
Transport Authority, West Bengal. 


(k) Each applicant for a composite permit shall have to choose a 
minimum number of States including West Bengal for opera- 
tion as stipulated in a Special Reciprocal Agreement. An 
option once exercised will not be allowed to be changed except 
in accordance with the stipulations of the said Special Reciprocal 
Agreement. 


(I) The provisions of the Act and these rules relating to the grant, 
revocation and suspension of permits shall apply to the grant, 
revocation and suspension of composite permits.”;

appeal against an order of the State Transport Authority,” insert 
the following words, figures, letters and brackets, namely:— 


“passed under sub-rule (f) of rule 109E or sub-rule (b) of rule 109F or 
passed”;

ABSTRACT OF CONDITIONS OF COMPOSITE PERMIT 


l. This authorises the operation of the vehicle on all the National and 
State Highways in the signatory States chosen for operation other than the 
State of West Bengal with deviations up to 30 Kms. on either side of the 


specified routes. 


2. While operating in any area outside the State of West Bengal, goods 
shall not be picked up or set down between any two points lying wholly within 
the jurisdiction of the reciprocating States, i.e., in such cases, the vehicle shall 
be prohibited from carrying any intra-State business. 


3. The vehicle shall be painted in the colour specified by the State 


Transport Authority, West Bengal, at the time of issuing the permit and shall 
carry special markings to be similarly specified. A board showing 016 
following inscription shall be carried prominently in front of the vehicle at the 
top above the ‘PUBLIC CARRIER’ board, the colour of the letters and the 
background being specified by the State Transport Authority, West Bengal, at 


the time of issuing the permit: 
Inscription 


COMPOSITE PERMIT | 


(Under Special Reciprocal Agreement) 


Valld in?” سس می وی وی‎ ০2222522585 


(**Here, Write, the names of the States and Union 
Territories applicable) 


4. Each vehicle covered by a composite permit shall have two drivers. 
The vehicle shall be provided with a scat across the full width of the vehicle, 
behind the driver's seat, providing facility for the spare driver to stretch 
himself and sleep. 


5. The vehicle shall at all times carry Bill/ Bills of Lading in Form SRA- 
LAD. The goods conveyed shall be in conformity with the declaration in the 
Bill/ Bills of Lading. 


6. Quarterly returns in Form SRA-QLY shall be submitted by the permit- 
holder to the Secretary, State Transport Authority, West Bengal, with as many 
copies as may be specificd at the time of issuing the permit by the State 
Transport Authority, to reach him not later than the 30th day cf the month 
succeeding the quarter concerned. 


7. The vehicle shall conform to, and comply with, all the provisions of the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, as well as the provisions of the Bengal Motor 
Vehicles Rules, 1940, subject to such restrictions as may be imposed by the 
State Governments from time to time under the provisions of the Act.

8. The vehicle shall be subject to the load and other restrictions as may 
be imposed by the Government of the signatory State in the area of which the 
vehicle is plying for the time being. 


9. The vehicle shall at all times carry a valid certificate of fitness, a 
certificate of insurance, the certificate of registration, the composite permit 
and the authorisation issued in pursuance of a Special Reciprocal Agreement. 


10. The holder of the composite permit shall pay the Motor Vehicles Tax 
in West Bengal and shall also pay such amounts in lieu of taxes due ) the 
other signatory States in respect of the vehicle, as may be stipulated under a 
Special Reciprocal Agreement. 


11. The vehicle, as soon as it becomes seven years old reckoned from the 
date of its first registration as new, shall be replaced by a later model vehicle 
with the previous approval of the State Transport Authority, West Bengal. 


12. Each applicant for a composite permit shall have to choose a minimum 
number of States including West Bengal for operation as stipulated under a 
Special Reciprocal Agreement. An option once exercised will not be allowed 
to be changed except in dccordance with the stipulations of the said Special 
Reciprocal Agreement. 


13. The provisions of the Act and these rules relating to the grant, revo- 
cation and suspension of permits shall apply to the grant, revocation and 
suspension of composite permits.

PART I—Orders and netifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


INFORMATION AND PUBLIC RELATIONS DEPARTMENT 
RESOLUTION 


No. 45735-IPR.—28th December 1973.—The question of award of Cash 
Prizes to feature films produced in West Bengal has been under active considera- 
tion of the Government for some time. 


With the object of encouraging the production in the State, of films of high 
aesthetic and technical standards and of social, educational and cultural value, 
the Government, after careful consideration, has been pleased to constitute an 


Award Committee for the said purpose composed of the following persons as 
members : 


(1) Minister|Minister of State-in-charge, Information and Public Relations 
Department—Chairman. 


(2) Not more than six persons distinguished in the fields of film apprecia- 
tion, arts and literature nominated by Government. 


The Deputy Secretary to the Government of West Bengal, Information and 
Public Relations Department, will act as Convenor-Secretary of the Committee. 


The Governor has also been pleased to make the following rules for Cash 
Awards of films produced in West Bengal in terms of this resolution : 


RULES 
(i) These rules shall be called Rules for Cash Award for Films. 
(ii) The following categories of Cash Awards will be available under these 


rules : ۱ 
(i) Ist best feature film .. i .. Rs. 20,000.00 
2nd best feature film .. -7 a Rs. 15,000.00 
3rd best feature film .. 7 . Rs. 10,000.00 
(ii) (a) Best Director ae 7 .» Rs. 10,000.00 
(b) Best Script Writer oF -. Rs, 5,000.00

(i) Best Make-up Man ٦ Rs. 5,000.00 


An additional sum of Rs. 6,000 is to be provided for payment of suitable 
awards to the Assistants in the categories of (a), (b), (c), (f), (g), (h) and 
(i) above in such a manner that no individual Assistant gets more than Rs. 500 
and to no group more than Rs. 1,000 should be allotted. The amount of 
Rs. 1,000 may be divided equally amongst the Assistants in that particular 
group. 


Explanation 


(i) The term “producer”, “director”, “cameraman”, “actor”, “actress”, “child 
actor|actress”, “playback singer”, “‘music director”, “screen play writer|script 
writer’, “lyric writer”, used in these rules will be construed as referring to the 
“producer”, “director”, “cameraman”, “actor”, “actress”, “child actor|actress”, 
“playback singer”, “music director”, “screen play writer|script writer”, “lyric 
writer”, as the case may be as given in the credit titles of the film duly certified 
by the Central Board of Film Cehsors. 


(ii) All films produced in West Bengal and released in the calendar year 
will be eligible for entry. A declaration to that effect shall be made by the 
producer or any other duly authorised person in the form contained in the 
Schedule hereto annexed. 


(iii) Entries for the awards will be invited every year by a date to ০৪ 
specified by the Government in a notice to be published in the “Calcutta 
Gazette” and also in newspapers. 


Every application for entry shall be made on the form contained in the 
schedule to these Rules and be accompanied by an entry fee of Rs. 25. 


(iv) Each entrant will submit, at his cost, to the Secretary, Award Committee 
for Films, or to any other authority as may be specified by Government from 
time to time a print of the film as certified by the Central Board of Film Censors 
at the time and place indicated by the Secretary, Award Committee for Film, 
or authority, twenty copies of synopsis and an equivalent number of copies of 
songs, if any. 


The cntrant of a film selected for vicwing by the Award Committee will 
submit, at his cost, the required number of copies of the detailed dialogue, 
6 stills, script in BengalilEnglish as well as publicity material relating thereto, 
in addition to the print and 15 additional copies of synopsis of the film. 


The decision of the Committee whether a film is eligible to be entered for 
the awards and whether any film is a feature film, national integration film, 
children’s film, information film, educationallinstructional film, experimental film 
for the awards will be final. 


The last date of entry may be relaxed at the discretion pf the Government 
in exceptional cases. 


No film which has not been entered for the Cash Awards will be considered 
eligible for these awards. 


(v) All transport costs and other incidental expenses on the consignment 
and return of the film and publicity materials will be payable by the entrant. 


(vi) All films will be submitted at the owners’ risk and while the Committee 
will take very reasonable care of the films submitted, it cannot accept any 
responsibility whatsoever for loss or damage to the film while in its possession. 


(vii) Government shall be entitled to retain the print of the film entered 
for the awards and which receives an award in cash, or payment of print cost. 


(viii) Canvassing in any form in respect of an entry will render that entry 
liable to be disqualified. Any member of the Committee found canvassing for 
a particular film is liable to be disqualified for membership of the Committee.

(ix) If the producer and director of an award-winning film happen to be 
the same person and eligible for award in both capacities, he will be given an 
award either as a producer or a director and not both. 


(x) The decisions of the Government in respect of the awards and of inter- 
pretation of these rules shall be final and no appeal shall lie against them. 


(xi) A person who participates in the Cash Awards for films under these 
Rules shall be deemed to have accepted these rules. 


Ordered that a copy of the Resolution be published in an extraordinary issue 
of the “Calcutta Gazette” and copies hereof forwarded to all Departments of 
the Government and also to Members of the Committee. 

By order of the Governor,

Cash Awards for Films

constituting the Committee for Cash Award of Prizes for Films and making rules 
for grant of such awards entries for the cash awards for films applications are 
hereby invited in respect of the films produced in West Bengal and released in 
the Calendar year 1973. The value of awards will be as follows: 


1. (i) Ist best feature film 3 .. Rs. 20,000.00 
2nd best feature film ۰ .. Rs. 15,000.00 

3rd best feature film 7 .. Rs. 10,000.00

PART I—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government 
Treasury, etc. 


GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
LABOUR DEPARTMENT 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 38]1-L.W./LW/1R-10/73.—7th November 1973.—The following draft 
of rules, which in exercise of the power conferred by section 64 of the Factories 
Act, 1948 (Act 63 of 1948), the Governor proposes to make, is hereby published 
as required by section 115 of the said Act for the information of ptrsons likely 
to be affected thereby. 


The draft will be taken into consideration after three months from the 
date of publication of the Notification in the “Calcutta Gazette”, and any 
objection or suggestion with respect thereto which may be received by the 
undersigned within three months from the date of publicatjor of the Notifica- 
tion in the “Calcutta Gazette” shall be duly considered, ~ 


DRAFT RULES 


1. Short title—These rules may be called the West Bengal Factories 
(Exemption) Rules, 1974. 


2. Definitions.—In these rules— 


(a) “the Act” means the Factories Act, 1948 (Act 63 of 1948); 
(b) “form” means the form appended to these rules; 


(c) “holiday” includes a compensatory rest period referred to in sub-clause 
(c) of clause (40) of rule 9 of these rules; and 


(d) “section” means a section of the Act. 


3. Persons deemed to be holding positions of supervision or management, 
etc., in a factory.—(1) The following persons employed in a factory shall, under 
sub-section (1) of section 64, be deemed to be persons holding positions of 
টা or management or persons employed in a_ confidential position, 
namely:— 


(a) Manager, 


(b) any other person who, in the opinion of the Inspector, holds a position 
of supervision or management or is employed in a confidential 
position. 


321) 


32(2) THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, JANUARY 8, 1974 . {Part 1 


১১১ 


(2) A record of the names and designations of all persons defined under 
sub-rule (1) shall be maintained correctly, legibly, in ink, and shall be available 
in every factory for examination by the Inspector. 


4. Weekly working hours.—No adult worker exempted from the provision 
of section 51 other than an adult male worker employed under rule 6 of urgent 
repairs shall be allowed to work for more than 56 hours in any week. 


5. Holidays due to workers.—Notwithstanding anything contained in these 
rules no adult worker in respect of whom exemption from the provisions of 
section 52 has been granted shall be deprived of any holiday due to him in 
accordance with the provisions of section 53. 


6. Urgent repairs.—The provisions of sections 91, 52, 54, 55, 56 and 6] 
7 not apply to adult male workers employed on urgent repairs, on condition 
that— 


(a) throughout the full period of such work, a notice stating the names of 
the workers employed thereon, shall be displayed and maintained in 
accordance with the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 108; 


(b) a notice stating fully the nature of the repairs, the time of commence- 
ment of work on the same and its probable duration shall be sent 
to the Inspector forthwith; 


(c) no worker shall be employed on such work for more than— 


(i) ten consecutive days without a holiday for a whole day, 

(ii) fifteen hours on any one day, 

(iii) thirty-nine hours during any three consecutive days, or 

(iv) sixty-six hours during each period of seven consecutive days; and 


(d) a statement showing the total number of hours worked each day in the 
week by each worker shall be sent to the Inspector within thirty-six 
hours after the completion of the work. 


Exvlanation.—“Urgent repairs” mean— 


(a) breakdown repairs to the motive power or plant and machinery of a 
factory which if not carried out expeditiously would involve danger 
to human life or safety or delay in resumption of the men 
manufacturing process; 


(b) breakdown repairs to ships which are essential to enable them to leave 
port at proper time or continue their normal operations in a sound 
condition; 

(c) repairs to commercial aircraft, its engines or other equipment done in 
a factory, which are essential to enable such aircrafts to leave air- 
port at proper time or continue their normal operations in an air- 
worthy condition; 


(d) breakdown repairs carried out in general engineering works or 
foundries to the motive power or plant of other factories, collieries, 
railways, dock-yards, harbours, tramways, motor transport, gas 
works, electrical generating and distributing stations and pumping 
stations, which are necessary to enable such concerns to maintain 
their services or resume their main manufacturing process with as 
little delay as possible; 


(e) breakdown repairs to tractors and cranes used in connection with 
construction projects; and 


(f) repairs in connection with a change of motive power, for example, 
from steam to electricity vr vice versa, when such repairs cannot ১৫ 
done without stoppage of the main manufacturing process. 


7. Boiler house and engine room attendants.—The provisions of section 51, 
52, 54, 55, 56 and 61 shall not apply to adult male workers engaged solely on 
the work of attending to boilers or prime movers, on condition that 


(a) the manager of the factory shall classify all such workers into groups 
according to the nature of their work; 


(b) a notice showing the group or groups of workers working under the 
provisions of this rule shall be displayed and maintained in 
accordance with the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 108;

ment under the Land Acquisition Aot, 1894 (Act I of 1894), in relation to tho acquisition of land for the purpose of

and measuring, more or less, -0990 of a hectare (02446 of an acre) are needed for the aforesaid public purnose at the

NOTIFICATION 


No. 1-P.A.—-9th January 1974.—In exercise of the powers conferred by 
section 7, read with section 8, of the West Bengal Salaries and Allowances 
Act, 1952 (West Ben. Act V of 1952), the Governor is pleased hereby to make 
the following rules, namely:— 


Rules 


Definition. .ا‎ These rules may be called the West Bengal Legislative Assembly 
(Presiding Officers’ Medical Attendance) Rules, 1973. 


2. In these rules, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or 
context:— 


(a) “Speaker” and “Deputy Speaker”, respectively, mean the Speaker and 
the Deputy Speaker of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly; 


(b) “hospital” means a hospital, health centre, dispensary, clinic or 
laboratory; 


(c) “medical attendance” means attendance for দাও advice (i) in 
a hospital, or (ii) at the consulting room of the medical practitioner, 
or (ili) at the residence of the patient and includes such patholo- 
gical, bacteriological, radiological, bio-chemical or other methods 
of examination for the purpose of diagnosis as may be considered 
necessary by the attending medical practitioner; 


(d) “medical practitioner” means a_ registered medical practitioner 
registered under the Bengal Medical Act, 1914 (Bengal Act VI of 
1914), the Paschim Banga Ayurvedic System of Medicine Act, 196] 
(West Ben. Act XIII of 1961), or the West Bengal Homeopathic © 
System of Medicine Act, 1963 (West Ben. Act ۸۸۸111 of 1963);

(6) “treatment” means the use of medical and surgical facilities available 
(1) at a hownital, or (ii) at the consulting room of the medical 
practitioner, or (iii) at the residence of the patient and includes— 

(i) the employment of such pathological, bacteriological, radiological, 
bio-chemical or other methods as are considered necessary by the 
attending medical practitioner; 


(ii) the use of such medicines, vaccines, sera or other therapeutic 
substances as are considered nevessary by the éevtending medical 
practitioner; 

(iii) medical an surgical services at continement; 

(iv) dental treatinent including supply of denture;

special nursing at the hospital as the attending medical practitioner 
may certify in writing to be essential for the recovery or for the 


prevention of a serious deterioration in the condition of the 
patient; 


(vii) blood transfusion. 


3. The Speaker and the Deputy Speaker shall be entitled to benefits of 
medical attendance and treatment in respect of themselves only as follows:— 


(a) Free medical attendance and treatment in State hospitals; 
(b) Re-imbursement of the cost of— 


(i) medical attendance and treatment in State-aided hospitals; ا‎ 


(ii) medical attendance and treatment by any medical practitioner 
either at his consulting room or at their residence; 


(11) pathological, bacteriological, radiological, bio-chemical or ‘other 
methods of examination for the purpose of diognosis carried out in 
a private laboratory or clinic; 


(iv) denture, if any; - 

(v) spectacles, if any; 

(vi) special nursing, if any; 

(vii) medicines, vaccines, sera or other therapeutic substances exclud- 


ing those supplied free of cost for treatment in a State or 
State-aided hospital; 


(vill) engagement of private attendant (bearer or ayah) in a State or 


State-aided hospital, if required, by the authorities of the said 
hospital. 


4. All claims for re-imbursement of medical expenses admissible under 
these rules except that relating to the fees paid to the medical r-acti.‘oners 
shall be supported by prescriptions and receipts or vouchers or cash memos, 
as the case may be, showing payments made by the patient.

THE WEST BENCAL PANCHAYAT ACT, 1973. 


[Passed by the West Bengal Legislature.) 


{Assent of the President was first published in the Calcutta} 
Gazette, Extraordinary, of the 17th January, 1974.) 


An Act to reorganise Panchayats in rural areas Of West 
Bengal and to provide for matters connected therewtth. 


WHEREAS it is expedient to reorganise Panchayats in rurak 
areas of West Bengal and to provide for matters connected 


therewith ; 


It is hereby enacted in the Twenty-fourth Year of the 
Republic of India, by the Legislature of West Bengal, ag

may itself effect the demolition and recover the cost thereof 
from the owner as a public demand. 


(7) Any person who erects any structure or building in 
contravention of the provisions of sub-section (7) shall be 
liable on conviction by a Magistrate to a fine which may ex- 
tend to two hundred and fifty rupees.

— Provided that the Munsif who would have had jurisdic- 
tion to try the suit but for the provisions of this Act, may, 
on ‘the application of any party to the suit made within 
thirty days of the decree or order of the Nyaya Panchayat, 
cuncel or modify the decree or order of the Nyaya Panchayat 
or direct a retrial of the suit by the same or any other 
Nyaya Panchayat if he is satinSied that there has been a 
failure of justice. 


75. If the plaintiff or defendant in any suit dies before 
the suit has been decided, the suit may, subject to the pro- 
visions of clause (d) of section 62, be proceeded with at the 
instance of, or against the legal representatives of, the 
deceased pluintif¥ or defendant, os the case may he. 


76. The decision of a Nyaya Panchayat on the question 
of title, legal character, contract or obligation shall not bind 
the parties except in respect of the suit in which such matter 
is decided, 


77. (1) The provisions of— 
(a) the West Bengal Court-fees Act, 1970, 


(b) the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, 
(6) the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and 
(d) the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, 
shall not upply to any trial before a Nyaya Panchayat. 


(2) The procedure to be followed by a Nyaya Panchayat 
in any trial, in the enforcement of its decisions and orders, 
and in the method of forming a quorum shall, subject to the 
provisions of this Act, be,in accordance with prescribed rules. 


78. No Nyaya Panchayat shall try any case or suit or 
other proceeding in which the Gram Panchayat concerned or 
any member of such Nyaya Panchayat is a party or is 
interested. 


79 (/) The Sessions Judge or the Sub-divisional Judicial

unother Judicial Magistrate who would have had jurisdiction

199. All members, officers and employees of the Gram 
Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zilla Parishad _ shall be 
deemed, when acting or purporting to act in pursuance of 
the discharge of their duties, or in the exercise of their 
powers under this Act or under the rules or bye-laws made 
thereunder, to be public servants within the meaning of 
section 21 of the Indian Penal Code. 


200. No suit or other legal proceeding shall lie against a 
Gram Panchayat, a Panchayat Samiti, a Zilla Parishad or 
against any member thereof or any officer or employee 
for anything in good faith done or intended to be done in 
pursuance of this Act or of any rules or bye-laws made 
thereunder.

No. 305-F.T.—25th مر‎ 1974.—In exercise of the power conferred by

Rules, 1972 (hereinafter referred to as the said rules), namely: 


ntertainments and Luxuries (Hotels and Restau- 


Amendments 


In the said rules,— 
(1) for rule 4, substitute the following rule, namely: 
“4. Any proprietor of a hotel or restaurant, which is provided with 


luxury and where an entertainment is provided, shall, within 
three days of the date of an entertainment or within three weeks 
of the date of publication of the Government of West Bengal, 
Finance (Taxation) Department, Notification No. 305-F.T., dated 
the 25th January 1974, in the “Calcutta Gazette”, whichever is 
later or, where the entertainment is a regular feature, within the 
seventh day of the month following the month for which the 
tax is due, or within three weeks of the date of publication of the

“Calcutta Gazette”, whichever is later, deposit the amount of 
entertainment tax recovered under rule 3 at the appropriate 
Government Treasury, and shall furnish, within ten days of the

ing particulars of cash memo/voucher/receipt/bill/ticket issued 
daily and the sum realised against the same and the amount of 
entertainment tax payable thereon along with the copy of the 
Treasury challan showing the payment of such amount. A 
register shall also be maintained by the proprietor in Form A.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
LAND UTILISATION AND REFORMS AND LAND AND LAND 
REVENUE DEPARTMENT 
Land Reforms 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 1384-L.Ref.—22nd January 1974.—The Governor is pleased hereby to 
constitute the West Bengal Kanungo Grade II Service and in exercise of the 
power conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution of India, to 
make the following rules regulating the recruitment and the conditions of 
service of persons appointed to such service, namely: 


Rules 


The pay, method of recruitment and the qualifications required for recruit- 
ধা to the West Bengal Kanungo Grade II Service, shall be 25 detailed 
elow:— 


1. Pay: Scale of pay Rs. 230—5—275—74—365—10—425 (with higher 
initial start at Rs. 275) (E.B. after 8th and 1600 stages]. 


2. Appointing Authority: Director of Land Records and Surveys, West 
Bengal. 


3. Method of recruitment: By selection from the rank of Settlement 
Peshkars/Clerks' Draftsman/Typists and similar other posts of 
equivalent rank (borne in the scale of pay of Rs. 230-425) who 
have served for at least 3 years continuously as such. Women 
candidates are not eligible. Selection shall be made by a 
Selection Board to be constituted by the Government for the 
purpose. 


4. Qualifications— 


(a) Age: Not exceeding 45 years on the Ist day of September of the 
year in which recruitment is made. The upper age limit may, 
however, be relaxed by the Government in special cases. 


(b) Education: Candidates must have 4d degree in Arts, Science, 
Commerce or Agriculture. 


(c) Physical fitness: (Candidates must be in sound health and physically 
fit for continuous outdoor touring in rural areas. 


5. Training: The candidates shall be required to undergo a course of 
training to be determined by the Director of Land Records and 
Surveys, West Bengal. In deserving cases, the Director of Land 
Records and Surveys, may exempt a candidate from undergoing 
training. The trainees shall ‘be given appointment on successful 
completion of the training. 


During the period of training, a trainee shall draw the pay and allowances 
at the rate last drawn by him. 
By order of the Governor,

PART I—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government 
Treasury, etc. 


GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
CO-OPERATION DEPARTMENT 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 100-Co-op./2R-17/73.—15th January 1974.—The following draft of rules 
which, in exercise of the power conferred by section 142 of the West Bengal 
Co-operative Societies Act, 1973, the Governor proposes to make to replace the 
Bengal Co-operative Societies Rules, 1942, as subsequently amended (herein- 
after referred to as the said rules), is hereby published, as required by 
sub-section (1) of the said section, for the information of persons likely to be 
affected thereby. 


The draft will be taken into consideration on or after the thirty-first day 
from the date of publication of this notification in the “Calcutta Gazette”, and 
any Objection or suggestion with respect thereto, which may be received by 
the undersigned before that day, shall be considered. 


Draft Rules 
CHAPTER I 


Preliminary 


1. Short title—These rules may be called the West Bengal Co-operative 
Socicties Rules, 1973. 


2. Definitions—(1) In these rules, unless there is anything repugnant in 
the subject or context— 


(a) “the Act” means the West Bengal Co-operative Societies Act, 1973; 


(b) “borrowed capital” means the total of loans, deposits and other 
borrowings of a co-operative society; 


(c) “Additional Registrar of Co-operative Societies”, “Joint Registrar of 
Co-operative Societies”, “Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Socie- 
ties”, “Assistant Registrar of Co-operative Societies’, “Chief 


188(1) 


188(2) THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, JANUARY 30, 1974 [PART | 


8২ পি হস সপ OE ০০০ 
Auditor of Co-operative Societies’, ‘District Auditor of Co-opera- 

tive Societies", and “Co-operative Development Officer” mean 

respectively persons appointed by those designations by the State 

Government to assist the Registrar of Co-operative Socicties; 


(d) “director” means a member of a managing committee but excludes a 
managing director; 


(e) “distrainer” means a person, who is empowered by the Registrar to 
distrain and sell the produce of mortgaged land including the 
standing crops thereon, in accordance with the provisions of 
section 99; 


(f) “member” includes delegates of members referred to in the proviso 
to sub-section (1) of section 20; : 


(g) “owned capital” means the total of paid up share capital and accumu- 
lated reserve fund and other funds created out of profits of a 
co-operative society or otherwise; 

(h) “schedule” means the schedule of forms appended to these rules; 


(i) “secretary” means a person who, subject to the control of the manag- 
ing committee is empowered with the management of the affairs of 
a co-operative society and includes a member of a managing 
committee or any other person discharging the duties of a secretary 
by whatever name called and whether under a contract of service 
with the society or not; 


(j) “section” means a section of the Act; 


(k) “working capital” means the total capital of a co-operative society 
consisting of borrowed capital and owned capital; and 


(1) words and expressions used in these rules but not defined and defined 
in the Act shall have the same meanings as are respectively 
assigned to them in the Act. 


(2) Unless otherwise specified m these rules and the bye-laws of a 
co-operative society— 


(a) words importing the masculine gender include the faminine gender; 
(b) words in the plural include the singular and vice versa; 
(c) the word “person” includes a body of persons corporate or otherwise; 


(d) expressions referring to writing include printing, typing, lithography, 
photography, and other methods of representing or reproducing 
words in a visible form; and 


(e) with reference to a person who is unable to write his name, the word 
“signature” shall include his thumb impression or other mark duly 
attested to signify his signature. 


(3) There shall be the following classes of co-operative societies, namely:— 


(i) “agricultural society” means a_ co-operative society of which the 
majority Of members are agriculturists; 


(ii) “agro-service co-operative” means a co-operative society formed of 
unemployed— 


(a) degree holders in any branch of enginecring, technology, science, 
commerce, arts or agriculture, 


(b) diploma-holders in any branch of enginecring or technology, 


(c) certificate-holders in any industrial trades, for their exclusive 
benefits, the percentage of degree or diploma holders in agricul- 
tural cngineering and in any branch of agriculture 11) the 
membership of the co-operative society being not 1995 than sixty 
per cent. 


(iii) “Consumers’ Society” means a co-operative society, the primar 
object of which is to supply consumers’ goods and to render suc 
other services to its members as may be required in respect of 
supply and production of consumers’ goods and includes wholesale 
consumers’ co-operative societies or a federation of such societies; 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, JANUARY 30, 94 188(3)‏ و2 


ee জপ তি আরা IEE a وکس سے سد ہے‎ ৭ শা Ra EE ES SS 


(iv) “Housing Society” means a society the object of which is— 


(a) providing its members with dwelling houses, flats or lands for 
construction of dwelling houses; or 


(b) maintenance of common services in completed houses, tenements or 
flats or in colonies; 


(v) “Marketing Society” means a primary society composed of primary 
credit societies, service co-operatives and _  agriculturists as its 
members; 


(vi) “Multipurpose Society” means a co-operative society which includes 
among its object two or more of the primary objects specified in 
clauses (iii), (vii), (x), (xi), (xii) and (111), or any other object for 
which a transport co-operative society is formed; 


(vii) “mutual benefit society” means a co-operative society, the primary 
object of which is to create funds by raising contributions from its 
members by accepting grants and donations or otherwise, and 00 
employ such funds for the benefit of its members or their nominees; 


(viii) “non-agricultural society” means a co-operative society of which the 
majority of members are not agriculturists; 


(ix) “processing society” means a co-operative society, the primary object 
of which is to process agricultural produce into a state which is fit 
for consumption; 


(x) “production and sale society” means a_ co-operative society, the 
primary object of which is the collective production and/or disposal 
of goods of its members or otherwise; 


(xi) “purchase and sale society” means a co-operative society, the primary 
Object of which is to purchase goods and distribute them amongst 
its members; 


(xti) “students co-operative” means a co-operative society formed mainly 
of students of educational institutions for their exclusive benefit; 


(xiii) “thrift and savings society” means a co-operative society, the primary 
object of which is to encourage and provide facilities for the 
exercise of thrift among its members; 


(xiv) “transport society” means a co-operative society formed of drivers, 
conductors, cleaners, mechanics or other workers employed in any 
transport undertaking and users of transport services: 


Provided that the percentage of drivers, conductors, cleaners, mechanics 
and other workers shall not be less than 70 per cent. of the total 
membership of the society. 


3. Determination of one-half, one-third, etc.—When any rule requires the 
determination of one-half, one-third or any other fraction of a number and 
that number is not evenly divisible by 2, 3 or such other figure as may be 
required, the number next below, which is evenly divisible by 2, 3 or such 
other figure, shall be taken for the original number. 


4. Forms.—The forms set forth in the schedule or forms as near thereto 
as circumstances admit shall be used in all matters to which these forms 
relate: 


Provided that the Registrar may at his discretion— 
(i) modify any of the forms set forth in the schedule; or 


(ii) suggest new forms in their places or for any other matter for which 
forms are required. 


5. Net profits.—The ‘net profits’ of a co-operative socicty shall be the 
profits remaining after allowing for the following charges in addition to those 
specified in clause (z) of section 2, namely— 


(a) all other usual working charges, such as, repairs, rent, taxes and the 
like, bounties or subsidies received; depreciation and irrecoverable 
book debts written off; 


(b) capital expenditure written off either wholly or in part;

(c) capital loss actually incurred and not adjusted against any fund created 
out of profits; and 


(d) provision for estimated bad debts, if any. 


6. Co-operative year.—The co-operative year shall mean 016 year 
cOmmencing on the Ist day of July. 


7. Functions of the State Co-operative Union.—Subject to such directions 
as the State Government may, from time to time, issue regarding utilisation 
of its funds or otherwise, the State Co-operative Union may carry out the 
following functions, namely— | 


(i) to promote and develop the co-operative movement in West Bengal, 
to educate, guide and assist the people in their efforts to build up 
and expand the co-operative sector and to serve as an exponent of 
co-operative principles and ideas; 


(ii) to organise co-operative training programmes and run training centres 
according to the schemes of the State Government or otherwise; 


(iii) to develop inter-co-operative relationship and help the co-ordinated 
functioning of the co-operative movement in various sectors; 


(iv) to organise, conduct, collaborate and assist in carrying out research 
and investigation on important co-operative problems; 


(v) to maintain an information bureau and a library; 


(vi) to express and organise opinion on matters of co-operative policy and 
act as the accredited representative of West Bengal’s Co-operative 
Movement in the national and international spheres; 


(vii) to convene, organise and hold co-operative seminars, meetings, confer- 
ences and exhibitions; to spread the message and_ ideals of 
co-operative movement in the State and to mould public opinion in 
respect thereof; 


(viii) to facilitate the promotion of co-operative societies and assist the 
affiliated societies in resolving their problems and difficulties; 


(ix) to select delegates, representatives or observers on behalf of the 
Union for participation in the international, national and State 
conference; 


(x) to organise, promote or undertake such other activities or functions 
as are considered beneficial or conducive towards the attainment of 
the objects of the aforesaid Union in accordance with the bye-laws 
thereof. 


CHAPTER II 
Registration 


8. Formation of Co-operative Socicty.—({1) No primary credit society shall 
be registered unless the applicants— 


(i) reside or hold landed property in the same town or village or in the 
same group of villages; or 


(ii) are members of the same class or occupation: 


Provided that the State Government may, if it is satisfied that it is 
necessary 50 to do to ensure at the very inception that the societies hold 
reasonable promise of future growth, self reliance, broad numerical and 
financial base and other elements of assured viability, by general or special 
order, direct that different classes of co-operative societies shall be registered 
with such contribution to share capital of such societies by the members 
thereof as may be specified in the order. 


(2) No Apex or Central Society shall be registered unless it has among its 
applicants at least— 
(a) six co-operative societies; or 
(b) six applicants composed of individual persons and _ co-operative 
societies: 


Provided that the number of individual persons shall not exceed one-third 
of the total number of applicants.

9. Application for registration—{1) An application for registration of a 
society shall be submitted to the Registrar in the form set forth in the schedule 
and shall be signed by the applicants. 


(2) Where a co-operative society is an applicant, the application shall be 
নী, by an officer of the society duly empowered to sign documents on 15 
ehalf. 


(3) With every application there shall be submitted two copies of the bye- 
laws which the socicty proposes to adopt duly signed by the applicants and a 
third copy, if the society intends to be a member of a financing bank. 


10. Registration of society and refusal to register—{1) On receipt of the 
application, the Registrar shall satisfy himself that the bye-laws are— 


(a) in conformity with the Act and the Rules, 
(b) suitable for carrying out the objects of the society, and 
(c) suitable for ensuring the safe conduct of the business of the society. 


(2) When a society is registered, the Registrar shall grant certificate of 
registration in the form set forth in the schedule. 


(3) On the registration of a society, two copies of its approved bye-laws 
shall be stamped with the official seal of the Registrar. One of the said copies 
shall be retained in the office of the Registrar and the second copy together 
with the certificate of registration shall be forwarded to the society. 


(4) If the society intends to be a member of a financing bank, a third copy 
shall be authenticated and sent to the financing bank. 


(5) In every case in which the Registrar refuses to register a society, he 
shall record in writing the reasons for his refusal and shall communicate his 
decision by registered post to the applicant whose name appears at serial No. 1 
in the application for registration. 


11. Restriction on membership.—No person qualified under the bye-laws 
to be a member of a co-operative society shall be excluded from membership 
without efficient cause: 


Provided that without the permission of the Registrar— 


(i) no person shall be entitled to membership of any society with 
unlimited liability who is, or has at any time during the two preced- 
ing years becn, a member of any -other society with unlimited 
liability; and 

(ii) no person shall be entitled to membership of any credit society even 
with limited liability if he is a member of any other such society 
until he has obtained in writing the consent 2) the society of which 
he is already a member. 


12. Making of bye-laws.—({1) Every co-operative society shall make bye- 
laws in respect of the following matters, namely:— 
(a) the name and registered address of the society; 


(b) the extent of the area—the inhabitants of which are eligible to apply 
for membership of the society; 


(৫) the object for which the society is established and the purpose to 
which its funds may be applied; 


(d) the qualifications required for membership and the terms of admission 
of members; 


(e) the rights and 11901110105 of membership; 
(6) the manner in which the capital may be raised; 


(g) the mode of appointment and removal of the directors and officers of 
the society, and the duties and powers of the Managing Committee; 


(h) the mode of summoning and conducting meetings, and the right of 
voting; 


(i) the general conduct of the business of the society; 
{j) the disposal of profits;

13. Withdrawal, removal or expulsion of member.-—(1) A member of any 
registered society may, if he is not in debt to the society or is not surety, 
withdraw from the society after giving onc month's notice in writing to the 
Secretary or any officer performing the duties of the Secretary. 


(2) A member may be removed or expelled from a registered society only 
for such causes, and in accordance with such procedure, as may be provided 
in the bye-laws. 


(3) A member who ceases to be qualified under the bye-laws may be 
removed by the managing committee. 


14. Amendment of bye-laws.—(1) After the bye-laws have been registered, 
a co-operative society may amend them by altering or rescinding any bye-law 
or by making a new bye-law. No such amendment shall be made save in 
accordance with a resolution passed at a gencral meeting: 


Provided that subject to sub-rule (2), no such’ resolution shall be valid 
unless it is passed by one-third of the total number of members subsisting as 
such on the date of issue of the notice of the general meeting and by two-thirds 
of the members present at such mecting.

(2) In special cases the Registrar may register an amendment which is

(i) that it is impossible for the society to secure the attendance of one- 
third of the total number of members at a general meeting, and 


(11) that the adoption of the proposed amendment is in the interests of 
the society. 


(3) In every case in which the bye-laws of a society are amended, an 
application in the form set forth in the schedule for the registration of the new 
or altered bye-law or for the rescission of an existing bye-law shall be sub- 
mitted to the Registrar, signed by the Secretary or any other officer performing 
duties of the Secretary and three directors. The application shall show— 


(a) the date of the general meeting at which the amendment was passed; 


(b) the number of members on the roll of the society on the date of giving

(c) the number of members present at the meeting; and 
(d) the number of members who voted in support of the amendment.

(5) When the Registrar registers an amendment of by-laws he shall retain

another copy to the society together with < certificate of registration in the 
form set forth in the schedule. If the 9০০19 is a member of a financing bank, 
the third copy duly authenticated by the Reyistrar shall be sent to such bank. 


(6) When the Registrar finds that there are prima facie grounds for refus- 
ing to register the proposed amendment under sub-section (2) of section 17, 
he shall, before making the order, afford the society an opportunity of making 
its representation by sending back the proposal papers to it under a memoran- 
dum stating clearly therein the grounds on which he proposes 00 refuse to 
register the amendment and advising it to show cause why the same should 
not be refused. The Registrar shall make the final order after hearing the 
society and duly considering its contentions. 


15. Amendment of bye-laws at the instance of the Registrar—(1) If it 
appears to the Registrar to be necessary or desirable in the interest of any co- 
operative society to amend the bye-laws of such society, the Registrar may, on 
his own motion or on the application of a financing bank of which the society 
is a member and a debtor, supported by a resolution of the managing committee 
of the financing bank indicating the amendment and the reasons justifying the 
Same, authorise any person, by special order in writing, to call a special general 
meeting of the society to make the amendment within one month or such 
longer period as may be specified by the Registrar. 


(2) Notwithstanding any rule or bye-law prescribing the period of notice 
for, and the mcthod of summoning, a general meeting, the Registrar, in the 
case of a meeting called under sub-rule (1), may specify the time and place for 
the meeting, the manner in which it shall be summoned and the matter which 
shall be discussed thereat. 


(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rules (1) and (2) of rule 14, 
the Registrar may registcr the amendment, if passed by two-thirds of the 
members present at the mecting. 


(4) On receipt of the approval of the general mecting regarding such 
amendment, the Registrar shall register the amendment. 


(5) When the Registrar registers the amendment of bye-laws, he shall 
retain one copy of the new bye-laws and send another copy to the society 
together with a certificate of registration in the appropriate form set forth in 
the schedule. If the society is a member of a financing bank, a third copy 
duly authenticated by the Registrar shall be sent to such bank.

CHAPTER III 
Management of Co-operative Socicties 


16. Notice of General Meeting.—(1) A general meeting shall be convened 
by the Secretary or any officer authorised by the managing committee, in 
accordance with the direction of the managing committee: 


Provided that where a Government officer has been 0 to the service 
of a co-operative society under section 24 he shall, where there is no Secretary, 
convene the general meetings in accordance with the provisions of the Act and 
the rules thereunder. 


(2) Unless otherwise provided in the bye-laws, a notice of the mecting 
stating the place, date and hour of the meeting together with a statement of 
business to be transacted at it shall be sent to every member fifteen clear days 
before the date of the meeting in the manner provided in the bye-laws. 


(3) Any accidental omission to give notice to any member or the non- 
receipt of the notice by any member shall not invalidate the proceedings of 
any meeting. 


17. General Meeting.—(1) A general mecting of cvery co-operative society, 
to be called the annual general meeting, shall be held within fifteen months 
from the date of its registration and thereafter as provided in section 2l. 


(2) (i) If the managing committee fails to take steps, or does not give 
direction, to convene the annual general meeting at least twenty-one days 
before the expiry of the period referred to in sub-rule (1), the Chairman, or 
in his absence the Vice-Chairman, shall convene the meeting. 


(ii) Where the general meeting is required to be held by convoking 
representatives, the election of delegates shall be completed before the 
aforesaid period of twenty-one days: 


Provided that in case of failure of the managing committee to take steps or 
to give direction, sufficiently in advance, towards holding of such election 
within the period SET | just above, the Chairman, and in his absence the 
Vice-Chairman, shall perform, within the said prescribed period, such duties 
on behalf of the managing committee. 


18. Special gencral meeting.—At a special general meeting, no business 
other than that specified in the notice issued under sub-rule (2) of rule 16, 
Shall be discussed. 


19. Requisition of special general meeting —A requisition for a special 
general meeting to be convened under clauSe (a) of sub-section (1) of section 22 
shall state the object of the meeting, shall be signed by the members requisi- 
tioning it and shall be sent to the registered office of the society. 


20. Powers of general meeting.—(1) The general meeting of a co-operative 
society shall examine, subject to the provisions of section 21, the annual report 
regarding working of the society and in particular, the work of the managing 
committee and shall be competent to take all steps that may be necessary in 
the interest of the society. 


(2) Every resolution at a meeting shall be decided by a majority of votes 
of members, and if the votes be equal, the Chairman shall have a second or 
casting vote. 


21. Chairman of gencral meeting.—(1) The Chairman, or in his absence 
the Vice-Chairman, of a society shall preside over the general meeting of a 
society. In the absence of the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman, one of the 
directors in the panel mentioned in sub-rule (6) of rule 28 in order of their 
names in the panel, shall be the Chairman of the meeting. 


The said Chairman shall presjde over the meeting till the item for electing 
members of the managing committee is taken up; and thereafter, if the said 
Chairman is a candidate for election, the Presiding Officer elected or the 
Election Officer appointed in terms of rule 29, as the case may be, shall conduct 
the election, and at the conclusicn of the meeting both the Presiding Officer or 
Election Officer, as the case may be and the Chairman mentioned above shall 
sign the proceedings of the meeting.

(2) The Chairman of the general meeting shall maintain order in the meet- 
ing and shall control and conduct the proceedings in such manner as may be 
conducive to expeditious and satisfactory disposal of business. He shall 
decide all points gf order and his decision upon such points shall be final. 


(3) The Chairman of the general meeting may direct any member to 
withdraw for disorderly conduct, and the member so ordered shall immediately 
withdraw and unless otherwise directed by the Chairman shall remain absent 
during the remaining period of the meeting on that date and shall not be 
entitled to vote without the permission of the Chairman. 


(4) In the event of disorder, the Chairman of the meeting may suspend the 
meeting and adjourn it. 


(5) In case where the business of the general meeting cannot be completed 


in the course of one sitting, the same may be adjourned by the Chairman of 
the meeting. 


22. Quorum of gencral meeting.—{]) The quorum for a general meeting 
shall be one-fifth of the total number of members subsisting as such 25 on the 
date of notice of the meeting. After the issue of such notice, no new member 
shall be admitted till the general mecting is over. 


(2) No business shall be transacted at any meeting unless there is a quorum 
at the time when the business of the meeting is due to commence. 


(3) If within half-an-hour from the time appointed for the meeting a quorum 
is not present, the meeting shall stand adjourned: 
Provided that— 


(i) no quorum shall be necessary at a meeting adjourned in accordance 
with this sub-rule, and 


(ii) a meeting, which has been called on requisition under clause (a) of 
sub-section (1) of section 22, shall not be adjourned but dissolved. 


(4) If at any time during tha meeting sufficient number of members are not 
present to form a quorum, the Chairman of the meeting, on his attention being 
drawn to this fact, shall, adjourn the meeting, and the business that remaing 
to be transacted at this meeting, if any, shall be disposed of in the usual manner 
at the adjourned meeting. 


(5) Where a general meeting is adjourned under sub-rule (4) or sub-rule (5) 
of rule 21 or under sub-rule (3) or sub-rule (4) of this rule, the adjourned 
meeting shall be held ordinarily at the same place, on the same day of the 
next week and at the same time, and the fact of adjournment shall be notified 
at the office of the society and at its branches, if any, and on the notice board 
of the local panchayat office, if there be any. 


23. (1) Minutes of general meeting.—Every co-operative society shall cause 
minutes of proceedings of general meetings to be entered in a book kept for 
that purpose. 


(2) Unless the minutes are drawn up and are duly signed by the Chairman 
immediately on the termination of the meeting, the minutes free from all 
alterations or corrections, shall be drawn up and shall be signed by the Chairman 
of the meeting within seventy-two hours from the time when the meetings 
terminated. The minutes so signed shall be evidence of the proceedings of 
that meeting. 


(3) Until the contrary is proved, every general meeting of a society, in 
respect of the proceedings whereof minutes have been so recorded, shall be 
deemed to have been duly called and held. 


24. Voting of general meceting.—({1) A resolution which is put to the vote 
of a general meeting shall be decided on a_ show of hands unless (whether 
before or after the declaration of the result of the show of hands), a poll 15 
demanded by at lcast ten members, and if no poll is demanded, a declaration 
by the Chairman of such meeting that a resolution has been carried or lost 
and an entry to that effect in the minutes of the proceedings shall, for the 
purposes of the Act, be conclusive proof of the fact that such resolution has 
been duly carried or lost but it shall not be proof of the number or proportion 
of the votes recorded in favour of or against such resolution.

26. Division of area of a society for election of delegates.—(1) The manag-

purpose of election of delegates. 


(2) The division of the area of operation of a society under sub-rule (1) shall

(a) the manner of nomination and election of delegates,

accordance with sub-rule (2) of rule 25.

(b) appointment by such bodies as may be specified in this behalf in the 
bye-laws of the society; and 


(c) nomination by State Government when it decides to make such nomina- 
tions in terms of section 28.

mittee of a co-operative society under sub-section (1) of section 28 shell hold 
office until a fresh nomination is made in his place, and the State Government 
may similarly nominate a new member to fill up any casual vacancy among the 
nominated members.

not more than eighteen elected directors as may be fixed in the bye-laws:

as the case may be, is established beyond reasonable doubt. 


(ii) The committee shall give all reasonable facilities to the contesting 
candidates or their representives to examine all the nomination papers for 
Satisfying themselves about the correctness of their scrutiny. 


(iii) The Managing Committee shall endorse on each nomination paper its 
decision accepting or rejecting the same, and if the nomination paper is reject- 
ed, shall record in writing a brief statement of its reasons for such rejection. 


(7) The list of valid nominations, as decided by the Managing Committee, 
shall be published on the notice board of the society on the same day on which

(12) The ballot paper shall contain the names of the candidates, their 
symbols other than accredited symbols approved by the Election Commissioner 
of India, if so desired by the candidate and the seal of the society. 


(13) No ballot paper shall be issued to a voter unless the Polling Officer is 
Satisfied that the person concerned is the same as noted in the list of members 
or of delegates furnished to him. 


(14) If owing to blindness or other physical infirmity, or illiteracy, a voter 
is unable to mark the ballot paper, the Polling Officer shall ascertain from ‘him 
the candidate or candidates in whose favour he desires to vote and shall

(15) The counting of votes shall commence immediatcly after the polling 
is declared over by the Presiding Officer and no member shall be allowed to cast 
his vote after such declaration. Votes shall be counted by or under the direct 
supervision of the Presiding Officer. Each candidate and his authorised agent 
Shall have a right to be present at the time of counting. 


(16) (i) A ballot paper shall be rejected— 


(a) if it bears any mark by which the member, who voted, can be 
identified; or 


(b) if it does not bear the seal of the society; or 


(c) if the mark indicating the vote there is placed in such manner as to 
make it doubtful to which particular candidate the vote has been 
cast. 


(ii) The Presiding Officer shall be the authority competent to reject a ballot 
paper. 


(17)(i) Soon after the counting of votes is over, the Presiding Officer shall 
prepare and certify a return setting forth— 


(a) total number of ballot paper issued; 
(b) the number of valid votes given to each candidate; and 
(c) the number of ballot papers declared to be invalid or rejected. 


(11) On the basis of the return, the candidates who have secured the largest 
number of valid votes shall be declared elected at the general meeting and 
their names shall be immediately published on the notice board of the society 
under the signature of the Presiding Officer; and in case of cquality of votes 
ت۵‎ by two or more candidates, lots shall be drawn in such manner as the 

residing Officer may fix, to determine the names of the successful candidate 
or candidates. 


(18) The Chairman of the society shall immediately take custody of the 
ballot papers and shall preserve them for three months from the date of the 
poll. The ballot papers and other records relating to the election shall 
immediately, in presence of the candidates or their representatives as may be 
available be secured in a container which shall be affixed with the seal of the 
society and of a candidate who desire to affix their seals, if any. They shall 
be destroyed with the approval of the Registrar after the said period of three 
months, if no dispute relating to, or in connection with, that election is referred 
to, the Registrar.
