(19) The results of the election shall be immediately recorded in the minute 
book of the society and attested by the Presiding Officer. 


(20) The Registrar may, in respect of any primary co-operative society 
coming within the purview of the rule, either on an application from the 
Managing Committee of such society or from one-third of the total number 
of its members of fifty, whichever is, less, or on his own motion after an enquiry 
into the affairs of the society under section 84 or an inspection under section 
82, by an order in writing recording reasons thereon, appoint any person as 
an Election Officer to conduct the election, if, in the opinion of the Registrar, 
such a course is necessary for the proper conduct of the election. 


(21) In any co-operative society mentioned in sub-rule (20), the Registrar 
may, by an order in writing, appoint any person as an_ election officer to 
conduct the election. 


(22) Where an election officer is so appointed either under sub-rule (20) or 
sub-rule (21) all reference to Chairman, Presiding Officer or the Managing 
Committee, as the case may be, occurring in clause (111) of sub-rule 5, clause 
(ii) of sub-rule (11) and sub-rules (6), (7), (8), (9), (10), (11), (15), (17), (18) and 
(19) shall be construed as reference to the election officer. 


(23(i) The election of Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, Treasurer and 
other necessary office-bearers of the committee shall be conducted by the 
Presiding Officer or by the Election Officer, as the case may be, at a meeting to 
be called by him within the period prescribed under sub-rule (5) of rule 28 and 
in the manner, as may be laid down in the bye-laws of a society or as may be 
decided by the Presiding Officer or the Election Officer: 


Provided that the Presiding Officer or the Election Officer, as the case may 
be, shall before calling the meeting, ascertain from the appropriate authority 
whether such authority proposes to nominate any member on the Managing 
Committee of the society, and if the Presiding Officer or the Election Officer 
does not receive any reply to his aforesaid enquiry, within fifteen days from the 
দা of such enquiry, he shall proceed with the election as provided in the 
rules: 


Provided further that not less than seven clear days’ notice in writing shall 
be given by registered post with acknowledgment due to the members of the 
newly-constituted Managing Committee for such a meeting, 


(ii) As soon as the election is over, the result shall be immediately declared 
in the meeting, published in the notice board of the society and recorded in the 
minutes book of the Managing Committee under the attestation of the 
Presiding Officer. 


(24) Primary societies with working capital or annual transactions of less 
than rupees five lakhs may not follow the provisions contained in this 1016; 
and in respect of matters mentioned therein, such societies shall be guided by 
the provisions contained in the bye-laws or where there is no such provision 
in the bye-laws, by the written directions of the Regional Assistant Registrar. 


Explanation.—In this sub-rule “Regional Assistant Registrar” means, in 
relation to a primary society, a person appointed under section 9 of the Act to 
assist the Registrar and having jurisdiction over the area of operation of that 
society. 


30. First managing committee.—{1) Except where the first directors and 
the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman are named in the bye-laws or in the 
application for registration of a society, the first directors including the Chair- 
man and the Vice-Chairman shall be- appointed by the Registrar. 


(2) The directors so appointed shall hold office till directors are elected by 
members at a general meeting: 


Provided that any director appointed under sub-rule (1) may be removed 
by the Registrar before the expiry of his term of office, if the Registrar is, for 
reasons to be recorded by him in writing, of the opinion that the continuance 
in Office of such director is not desirable in the interests of the society. 


(3) Directors appointed under this rule may or may not be members of the 
society. 


(4) If a vacancy occurs in the office of an appointed director, the vacancy 
Shall be filled up by appointment.

(5) Where the first directors including the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman 
are named in the bye-laws, or in the application for registration of a society, 
a caSual vacancy occurring in the office of such director shall be filled up by 
co-option by the remaining directors. 


31. Election and retirement of directors in a primary society other than 
a non-agricultural credit society—(1) The directors of a primary society other 
than a non-agricultural credit society shall retire annually from office and shall 
be eligible for re-election. | 


(2) The vacancies caused by the retirement of the directors shall be filled 
up by election at the general meeting at which they retire. 


(3) If at any mecting at which an election of directors ought to take place, 
the places of the vacating directors are not filled up, such election shall take 
place within three months from the date of such meeting and the vacating 
directors shall be deemed not to have vacated their offices till the directors 
required to be elected in their places have been duly elected. 


32. Election and retirement of dirctors in an Apex, Central or Primary 
non-agricultural Credit Socicty.—{1) At every annual general meeting of an 
Apex Society, a Central Society or a primary non-agricultural credit society, 
one-third of the directors elected by the members shall retire from office and 
shall, subject to the provisions of section 23, be eligible for re-election. 


(2) The vacancies caused by the retirement of directors under sub-rule (1) 
shall be filled up by election at the general meeting at which they retire. 


(3) If at any meeting at which an election of directors ought to take place, 
the places of the vacating directors are not filled up, such election shall take 
place within three months from the date of such meeting and the vacating 
directors shall be deemed not to have vacated their offices till the directors 
required to be elected in their places have been duly elected. 


33. Qualifications of members of Managing Committee.—Subject to the 
provisions of these rules, every member of a co-operative society above the age 
of 21 years shall be qualified to be elected or appointed as director: 


Provided that in the case of a Students’ Co-operative, a member below the 
age of 2] years may also be elected or appointed as a director. 


34. Nomination by a co-operative society of one of its members as [থে 
representative to another co-operative society.—The Managing Committee of 
a cO-operative society may, in a meeting with specific agenda, nominate 
a member of such society as its representative to another co-operative society 
to which the first named society is affliated and may also recall such represen- 
tative if a resolution is passed by the committee in that behalf at a meeting for 
which such an agenda item was given: 


Provided that at the same meeting, where a resolution of such recall is made, 
there shall be a fresh nomination of another representative of such society, 
that no new representative shall be nominated under this rule until the repre- 
sentative previously nominated has been recalled, that no one shall be nomi- 
nated as representative of a society if he is individually a member of the other 
society, and that in case of such recall and fresh nomination by an 0 
Society in a single-member constituency, the freshly nominated representative 
Shall automatically be a director of the other society. 


35. Cessation of membership of managing committee.—A _ director shall 
cease to hold office— 


(a) if he resigns his office, or 
(b) if he is removed by the general meeting held in accordance with rule 38, 


(c) where he has been chosen as, and is, a director of a society by virtue 
of his qualification of being— 


(i) a member of that society, or 


(ii) a member of any other society which is a member either of the 
society hereinbefore in this rule first referred to or of another 
society which, in its term, is a member of the society herein- 
before in this rule first referred to,

36. Removal, expulsion, etc. of the Chairman, directors and other officers.— 
The Chairman of a society or any other officer elected under sub-rule (5) of 
rule 28 may be removed from his office by a resolution of a general meeting 
specially convened for the purpose. 


37. Notice of meeting.—Notice ot a meeting of the Managing Committee 
in respect of any society or class of societies shall be given in writing, subject 
to the provision of section 27(1), by the Secretary, or any officer performing the 
duties of Secretary, to every director specifying the place, date and hour of 
the meeting together with a statement of the business to be transacted thereat, 
not less than seven days before the date of the meeting. In case of urgency, 
the Chairman may convene a meeting of the Managing Committee with clear 
three days’ notice: 


Provided that any urgent business, not included in the statement accom- 
panying the notice, may be brought up and considered with the consent of 
two-thirds of the directors present at the meeting. 


38. Meeting of Managing Committee.—The Managing Committee | shall 
meet for the transaction of the business of the society at least once in every 
two months. 


39. Voting at the meeting of Managing Committee.—Every resolution at 
a meeting of the Managing Committee shall be decided by a majority of votes, 
and if the votes be equal, the Chairman shall have a second or casting vote. 


40. Chairman of meeting.—The Chairman of a society shall preside over 
all meetings of the Managing Committee at which he is present. In the absence 
of the Chairman, the Vice-Chairman shall take the chair and in absence of 
the Vice-Chairman, one of the directors in the panel mentioned ا‎ sub-rule 
(6) of rule 28, in order of their names in the panel, shall be the Chairman of 
the meeting. 


41. Quorum of meeting.—({1) Unless a larger proportion is provided in the 
bye-laws, the quorum at a meeting of the Managing Committee shall be 
one-third of the total number of directors. 


(2) No business shall be transacted at any meeting including an adjourned 
meeting of the Managing Committee unless there is a quorum at the time when 
the business of the meeting is scheduled to commence or within half-an-hour 
from the time appointed for the meeting, and a fresh notice in terms of rule 
38 shall then be issued for holding the next meeting. 


42. Requisition meeting.—{1) One-third of the directors may requisition 
a special meeting of the Managing Committee by giving seven clear days’ notice. 


(2) The requisition shall specify the object of the meeting and_ shall be 
signed by the requisitionists and shall be delivered at the office of the society. 


(3) If the Secretary or anybody performing the duties of the Secretary does 
not convene the meeting within seven days from the date of receipt of the 
requisition, a notice signed by the requisitionists specifying the object and 
appointing the date and time of the meeting, shall be sent to all the directors. 
No separate notice as per rule 38 shall be necessary for such meetings to be 
held at the office of the society. 


(4) At such special meeting, no business other than that specified in the 
requisition shall be transacted, and if there is no quorum within half-an-hour 
from the time appointed, the meeting shall not be adjourned but dissolved.

43. Powers of the Managing Committee.—The Managing Committee of a 
co-operative society shall exercise all or any of the following powers as may 


be provided in the bye-laws— 


(a) to admit new members; 


(b) to fine, suspend, remove or expel existing members by the votes of 
two-thirds of the members of the Managing Committee present and 
voting at a meeting: 


Provided that no such action shall be taken by the Managing Committee 
without giving the member concerned an opportunity of explaining 
his conduct for which he is to be fined, suspended, removed or 
expelled; 


(c) to raise funds; 
(d) to invest funds; 


(e) to empower any employee, other than those mentioned in clause (21) 
of section 2, to give direction in regard to the business of the 
society; 


(f) to appoint or to dismiss or to remove salaried or non-salaried officers 
and other employees of teh society, to define the duties and respon- 
sibilities of the officers and to determine the securities to ০৫ 
furnished by the officers and other employees: 


Provided that no _ officer or employee of a co-operative society can be 
dismissed or removed from service of such society except after an 
enquiry in which he has been informed of the charges against him 
and given 2 reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of those 
charges, and where it is proposed, after such enquiry to dismiss 
or remove him, until he has been given a reasonable opportunity 
of making representations on the penalty proposed: 


Provided further that in case of urgency, the Chief Executive Officer of 
the society, by whatever designation he may be called, who 15 
empowered to settle the duties of other employees, may also 
reallocate the duties and responsibilities of the officers of the society 
temporarily, as the circumstances demand, in between the two 
meetings of the Managing Committee, but if such reallocation 15 
required to be continued for a period of more than seven days, the 
Chief Executive Officer shall obtain the approval of the Chairman 
in respect thereof, -and the fact of such reallocation shall also be 
brought to the notice of the Managing Committee at its meeting 
immediately following the date of such reallocation; 


(g) to compound or abandon or delay to enforce any debt or demand of 
the society or to institute, defend or compromise legal proceedings; 


(h) to dispose of applications for shares and to issue shares against rebate 
as declared by the Managing Committee, subject to directions given 
by the general meeting from time to time; 


(i) to dispose of applications for loans and to determine the security to be 
taken; and 


() to appoint sub-committees as may be deemed necessary from time to 
time and to confer such powers and impose such duties upon such 
sub-committees as may be deemed proper: 


Provided that the Managing Committee of an apex society may, for 
administrative convenience, appoint any committee, consisting of 
as many members of the Managing Committee as may be considered 
necessary, and confer all or any of its powers mentioned in rule 43 
and impose all or any, of the duties mentioned in rule 44 upon such 
commitgee, Subject to any requisitions made or restrictions imposed 
by the Managing Committee. 


44. Duties of the Managing Committee.—The Managing Committee shall 
observe, in all their transactions, the provisions of the Act, rules and نا‎ 9 
and shall cause to perform the following duties, namely,— 


(a) to receive and disburse money; 


(b) to maintain true accounts of money received and expended, and 
accounts of the assets and liabilities;

(11) an annual stutement of accounts which shall include—

(m) to examine and take prompt action in cases of all arrears and defaults 
in repayment of loans and advances; and 


(n) to perform such other duties as may be entrusted by the general 
meeting. 


45. Powers and duties of the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman of society. 
—Unless otherwise provided in the Act, the rules, or the bye-laws, the Chair- 
man, or the Vice-Chairman in the absence of the Chairman shall, for the 
transaction of the business of the society exercise general control and power 
of supervision over the affairs and officers of the society, and in cases of urgency, 
exercise all powers and perform all duties required to be exercised and peform- 
ed under the Act, the rules or the bye-laws by the Managing Committee except 
the power of sanctioning loans and ex-gratia payments to employees: 


Provided that the Chairman or the Vice-Chairman shall not act in opposi- 
tion to, or in contravention of, any order given or decision taken by the 
Managing Committee at a meeting. 


46. Orders of Chairman and Vice-Chairman to be placed before meeting.— 
All orders passed and all acts done by the Chairman or the Vice-Chairman in 
the absence of the Chairman in exercise of his powers and performance of his 
duties under rule 45 shall be placed for confirmation before the Managing 
Committee in the meeting immediately following. 


47. Government officer on deputation to be called Executive Officer.— 
(1) A Government officer, when, deputed to the service of a co-operative society 
under section 24, shall be called the Executive Officer of the society. 


(2) Subject to any condition to the contrary that the State Government may 
in any particular case think fit to impose, the Executive Officer shall be under 
the pene control of the Managing Committee of the society and shall, in the 
conduct of the business of the society, exercise the following powers, namely— 


(i) have control over the staff of the society with power to impose any 
punishment upon or to suspend, any member thereof in terms of 
clause (h) of sub-rule (2) of rule 51 and clause (i) of sub-rule (2) 
of rule 51 respectively; 


(ii) institute, defend and conduct legal proceedings in Law Courts and 
other places and enter into compromise or arbitration with creditors 
and debtors of the society.

48. Duties of the Executive Officer.—{1) The Executive Officer shall 
perform the following duties, namely:— 


(i)(a) receive all moneys on behalf of the society and issue receipts, other 
than receipts likely to create fresh obligations on the part of the 
society, in effectual discharge of the moneys stated to have been 
received therein, 


(b) operate, with such other officers of the society in case the Managing 
Committee so desires, accounts of the society lying with banks, and 


(c) draw, accept, make, endorse or negotiate all bills of exchange, pronotes, 
debentures, securities and other documents standing in the name 
of, or held by, the society; 


(ii) pay all costs of management and working expenses out of the funds 
of the society, e.g., salaries of the staff, travelling and other contin- 
gent expenses to be incurred in the working of the society; 


(iii) deposit all moneys received on behalf of the society and securities and 
other effects as prescribed under rule 97; 


(iv) maintain proper and accurate records and accounts of the working of 
the society; 


(v) be responsible for proper custody of stock and maintenance of stock 
accounts; 


(vi) call general meetings and meetings of the Managing Committee of the 
society, where there is no Secretary: 


Provided that where such meetings are not convened by the Secretary 
according to the provisions of the Act and the rules, the Executive 
Officer shall call the meetings as may be necessary for the proper 
conduct of the business of the society and shall always remain 
present at such meetings and take part in the deliberations thereof, 
ake signed, along with the Chairman, the minutes of such meetings; 
an 


(vii) place, from time to time, before the Chairman or such other autho- 
rity as the Managing Committee may direct, statement of reports 
and disbursements for examination and approval. 


(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in rule 43, rule 47 or sub-rule (1) 
of rule 48, where by reason of an order of a Court or for any other reason the 
Managing Committee of a co-operative society 15 unable to exercise the powers 
conferred by these rules, or its bye-laws, the Executive Officer shall, during 
the period of such inability, exercise such powers of the Managing Committee. 


49. Procedure in case of difference of opinion.—In the event of any differ- 
ence of opinion between the Executive Officer and the Managing Committee 
of the society with regard to any matter concerning the business of the society, 
the Executive Officer may refer the matter to the Registrar for his decision, 
and the decision of the Registrar shall be final. 


50. Indemnification of Executive Officer.—{1) The Executive Officer shall 
be indemnified out of the funds of the co-operative society for all costs, charges, 
travelling and other expenses incurred by him in the conduct of the society's 
business or in the discharge of his duties. 


(2) The society shall make such contribution towards the cost of the deputa- 
tion of the officer as the State Government may direct.

CHAPTER IV 


Duties and obligations of Co-operative Socicties 


52. Registration of address of Co-operative Society—(1) Every co-opera- 
tive society shall state in the bye-laws its address mentioning the place of 
business, post office, police-station and the district. 


(2) A change of address of a society may be made by a resolution of the 
Managing Committee and such change shall be reported to the financing bank, 
if any, and to the Registrar for record in the form set forth in the schedule.

central society to which such society is affiliated.

which candidates with required suitable qualifications, after selection, may be

55. Books of account.—Every co-operative society shall keep a regular 
account of— : 


(a) all sums of money received and expended by the society and of the 
matters in respect of which the receipt or expenditure takes place; 


(b) all sales and purchases of goods by the society; 
(c) the assets and liabilities of the society; 


and shall maintain corrected up-to-date such account works and subsidiary 
ledgers and in such form as the Registrar may direct. 


56. Books and Register.—Every co-operative society shall maintain such 
books and registers as may be necessary for proper conduct of its business and 
shall, in particular, maintain corrected up-to-date— 


(i) minute books recording the proceedings of the general meetings and . 
the meetings of the Managing Committee; 


(ii) register of members and their nominees in the form set forth in the 
schedule; 


(111) register of affiliated societies, if any, in the form set forth in the 
schedule;

(v) share ledger; 

(vi) loan ledger; 

(vii) ledger of deposits and other borrowings, if any; 


(viii) cash book, showing daily receipts and expenditure and the balance at 
the end of each day; 


(ix) receipt book containing forms in duplicate, (one form to be issued for 
money received and the other to be retained by the society); 


(x) voucher file (numbered serially) containing all vouchers for contingent 
and other expenditure incurred by the society; 


(xi) in the case of societies issuing loans—loan ledger, showing the number 
and date of disbursement of each loan issued to members, the 
amount of loan, the purpose for which it is granted and the date or 
dates of repayment, distinguishing principal and interest; 


(xii) in the case of a society with unlimited liability—register containing 
property and debt statements of members showing the assets and 
liabilities of each individual member on the date of his admission 
with full details of property including the survey number of the 
plots (the statement to be revised as often as necessary and in any 
case, at least once in three years); 


(xiii) in case of a society with working capital exceeding one lakh of 
rupees, general ledger showing receipts, disbursements and the 
outstandings under various heads from day to day; 


(xiv) registers showing sales and purchases of goods by the society, where 
applicable:

60. Persons whe will maintain accounts, books, ete.—The Managing Com- 
mittee shall specify which of the officers and employees of a society shall— 


(a) keep books of accounts; 
(b) keep other books and register; and 
(c) prepare returns and statements: 


Provided that a person charged with the keeping of accounts shall not be 
in charge of cash. 


61. Custody of accounts, books and records.—{1) The books and records 
of a socicty shall be kept in the custody of the Secretary or any other person 
exercising the powers or performing the duties of the Secretary. 


(2) No member or employee of a society shall, by any act or omission, 
prevent the Secretary or any other person exercising the powers or performing 


the duties of the Secretary from having custody of the books and records of 
the society. 


(3) ay member or employee of a society who commits 3 breach of 
sub-rule (2) shall, on conviction by a court, be punishable with fine which may 
extend to fifty rupees and, where the breach is a continuing one, with further 
fine which may extend to ten rupees for every day after the first during which 
the breach continues subsequent to such conviction. 


62. Preservation and destruction of books, records, etc.—The books and 
records of a society shall be preserved for such period as is set forth in the 
schedule or as may from time to time be directed by the Registrar. 


63. Preparation of statements, etc., at the expense of society and recoyery 
of such cost.—(1) If a co-operative society fails to send to the Registrar within 
the time allowed any statement or return required by the Act or the rules, the 
Registrar may cause such statement or return to be prepared by employing 


such staff as he may deem to be necessary and may assess upon the society the 
cost of such staff. 


(2) The cost assessed under sub-rule (1) shall be recoverable from the 
society by the Collector as a public demand upon requisition by the Registrar, 


and the society may recover such cost from the person or persons responsible 
for the neglect. 


64, Documents to be kept open to inspection.—In addition to ۶ 
documents mentioned in sub-section (4) of section 29, every co-operative 
society shall keep open to inspection a copy of the latest audited balance sheet 
and the register of members and directors. 


65. Publication of balance sheet.—(1) Every co-operative society shall 
publish its balance sheet within one month from the date on which it is 
adopted by the general meeting by displaying it in any conspicuous place in 
the registered office of the society and in every branch office where the business 
of the society is carried on. 


(2) The Managing Committee of a society shall in every co-operative year 
lay before a general meeting of the society a balance sheet made up to the 
date not more than one month prior to the date of meeting. 


66. Borrowings.—({1) The maximum amount which a society may borrow 
shall be determined annually at a general meeting of the society, and no 


society shall borrow beyond the maximum amount so determined and in force 
for the time being: 


Provided that the Registrar may at any tme revise the limit fixed by the 
general meeting.

67. Restriction on borrowings of primary agricultural credit society.—A 
primary agricultural credit society which is a member of a central bank shall 
not borrow by way of loans or deposits from any non-member without the 
sanction of the central bank, and where the society is not a member of any 
central bank, without the sanction of the Registrar. 


68. Restriction on borrowings of limited liability society—No society 
with limited liability shall, by accepting deposits or loans or in any other way, 
incur liabilities exceeding ten times the sum of the paid up share capital and 
i reserve fund for the time being separately invested outside the business of 
the society: 


Provided that— 


(a) the Central Co-operative Land Development Bank, or the State 
Co-operative Bank or a Central Co-operative Bank for the purpose 
of financing Land Development Ranke or a Land Development 
Bank for the purpose of financing its members, may incur liabilities 
by floating debentures, accepting deposits or in any other way to 
the extent of twenty times the value of paid up share capital and 
the reserve fund for the time being separately invested; 


(b) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
may impose, on agricultural society or a financing bank may incur 
liabilities for the purpose of advancing loans to members for 
production of crops and for financing the disposal of produce, 
repayable within a period of twelve months, irrespective of the 
amount of its paid-up share capital or reserve fund separately 
invested outside the business; 


(c) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
may impose, the Central Co-operative Land Development Bank or 
the State Co-operative Bank or a Central Co-operative Bank, or a 
Central or a Primary Society may incur liabilities, irrespective of 
the amount of its paid-up share capital and reserve fund separately 
invested outside the business, for the purpose of carrying on by 
itself or for the purposes of providing loans for carrying on by its 
members, the production, marketing and processing of any 
agricultural or industrial commodity; 


(d) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
may impose, a co-operative society may incur liabilities by way of 
loan or deposits from another co-operative society, repayable 
within a period of twelve months irrespective of the amount of its 
paid-up share capital and reserve fund separately invested, if such 
liabilities are incurred on pledge or hypothecation of marketable 
security or goods or both, and the amount of such liabilities does 
not exceed 80 per cent. of the market value of such security or 
goods or both, offered for pledge or hypothecation; 


(e) only in such districts or part thereof, where Small Farmers Develop- 
ment Agency and Marginal Farmers and Agricultural Labourers 
Development Agency have been setting up and with the permission 
of the Registrar and under such conditions as he may impose, a 
co-operative society may, for the purpose of financing its agricul- 
turist-members, incur liabilities to the extent of 20 times the sum 
of the paid-up share capital and the reserve fund, for the time being 
separately invested outside the business of the society; 


(f) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
may impose, a co-operative society composed solely of displaced 
persons and recommended by the Refugee Rehabilitation Com- 
missioner, West Bengal, may incur liabilities irrespective of its 
paid-up share capital and reserve fund separatcly invested.

Co-operative Banks coming within the purview. of the Banking Regulation Act,

1949 (Act 10 of 1949), if so required by the Registrar, shall keep a minimum 
liquid cover against deposits held by it according to the following scale:— 


(i) 40 per cent. of deposits at call or on current account and cash 
credits and overdrafts sanctioned but not drawn; 


Ezplanation.—Deposits matured but not drawn may be treated as deposits

(ii) 25 per cent. of savings deposits; 
(111) 25 per cent. of fixed deposits maturing within the next three months;

Provided that when the reserve fund of a society is invested in a Co-opera-

Provided further that the co-operative banks coming within the purview of 
the Banking Regulations Act, 1949 (Act 10 of 1949), shall maintain fluid 
resources or liquid cover according to the provisions of the said Act. 


Explanation.—{1) “Liquid cover” means any assets which can be converted 
into ready cash at once and which are maintained in one or more of the 
following forms:— 


(i) cash in hand, or in banks or with bankers approved by the Registrar; 
(ii) post office savings bank account; 


(iii) Government securities including Post Office Cash Certificate or 
National Savings Certificates; and 


(iv) other investments of liquid nature in outside concerns approved by 
the Registrar; 


Explanation._{2) The extent to which the assets in the above forms may 
be utilised for the purpose of calculation of fluid resources shall be as follows: 


(i) 90 per cent. of the market value of Government securities including 
Postal Cash Certificates or National Savings Certificates; 


(ii) 100 per cent. of cash on hand, balance with banks and post office 
savings bank; 


(iii) 80 per cent. of the market value of the debentures of land develop- 
ment banks and also of other trustee securities such as municipal 
loans; and 


(iv) 80 per cent. of the fixed deposits with other banks approved by the 
Registrar. 


(2) Under special circumstances the Managing Committee may with the 
approval of the Registrar decrease the proportions of the liquid cover as 
mentioned in sub-rule (1). 


70. Conditions for the guarantee of debentures by Government.—The 
issue of a debentures under section 33 shall be subject to the following 
conditions, namely:— 


(a) that such debentures are secured by mortgages held by the society 
and assigned to the trustee; and 


(b) that the total amount payable in respect of the debentures does not 
exceed two-thirds of the total value of the mortgages held by the 
society and assigned to the trustee.

(a) facilitating the production of commodities or disposal thereof by the

fourths of the total estimated net income from such lands during

76. Restriction on issue of loan.—In any co-operative society, in which 
the liability of the members is limited by shares, no loan shall be granted to a 
member exceeding ten times: the amount of share capital paid up by him: 

Provided that— 


(a) the Central Co-operative Land Development Bank, the State Co-opera-

Co-operative Land Development Bank up to twenty times the 
amount of share capital paid up by the land development bank; , 


(b) a land development bank may grant loans to its members up to twenty 
times the amount of share capital paid up by a member; 


(c) the State Co-operative Bank may advance loans to a society engaged in 
the purchase and production and disposal of goods of its members 
in excess of ten times the share capital paid up by such society; 


(d) with permission of the Registrar under such conditions as he ma 
impose, the State Co-operative Bank or any other financing ban 
may grant loans to its member-societies up to twenty times the 
amount of share capital paid up by the member-socicties;

he may impose, an agricultural society may grant loans to its 
members, repayable within a period of twelve months, for facilitat- 
ing production or disposal of crop, irrespective of the amount or 
the share capital paid up by such member; 


(f) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he 
"May impose, the State Co-operative Bank or any other financial 
co-operative bank may grant loans to its members against pledge 
or hypothecation of marketable security or goods or both up to a 
maximum limit of 80 per centum of the market value of such 
security or goods or both or against the guarantee of employer of 
the members of the society concerned, irrespective of the amount 

of share capital paid up by such members; 


(g) with the permission of the Registrar and under such conditions as he

pective of the amount of share capital paid up by such members; 


(h) only in such districts or part thereof where small farmers’ development 
agency and marginal farmers’ and agricultural labourers’ develop- 
ment agency have been set up and with the permission of the 
Registrar and under such conditions as he may impose, a co-opera- 
tive society may grant loans to its agriculturist members up 00 
twenty times the amount of share capital paid up by such members. 


77. Procedure for prohibiting transactions on mortgage of immovable 
property.—(1) When it appears to the State Government that the lending of 
money on the mortgage of immovable property by any society or class of 
society shall be prohibited or restricted, it shall publish a draft order 10 the 
“Calcutta Gazette”, prohibiting or restricting each transactions. 


(2) The copies of such draft order shall be sent to the society or class of 
societies concerned. 


(3) The order so published shall not take effect until thirty days have 
elapsed since the date of publication of the order in the “Calcutta Gazette” 
and until the State Government have considered the objections, if any, received 
within fifteen days from the date of publication of the order. 


_ (4) After consideration of the objections, if any, the State Government may 
withdraw the order or republish 1 with or without modifications as it thinks 
fit, and on such re-publication the order shall become final and binding on the 
society or class of socicties mentioned in the order,

APPENDIX TO CHAPTER IV 
Conditions of Service 


[See rule 53] 


1. Conditions for appointment.—(a) No person shall be eligible for being 
appointed to any post under any co-operative society unless he possesses the 
qualifications prescribed in rule 53: 


Provided that this rule shall not apply to the employees who are already 
in the service or are deputed by the State Government. 


(b) If the Managing Committee of any society decides to enhance the 
qualifications or scale of pay of any post in the interest of the business of the 
society that shall, subject to the approval of the Registrar, prevail, but the 
present incumbent of the post concerned shall be absorbed in another post in 
the same scale of pay as was enjoyed by the incumbent concerned at the time 
ef his absorption. 


(c) No person who has not attained the age of 18 years shall be eligible for 
appointment to any post under any co-operative society. 


No person over the age of 45 years shall be directly appointed to any post 
of grades I and II; and no person over the age of 30 years shall be appointed 
to any post of grade III and grade IV provided that in case of Scheduled Castes 
and Scheduled Tribes candidates the maximum age for direct appointment to 
grade III or grade IV posts shall be 35 years and these restrictions regarding 
age Shall not apply in case of promotion or deputation or appointment from 
the service of one co-operative society by another. The following documents 
Shall be accepted as proof of age of any person selected for appointment to 
any post under a co-operative society namely:— 


(i) Age recorded in the certificate of Matriculation or School Final or 
Higher Secondary or its equivalent Examination; and 


(ii) A certificate from the head of the Educational Institution last attended 


the case of those who are not certificate-holders as mentioned in 
(i) above. 


(d) No person shall be eligible for being 000 to any post under any 
Co-operative Society without a Medical Certificate of fitness to be obtained 
from a registered medical practitioner as may be required by the Managing 


Committee which has also have to be satisfied that he possesses good character 
and antecedents. 


(6) The Managing Committee shall be the competent authority to prescribe 
Scales and type of security deposit and/or personal sureties in respect of such 
category of employees as considered necessary. The Managing Committee 
Shall also be the competent authority to revise the same from time to time if 
circumstances so demand. The officers deputed by the State Government will 
not however be required to furnish any security.

The services of all the employees shall be classified as follows:— 
(i) Permanent, (ii) Probationer, (iii) Temporary. 


A “permanent” employee means an employee who shall be engaged on a 
permanent basis after satisfactory completion of probationary period. 


A “Probationer” means an employee appointed to fill a permanent vacancy 
of a post and has not completed the probationary period specified in the letter 
of appointment or tHe further extended period. 


A probationer shall ordinarily be on probation for one year. He may 
thereatter be confirmed in the post in his work and conduct are found 
Satisfactory. The probationary period may be extended by another year at the 
discretion of the competent authority. : 


A “temporary” employee means an employee who has been engaged for a 
work which is essentially of a temporary character and likely to be finished 
within a limited period or who is temporarily employed in connection..with a 
temporary increase in work of a permanent nature or who is temporarily 
appointed in a leave vacancy. 


3. Commencement of service and seniority.—({a) Service shall be deemed 
to commence from the working day on which a person reports for duty in the 
forenoon. If he reports in the afternoon the service shall* be deemed to 
commence from the working day next following. 


Seniority in a particular post of the employees who are already in service 
of the Bank on the date on which these rules come into force shall be deter- 
mined according to the date of joining the post. If in any case of any two or 
more employees, the date of joining is the same their inter se seniority shall 
be determined according to the age, the older being the senior, and if in the 
case of such employees the date ot birth of any two or more employees is also 
the same the inter se seniority shall be decided by the Managing Committee, 
whose decision shall be final. 


(b) Seniority of the employees appointed after the commencement of these 
rules in each category of posts shall be determined in the manner as follows:— 


(i) In case of employees appointed or promoted to a post in one batch, 
the seniority shall be determined in accordance with the orders of 
Seniority specified by the appointing authority on the results of 
the test taken at the time of making the appointment or promotion. 


(ii) In other cases, seniority shall be determined with reference to date 
of appointment. But if one or more promotees and one or more 


direct recruits join on the same date the promotees shall be placed 
above the direct recruits. 


4. Pay, allowances and other concessions.—{a) The Managing Committee 
Shall be the competent authority to frame scales of pay, dearness and other 
allowances in respect of each category of employees of the society. The 
Managing Committee shall also be the competent authority to revise the same 
from time to time if circumstances so demand: 


Provided that. whese any co-operative society has incurred loss in the 
previous year, the Managing Committee shall not increase the scale of pay in 
respect of any category of its employees without the approval of the Registrar. 


(b) Unless anything is otherwise provided in the terms of the appointment 
a person on first appointment to any post under the society shall draw the 
initial pay of the post in the time-scale of pay. 


(c) If any employee is promoted from a post to a higher post or he is 
appointed to officiate in a higher post for a period exceeding one month purely 
on a temporary measure, his initial pay in the higher post shall be fixed at the 


Stage in the new pay scale next above the stage in the pay scale of the lower 
post from which he is promoted. 


(d) The annual increment in the pay scale shall accrue normally to an 
employce after he has completed one year’s service at a stage in the pay scale, 


unless it has been previously withheld for reasons of unsatisfactory work, 
conduct or any other reason.

the rules of the society concerned: 


Provided that employees drawing basic salary of Rs. 350 or above shall be

(h) The employees of the co-operative societies shall be entitled to bonus 
if admissible under the provision of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 (Act 21 
of 1965). 


5. Transfer and training —Every employee shall be liable to be transferred 
from one post to another in the same scale of pay and/or from one station to 
another in the interest of the business of a co-operative society. Every 
employee shall also be liable to join any training course as may be decided by 
the management and will be entitled to full pay and allowances during the 
training period including period of journeys to and from the training centre. 
Any delinquency on the part of an employee in carrying out such order of 
transfer or posting or training will be treated as an act of insubordination 
which may culminate in the dismissal of such an employee from the service 
of the society. 


On transfer from one station to another or for joining a training centre or 
return therefrom every employee shall be entitled to three days’ joining time, 
in addition to the time required for the journey. The Chief Executive Officer 
of the society, however, in special cases may not allow or extend the joining 
time. 


6. Leave.—(a) The following categories of leave shall be admissible to an 
employee of a co-operative society to the extent noted against each— 


(i) Casual Leave—15 days in a year. 


(ii) Compensatory Leave—An employee required to perform duties on 
any Bank holiday(s) shall be eligible for compensatory leave for a 
corresponding number of days. 


(iii) Earned Leave—15 days in a year. 
(iv) Medical Leave—15 days in a year. 


(v) Maternity Leave—6 weeks at a time and not more than three times 
during the entire period of service for a married female employee. 


Leave mentioned in clause (i), (ii) and (iii) shall be on [01] pay and that 
mentioned in clause (iv) and (v) on half pay plus full allowances in all cases. 


(vi) Extraordinary Leave—This may be granted to any employee in 
Special circumstances when no other leave is, by rulc, admissible. 
This kind of leave shall be sanctioned as leave without pay. It 
shall be at the discretion of the sanctioning authority to fix the 
amount of extraordinary leave to be granted in each case. ] an 
employee fails to resume duty on the expiry of extraordinary leave, 
he shall automatically cease to be in the service of the society. 


(b) No leave of any kind of category can be claimed as of right and the 
grant of leave shall be subject to the exigencies of service and work and the 
circumstances of each case. 


(c) An employee shall be liable to be recalled from leave other than 
medical /maternity leave or casual leave if the exigencies of work so require 
provided the society bears tne actual travel fare of the employee recalled from 
leave if at the time of recall he is spending his leave at a place other than his 
headquarters,

7. Conduct and discipline——(a) Every employee of a co-operative society 
shall at all times: 


(i) maintain absolute integrity; 
(ii) maintain devotion to duty; 


(iii) abide by and comply with the rules of the society and all orders and 
directions of the superior authorities; 


(iv) discharge his dyty to the best of his ability in the interest of the 
society. 


(b) All employees shall so manage the private affairs to avoid habitual 
indebtedness or insolvency; and an employee against whom any legal proceed- 
ing is instituted for the recovery of any debt due from him or for adjudging 
him as an insolvent shall forthwith report the full facts of the legal proceedings 
to the society. 


(c) No employee shall join, or continue to be a member of association, the 
objects or activities of which are prejudicial to the interests of the sovereignty 
and integrity of India or public order or morality or to the interests of the 
society. 


(৫) No employee shall, except in accordance with any general or special 
Order of the Managing Committee or his superior officers or in the performance 
in good faith of the duties assigned to him communicate directly or indirectly 
the contents of any official document or any part thereof or other information 
to any other employee or any person to whom he is not authorised to commu- 
nicate such contents or information. 


(e) No employee shall accept or permit any member of his family or anv 
person acting on his behalf to accept any _ illegal জান or pecuniary 
advantage or gifts, etc., from any person or agent having dealing with the 
society. 


(f) No employee shall engage himself or participate in any demonstration or 
strike which is prejudicial to the interests of the society, of the sovereignty 
and integrity of India, the security of the State, friendly relations with foreign 
States, public order, decency or morality, or which involve contempt of court, 
defamation or incitement to an offence. 


(g) No employee shall, in any radio broadcast or any document published 
in his own name or anonymously, pseudonymously or in the name of any other 
person or in any Communication to the press or in any public utterance, make 
any statement of fact of opinion which has the effect of any adverse criticism 
of any policy or action of the society, or may embarrass the relations between 
the society, Central Government and the Government of West Bengal, or any 
other organisation: 


_ Provided that nothing in this rule shall apply to any statements made or 
views expressed by an employee in his official capacity or in the due 
performance of the duties assigned to him. 


(h) No employee shall, except for unavoidable reasons, absent himself from 


without taking prior sanction of leave or overstay the period of sanctioned‏ کت

Provided that the period of authorised training, participation in seminars, 
conferences, with proper sanction, including the period of journeys undertaken 
for that purpose will not be treated as absence from duty.

8. Misconduct and disciplinary action.—(a) The following acts _ shall 
constitute misconduct on behalf of an employee, namely:— 


(i) wilful insubordination or disobedience, whether in alliance with a 
co-employee or not, of any lawful and reasonable order of superior; 


(ii) wilfully avoiding work or abetment or instigation thercof; 


(iii) theft, fraud, misappropriation or dishonesty in connection with 
employer’s business or property or otherwise; 


(iv) habitual absence without leave, overstaying the sanctioned leave 
without sufficient grounds or proper and satisfactory explanation or 
habitual late attendance; 


(৮) commission of any act subversive of discipline or good behaviour in 
any public place such as drunkenness, riotous, disorderly or 
indecent behaviour, gambling or taking or giving bribes or any 
illegal gratification of any kind whatsoever; 


(vi) wilful damage to work or goods in process or to any property of the 
society; 

(vii) habitual neglect of work or gross or habitual negligence; . 

(viii) disclosing to an unauthorised person any information with regard to 


the society which may come into the possession of the employee in 
the course of his work; 


(ix) indulging in scurrilous attacks against the management and other 
Superiors of the employee in his official capacity; 


(x) delivering speeches or raising slogans tending to incite workers to 
violence; 


(xi) contempt of rules and disrespect of authority and general affront to 
the management; 


(xii) impertinent, rude and disrespectful language which is subversive to 
discipline. 
(b) The following penalties may be imposed for such misconduct by the 
Disciplinary Authority on an employee, namely:— 


(i) dismissal from service which shall ordinarily be a disqualification for 
future employment under the society; 


(ii) reduction in rank to a lower grade in service or post on a lower time 
scale; 


(iii) withholding of incremnets with cumulative effect; 
(iv) withholding of annual increment, without cumulative effect; 


(v) recovery from pay of the whole or part of any pecuniary loss caused 
to the society by negligence or breach of orders; 


(vi) censure; 
(vii) fine. 


Explanation.—The following shall not amount to a_ penalty within the 
meaning of this rule, namely:— 


(i) stoppage of an employee at the efficiency bar in the time scale of pay 
if any, on the ground of his unfitness to cross the bar; 


(ii) reversion to a lower grade or post of an employee officiating in a 
higher grade or post for want of vacancy or on administrative 
grounds unconnected with his conduct; 


(iii) reversion to his permanent service, grade or post of an employee 
appointed on probation to another service, grade or post during or 
at the end of the period of probation; 


(iv) termination of service— 


(a) of an employee appointed on probation during or at the end of the 
period of probation or ; 


(b) of any employee employed temporarily or under an agreement, in 


accordance with the terms of such agreement or at one month’s 
notice, for abolition of the post or otherwise;

(c) for the purpose of imposing any penalty under this rule the appoint- 
ing authority shall also be the ‘Disciplinary Authority’. The 
appointing authority, may, however, direct in accordance with 
rules 47 and 51 that the Executive Officer, Managing Director, 
‘Secretary or Manager of the society, shall be the disciplinary 
authority. But no penalty shall be imposed until the charges 
against an employee have been properly enquired into by an 
Enquiring Officer to be appointed by the Disciplinary Authority 
and the employee has been given an opportunity of explaining 
the charges personally and/or in writing: 


Provided that if any penalty is imposed by any authority other than the 
Managing Committee of the society an appeal against the order imposing the 
penalty shall lie to the Chairman. When the penalty is imposed or approved 
by the Managing Committee, no appeal shall lie against it. 


9. Suspension.—(a) An employee of the society whose conduct requires 
investigation on a charge of misconduct enumerated in clause (a) of paragraph 
8 may be placed under suspension by the Chief Executive Officer of the society, 
by whatever designation he may be called pending the result of enquiry into 
his alleged misconduct, if in the opinion of such authority, the attendance of 
such an employee on duty during the period of investigation of charges against 
him is likely to vitiate the proceedings. 


(b) No employee who has been suspended is entitled to absent himself 
from his station during the period of his suspension. 


(c) During the period of suspension, an employee shall be entitled to 
subsistence allowance equal to 50 cer cent. of his salary with other usual 
allowances admissible to him in full or at such rate as will be fixed by the 
Managing Committee from time to time. 


No payment of any kind, other than the authorised subsistence allowance 
and other admissible allowance, is to be made to an employee during the period 
of suspension. 


An order of suspension shall continue to remain in force until it is modified 
or revoked by the authority who suspended him or by the Managing Committee. 


(d) When the charge against an employee is held to have been unjustifiable 
or not wholly justifiable, or when an employee who has been dismissed, 
removed or suspended is reinstated, the Managing Committee may grant to 
him for the whole period of his suspension— 


(i) if he is honourably acquitted, the full pay and allowances, if any, to 
which he would have been entitled if he had not been dismissed, 
removed or suspended minus the subsistence, and other such 
allowances drawn by him. 


(ii) If otherwise, such portion of his pay and allowances, if any, as the 
Managing Committee may decide. 


In any case falling under clause (i) above, the period of subpension will be 
treated as a period spent on duty. In any case falling under clause (11) the 
period may be treated as on duty or on leave. But it will not be so treated 
unless the Managing Committee directs accordingly. 


(e) If any employee is absent from duty by reason of his being arrested or 
committed to prison either for debt or on criminal charge, he shall not be 
allowed to draw any pay, leave salary or allowances for the period of such 
absence until decision of the case against him, when an adjustment of 115 
emoluments may be made according to the circumstances of the case, the full 
amount being given only in the event of the employee being acquitted of blame, 
or if the imprisonment was for debt, of its being proved that the employee’s 
liability arose from circumstances beyond his control. When full amount is 
allowed, the period of such absence from duty will be treated as a period spent 
on duty. When less than full amount is allowed, the period may be treated 
as on duty or on leave as the Managing Committee may decide. 


10. Resignation, retirement and terminal bencfits—(a) A permanent 
employee desirous of tendering resignation from the service of a society shall 
give three months’ notice to the society in writing, failing which he shall be 
liable to pay an amount equal to three months’ salary and allowances.

A probationer or a temporary employee desirous of tendering resignation 
from .the service of the society before completion of his term shall give one 
month's notice to the society in writing, failing which he shall be liable to pay 
an amount equal to one month's salary and allowances: 


Provided that the Managing Committee may, in exceptional circumstances, 
dispense with the requirement of notice or reduce the requisite period of notice. 


(b) Except with the sanction of the Managing Committee resignation will 
not be permitted while the conduct of an employee is under investigation or 
until all departmental claims against him are settled. While placing before 
the Managing Committee an application for resignation, it should be stated 
whether there is anything adverse to the applicant or whether anything is due 
from him to the society. 


The authority receiving an applicatiqn from an employee asking for per- 
mission to resign should at once adjust all claims of the society outstanding 
against the applicant, and his resignation should not be accepted until his 
accounts are fully adjusted and charge of his office is formally made over. 


If without formally tendering resignation or having sent 015 resignation, 
an employee quit his post before receiving intimation of acceptance or before 
expiry of the requisite period of notice three or one month’s salary and allow- 
ances, as may be decided by Managing Committee, will be recovered from dues 
payable to him, from security deposit or from Provident Fund. 


(c) Every employee appointed in any post under a co-operative society 
shall unless he resigned or is discharged/dismissed earlier, retire on attaining 
the age of 58 years. 


Employees of co-operative society shall be eligible to এল of gratuity 
as indicated below on fulfilment of the following terms and conditions:— 


(1) When an employee retires after completing ten years of qualifying 
service, after attaining 50 years of age, he shall be granted when he 
relires from service, salary for the period of earned leave due to 
him and a retiring gratuity at the rate of half of the monthly basic 
pay drawn by him at the time of his retirement for each completed 
year of service subject to a maximum of fifteen times the salary or 
Rs. 6,000, whichever is less: 


Provided that in case of an apex society, the maximum amount shall be 
Rs. 10,000 


(2) When an employee who has completed five years’ qualifying service, 
dies while in service, a death gratuity not exceeding half of the 
monthly pay for each completed year of qualifying service, subject 
to a minimum of three times and maximum of fifteen times the pay 
drawn by him at the time of his death or Rs. 6,000 whichever is 
less, shall be paid to the person or persons on whom the right to 
receive the gratuity has been conferred by the deceased or if there 
be no such person to his legal heirs. Provided that in case of an 
apex society the minimum should be six times of the salary and 
the maximum should be Rs. 10,000. 


(3) When an employee after ten years’ of qualifying service becomes at any 
time physically or mentally incapable of rendering further service 
he shall be granted salary for the period of leave due to him and 
a gratuity at the rate of half of the monthly pay for each complet- 
ed year of service subject to a maximum of 15 times the pay drawn 
by him at the time of termination of his service for any one of the 
reasons set forth above: 


Provided that when an employee retires voluntarily or resigns before 
attaining 50 years of age, he shall not be entitled to any gratuity.

business and submit an application in the manner provided in rule 14 for 
registration of such amendments, 


(2) The notice required undef sub-section (2) of section 43 shall be issued 
under a certificate of posting.

87. Levy of water and embankment rate.—A مہ-۲‎ ۲۸1۷ ۲٢ society may levy

(a) such percentage of the value of estimated produce of the land

88. Procedure for notifying non-members to join a co-operative farming 
society.—(1) The directions to be given to the non-members by a co-operative 
society under clause (d)’ of sub-section (10) of section 49 shall be by a written 
memorandum in the form set forth in the schedule. 


(2) The time within which a non-member shall join the co-operative society

from the date of receipt of the memorandum referred to in sub-rule (1), and at

fee and the value of one or more shares as required by the bye-laws of the 
concerned society. 


(3) The memorandum referred to in sub-rule (1) shall be signed and dated 
by the Chief-Executive Officer of the society and shall be issued under the 
common seal of the society. 


89. Time within which, and the manner in which, mortgage deed referred 
to in sub-section (2) of section 52 to be sent to the Registering Officer.— 
(1) The period within which a copy of the mortgage deed, referred to in sub-

from the date of its execution, and before such document is sent as aforesaid, 
it shall be duly certified by the Manager, Branch Manager, on any officer of the 
Government deputed by the State Government or the Registrar under section 
24, as the case may be 


(2) Such a document shall be sent to the Registering Officer concerned by 
a messenger or by registered post with acknowledgment due. 


90. Application for compromise between a_ co-operative society and 105 
creditors.—(1) An application to the Registrar under section 54 shall contain 
the proposed terms and conditions of the compromise or arrangement and, 
where the applicant is a society, shall be accompanied by a resolution of the 
general meeting proposing the compromise or arrangement. 


(2) On receipt of such application, the Registrar may, if he is of opinion 
that the proposed terms and conditions of the compromise or arrangement 
shall tig beneficial to the parties, give directions as to the following matters, 
namely:— 


(i) the date or dates when the scheme of compromise or arrangement 
shall be placed before the creditors; 


(ii) the time and place where the meeting (or mectings) of the creditors 
shall be held; 


(iii) the preparation by a person duly authorised by him of a statement 
containing the names of the creditors likely to be affected and the 
amount due by the society to each of them; and 


(iv) the time within which the Chairman of the meeting shall forward his 
report to the Registrar. 


(3) Together with the direction to be given under sub-rule (2), the Registrar 
may refer any question touching the compromise or arrangement for considera- 
tion and decision of the meeting, and the Chairman, of the meeting shall put 
such question to the meeting. 


91. Notice of creditors’ meeting.—(1) On receipt of the order of the 
Registrar, the society or the liquidator (in case of a society in respect of which 
an order of winding up has been passed) shall, before thirty clear days of the 
date fixed for the meeting, issue a notice— 


(a) of the date, time and place of the meeting, and

92. Appointment of proxy by creditor unable to attend meeting.—(1) A 
creditor, who is unable to be present in person in the meeting, may appoint 
another person as his proxy in writing in the form set forth in the schedule. 


(2) The appointment of proxy shall not be valid unless the form, duly 
filled in, is deposited at the office from which the notice of the meeting is 
issued at least forty-eight hours before the time fixed for holding the meeting. 


93. Procedure to be followed at meeting—{1) On the date, time and place 
appointed for the meeting, the creditors present shall choose a person to be 
Chairman of the meeting. 


(2) Immdediately after the Chairman has been elected, he shall read out 
a statement, duly authenticated by an officer authorised in this behalf by the 
Registrar, containing the names of those creditors to whom notices under sub- 
rule (1) of rule 91 have been issued and the amount due by the society to each. 


(3) If as many creditors as are required by sub-section (2) of section 54 
are present, the Chairman shall read to the meeting the term of the proposed 
compromise or arrangement and shall put to the meeting the question whether 
the proposed compromise or arrangement is to be accepted. 


(4) Any creditor present may move an amendment to the compromise or 
arrangement proposed, if he has given notice of such amendment in accordance 
with sub-rule (3) of rule 91: 


Provided that the Chairman may put to the meeting any amendment 
proposed by a creditor of which such notice has not been given, if a majority 
of the creditors present agree that such amendment be considered by 1116 
meeting. 


(5) Every amendment shall be put to the meeting in such order as the 
Chairman may consider convenient for the purpose of discussion. 


(6) The persons present at the meeting may speak on the motion put by 
the Chairman or any amendment moved thereto in such order as the Chair- 
man may direct. The Chairman may fix a time limit for speeches. 


94. Minutes of mecting.—{1) The Chairman shall cause minutes to be 
prepared of the proceedings of the meeting and shall sign them before leaving 
the meeting. 


(2) The minutes shall contain the names of all creditors present at the 
meeting and if a poll is demanded, the number of creditors voting for or 
against the motion or any amendment moved thereto. 


(3) The Chairman shall forthwith forward to the Registrar a copy of the 
minutes of the proceedings of the meeting together with a copy of the terms 
of the compromise or arrangement, if any, duly signed by him. 


95. Dissolution of meeting, if required number of creditors are not present. 
—The Chairman shall dissolve the meeting if the number of creditors required 
under sub-section (2) of section 51 is not present and shall report to the 
Registrar,

96. Publication of compromise or arrangement.—A compromise or arrange- 
ment, sanctioned by the Registrar shall be published by the society by— 


(1) displaying it for thirty days in a conspicuous place at the registered 
office of the society; 


(ii) displaying it at such other conspicuous places in the area over which 
the society operates and in such other manner as the Registrar may 
direct; and 


(iii) sending copies of the same to all creditors to whom notices have been 
issued under sub-rule (1) of rule 91. 


CHAPTER VI 
Property and funds of Co-operative Societies 


97. Investment of funds.—In addition to the manner specified in section 55 
or in sub-section (5) of section 56, a co-operative society may invest or deposit 
its funds— 


(a) with the State Co-operative Bank; 


(b) with the Central Co-operative Bank of the area within which its 
registered address lies (including the branches of the said Central 
Co-operative Bank, if any), 


(c) in any other manner permitted by the Registrar. 


98. Creation of reserve fund in a society with unlimited liability—(1) In 
every cO-operative society with shares and unlimited liability, not less than 
one-half of the net profits in any year shall be carried to the reserve fund until 
that fund is equal to one-half of the total borrowed capital; thereafter not 
less than one-third of the net profits in any year until the reserve fund equals 
the amount of borrowed capital, and thereafter not less than one,fourth of the 
net profits in any year shall be carried to the reserve fund: 


Provided that if by any increase in the borrowed capital, the proportion of 
the reserve fund to the borrowed capital is reduced in any year, the share of 
the net profits to be credited to the reserve fund shall be raised to the extent 
required until the proportion is restored. 


(2) In every co-operative society with unlimited liability and without shares, 
not less than three-fourths of the net profits in any year shall be carried to 
the reserve fund. 


99. Use of reserve and other funds in the business of a society.—(1) A 
co-operative society may, subject to the approval of the Registrar and to such 
conditions as he may impose, use in its business— 


(i) up to one-fourth of its reserve fund, when the owned capital is less 
than the borrowed capital; 


(ii) up to one-half of its reserve fund, when the owned capital is equal to, 
Or exceeds, the borrowed capital; and 


(iii) the entire reserve fund, when there is no borrowed capital. 


(2) No part of the Bad Debt Fund, Agricultural Credit Stabilisation Fund 
or Inventory Loss Fund, maintained in terms of section 56, shall be used in the 
business of a co-operative society except in accordance with the rules, as may 
be framed by the State Government, for use of these funds. 


100. Provident fund of the employces.—(1) A co-operative society, coming 
within the purview of the Employees’ Provident Fund Act, 1952, shall 
establish, contribute to, and administer an Employees’ Provident Fund 
inconsistent with the provisions therein contained. 


(2) (a) Other co-operative societies may establish provident fund to be 
called the Employees Contributory Provident Fund. 


(b) A society creating such a fund shall, with the approval of the general 
body of members in a general meeting, formulate regulations for its manage- 


ment. Among other relevant matters, such regulations shall provide for the 
following, namely:— 


(i) authority to administer the Employees’ Contributory Provident Fund;

101, Declaration of dividend, rebate, etc—(1) In every co-operative 
society with shares, dividend may be declared up to a maximum of 12 per cent. 
per annum, on the amount paid up on shares. 


(2) (a) In any co-operative society dealing in goods, rebate may be allowed 
on the total amount of payments made by a member during a co-operative 
year towards his purchase of goods from the society during that year. 


(b) In case of credit societies, rebate in interest may be allowed to members 
making timely repayment. 


(3১ No dividend shall be paid by a society with shares and_ unlimited 
liability without the previous sanction of the Registrar. 


(4) No dividend or rebate shall be paid in any co-operative society unless 
such dividend or rebate is recommended by the Managing Committee and 
approved by the general meeting. 


(5) A society incurring loss shall not pay bonus to its employees at more 
than the minimum rate prescribed under the Payment of Bonus Act without 
the approval of the Registrar. 


102. Co-operative Development Fund.—{1) Every society shall, after the 
close of each co-operative year and after the audited balance-sheet is 
considered in a general meeting, while allocating the net profits, if any, make 
such contribution to the co-operative development fund as may be approved 
in the general mecting, subject to clause (a) of section 58. Such contribution 
shall, within two months from the date of the general meeting, be remitted to 
the West Bengal State Co-operative Bank Limited or to the Central Co-opera- 
tive Bank of the area concerned for credit to the fund. Where such 
contribution is remitted to the Central Co-operative Bank, such bank shall 
transfer the same to the West Bengal State Co-operative Bank within a period 
of thirty days, from the date of the receipt of the remittance. 


(2) (1) The funds shall be administered by a committee, called the Co-ope- 
rative Development Fund Committee, to be set up by the State Government, 
composed of the following persons, namely:— 


(a) Chairman of the State Co-operative Union—Chairman. 


(b) Three representatives of Agricultural Societies, to be nominated by the 
State Government-—Members. 


(c) Two representatives of non-agricultural societies, to be nominated 
by the State Government—Members. 


(d) One nominee of the Registrar—Member. 


(ii) The Executive Officer of the West Bengal State Co-operative Union, 
and in absence of such Executive Officer, the senior co-operative education 
officer of the said union, shall be the Secretary of the committee. 


(iii) The members of the committee shall hold office for a term of three 
years from the date of their appointment.

society may make contributions under sub-clause (iii) of clause (b) of section 58 
to the Co-operative Employees’ Benefit Fund, the West Bengal State Co-opera- 
tive Development Fund or any other fund which may be approved by the State 
Government by a general or special order made in this behalf. 


CHAPTER VII 
Privileges, liabilities and obligations of members of Co-operative Societies 


104. Appeal against refusal to admit any applicant as member of a 
society.—On receipt of an appeal under sub-section (4) of section 59, the 
Registrar shall issue clear seven days’ notice to the appellant and to the society 
concerned fixing the date, time and place of hearing; and after affording the 
parties an opportunity of being heard, the Registrar shall make such order as 
he deems proper and the order shall be binding on the society with effect from 
the date of receipt of the same. No resolution of the Managing Committee 
admitting the appellant as member shall be necessary. 


105. Disqnalification for voting—No member of a _ primary or a central 
Society shall be eligible for appointment to vote in the affairs of another 
co-operative society, of which the firstmentioned society is a member— 


(a) if such member is disqualified under the provisions of the Act or the 
rules for voting in the affairs of the society of which he is a 
member or for being appointed as a director: or 


(b) if, in the case of a primary society, the member is in arrear in payment 
of his dues and, the Managing Committee has not granted any 
extension of time for making such payment. 


106. Exercise of rights of membership.—(1) (a) Before a member may 
exercise rights of membership, he shall— 


(i) sign a declaration in such form, as may be required by the Managing 
Committee, undertaking that he shall be bound by the bye-laws of 
the society, 


(ii) sign the register of members, and 


(iii) make payment of such amount to the society, as may be determined 
by 00006 Committee, within ninety days fram the date of 
emand.

107. Nominal members.—Notwithstanding anything contained in the 
rules or the bye-laws in regard to membership, a co-operative society may 
admit in its own interest any person residing in the registered area of operation 
of the society, as a nominal member, subject to the following conditions 
namely:— 


(a) Any person applying for nominal membership shall submit an 
application to the society in the form prescribed by the Managing 
Committee and make such payment to the society as may be 
provided for in the bye-laws. The application shall be supported 
by at least two members ‘of the society. 


(b) The Managing Committee shall, after due consideration, sanction ০01" 
refuse an application for nominal membership, within 45 days from 
the date of receipt of the application: 


Provided that every application for nominal membership shall be dealt 
with in the manner provided for in sub-section (3) of section 59 
and the proviso thereto. 


(c) A nominal member shall be entitled to receive a special type of certifi-

kept by the society, shall be prima facie evidence of the following 
purticulars entered therem namely:— 


(i) the date on which the name of such person was entered in such 
register as a nominal member; and 


(ii) the date on which any such person ceaSed to be a nominal member. 


(d) A nominal member shall cease to be a member on his resignation, 
conviction in a criminal case, insolvency, lunacy, bankruptcy, or his 
leaving the area of operation without any intention to return: 


Provided that his obligation to the society as a nominal member shall 
subsist until he has discharged all his liabilities to the society. 


(e) The liability of such members for the debts of the society shall be 
limited to the payment made by them; and all fees paid by such 
members, which shall neither be transferable nor জনা e, shall 
be credited direct to the Reserve Fund of the society. 


(f) A nominal member shall sign a declaration to the effect that he shall 
be bound by the bye-laws of the society. 


(g) For the purposes of section 86 and section 126, the word ‘member’ 
shall be deemed to include ‘nominal members’ also. 


108. Associate members.—Notwithstanding anything contained in the 
rules, or the bye-laws in regard to membership, a co-operative society may 
admit in its own interest, any ও Or مه‎ association or body of persons 
residing in the সান area of operation of the society, as associate member 
subject to the following conditions namely:— 


(a’ Any person or association or body of persons applying for associate 
membership shall submit an application to the society in the form 
prescribed by the Managing Committee, supported by at least two 
members of the society, and make such payment to the society in 
respect of such membership as may be provided for in the bye-laws.
