109. An association or body of persons as a member of a_ co-operative 
society—When any association or body of persons is admitted as a member 
of a co-operative society, it shall appoint any one of its  office-bearers or 
officers, by an instrument in writing, to exercise its rights and perform 15 
duties in relation to such society. 


110. Manner of recalling a loan not utilised for the proper purpose.— 
Where the Managing Committee of a co-operative society has reasonable cause 
to believe that a member has not utilised a loan for the purpose for which it 
was advanced, the society may, by a notice, direct the member to show cause, 
within such time as may be specified in the notice, why the loan shall not be 
recalled, and where no cause is shown to the satisfaction of the society within 
the time specified, the society— 

(a) may recall the loan, and 


(b) if the loan is not refunded immediately on recall, shall apply to the 
ا‎ for an award under section 126 in order to recover the 
oan. 


111. Restriction on interest of a member of a society with limited liability 
and shares.—Where the liability of the members of a co-operative society 15 
limited by shares, no member other than a co-operative society shall hold more 
than one-seventh of the share capital of the society. 


112. Nomination of transferee.—A member of a co-operative society may, 
in accordance with section 69, nominate in writing any person to whom or to 
whose credit the share or interest or the valye of such share or interest shall, 
On his death bé paid or transferred under the provisions of the Act: 


Provided that such member may, from time to time, revoke or vary such 
nomination in writing. 

(2) Every co-operative society shall keep a register of all persons (if any), 
so nominated. 


(3) In case the nominee of a member dies, the member shall report the 
death to the society. ۱ 


113. Disposal of deceased members’ share or interest and procedure for 
calculation of value of shares—(1) When upon the death of a member of a 
co-operative society, the question of transferring the share, or paying interest, 
of such deceased member arises, and the Managing Committee of such society 
finds that the deceased member did not nominate any body as his nominee in 
accordance with the provisions of section 69, or that the existence or residen- 
tial address of the person nominated cannot be ascertained, or that for. any 
other sufficient cause such transfer or payment cannot be made_ without 
unreasonable delay, the Managing Committee may transfer the share or pay 
interest of such deceased member in favour of, or to, any person who presents 
in writing his or her claim for the said share or interest, and produces, in 
Support of such claims, probate, letter of administration or succession certifi- 
Cate issued by a competent court having jurisdiction, and makes a written 
declaration in an affidavit before a Magistrate that he or she is the rightful 
claimant, being the legal heir or representative of the deceased. 


(2) (a) Where a co-operative society has to make a refund of the value of 
a share, the value of the share shall be deemed to be equal to the amount paid 
upon the share: 


Provided that where a portion of the assets is estimated to be bad or 
doubtful in the latest audited balance shect, and is not covered by funds 
created out of profits, the Managing Committee may, for the purpose of such 
payment, reduce the value of the share, in the same proportions as the agegre- 
gate amount of assets which are not bad or doubtful, less the amount of outside 
liabilities, bears to the paid-up share capital. 


_ (b) Where a transfer of share or interest is made, the value of the share or 
interest shall be deemed to be the sum actually paid by the member for 006 
acquisition of such share or interest.

114. Publication of preliminary order made under section 76 or section 77, 
~—(1) When the Registrar makes a preliminary order providing for the— 


(a) amalgamation of two or more co-operative societies into one society 
under section 76, or 


(b) division of a co-operative society into two or more societies under 
section 77, or 


(c) transfer of assets and liabilities of one co-operative society to another 
society under section 77, 


he shall— 


(i) publish such order in the Official Gazette along with a notice calling 
upon the society or societies to be amalgamated or the society or 
societies to be divided or the transferor or the transferee societies, 
as the case may be, and every member or creditor of such society 
or societies to make objections or suggestions, ifg any, to the 
Registrar with respect to such order within two moff®hs from the 
date of publication of such order in the Official Gazette, 


(ii) simultaneously send a copy of such order and notice, by registered 
post, to such society or societies, and 


(111) expeditiously send a copy of such order to the financing bank of 
which such society or societies may be member or members. 


(2) Every society, receiving copy of an order and notice referred to in 
sub-clause (ii) of sub-rule (1), shall, within seven days of their receipt, com- 
municate, in writing, the substance thereof to its members and creditors either 
by delivery by hand after taking proper receipt or by registered post. 


CHAPTER IX 
Audit, inspection and inquiry 


115. Date of audit and audit fees—{1) The audit of a co-operative society 
shall be made and the audit report shall be submitted— 


(i) in case of a primary agricultural credit society, within nine months, 
and 


(ii) in case of any other society, within six months, from the date of the 
close of the co-operative year: 


Provided that if the audit officer fails to submit the audit report within 
the time as aforesaid, the Registrar shall arrange for completion of 
audit in course of the next three months, in such manner, as he 
may deem fit. 


(2) A co-operative society, other than a society dealing in goods shall pay 
an audit fee calculated on the average working capital in the last day of each 
mouth of the co-operative year, for which the audit fee will be due. 


(3) In the case of a society dealing in goods, the audit fee shall be calculated 
on the total value of the goods sold during the year: 


Provided that where a society, in addition to other business, deals in goods, 
the average working capital referred to in sub-rule (2) or the total value of 
the goods sold by the society during the year, whichever is higher, shall be 
taken into account in calculation of audit fee. 


(4) The audit fee shall be calculated at the following rates, namely— 


(a) sixty-two paise for every one hundred rupees or part thereof subject 
to the maximum of one hundred and forty rupees in the case of a 
ٴ‎ primary society with unlimited liability; 


(b) gaze paise for every one hundred rupees or part thereof up to 
s. 50,000, subject to a maximum of Rs. 250, thereafter Rs. 25 for 

every Rs. 25,000 or part thereof, up to one lakh of rupees, and 
thereafter Rs. 50 for every Rs. 50,000 or part thereof, subject to an

shall be assessed— 


(a) in case of a primary agricultural credit society which is a member of 
a Central Co-operative Bank, upon the said bank, and 


(b) in case of any other society, upon the socicty. 


(2) The audit fee paid by a Central Co-operative Bank on behalf of a 
member agricultural credit society shall be deemed to be a loan due 109 the 
bank by the society and shall be recoverable from the society concerned like 
any other loan payable by the society. 


117. Exemption and remission of Audit fees——(1) Societies registered at 
the Co-operative Training Centres, Public Health Socicties and Housing 
Societies, which have completed construction and/or allotted all the plots and 
houses under the scheme undertaken to the members, and societies less than 
18 months old excepting the societies which have raised a working capital of 
Rs. 10,000 or more during the said period of 18 months shall not be liable to 
pay audit fees. 


(2) The Registrar may, at his discretion, remit either wholly or in part the 
audit fee payable by any society. 


118. Payment of Audit fee—(l1) Where the audit of the accounts of a 
co-operative society 15 ccnducted by a departmental officer, the audit fee shall 
be deposited, within a period of three months from the date of submission of 
the audit report, in the nearest treasury or the sub-treasury of the area, as 
the case my be, under the appropriate receipt head of the State Government. 


(2) Where the accounts of a society are audited by an audit officer, not 
being a departmental audit officer, the audit fee shall be paid, within a period 
of three months from the date of submission of the audit report, direct to such 
Audit Officer.

119. Procedure of Audit.—(1) Unless the Registrar directs otherwise, the 
audit of a co-operative society shall be conducted in the registered office of 
the society and at the branches and pay offices, if any. 


(2) Previous intimation shall be given to the society before the audit is 
commenced: 


Provided that the verification or examination required by clauses (a), (b), 
and (c) of sub-section (4) of section 79, may be carried out without any 
previous intimation to the society. 


(3) The officers and employees of the society shall give the audit officer 
all assistance necessary, for the completion of the audit, and for this purpose 
in particular, prepare such statements and take such action with regard to the 
verification or examination of its accounts, as he may require. 


120. Form of Audit statements.—The statements of accounts. shall be 
prepared by the Managing Committee in the form set forth in the schedule 
or in such other forms as the Registrar may approve. 


121. Scope of Audit.—({1) The audit shall include annual audit, running 
audit or re-audit, where considered necessary by the Registrar. The Managing 
Committee of a co-operative society may further arrange to have its accounts 
internally audited on a periodical or other basis, as deemed proper, by such 


person or persons and on such terms as may be decided by the Managing 
Committee: 


Provided that each apex society shall arrange to have its accounts inter- 
nally audited in such manner and on periodical or other basis as is deemed 
proper by the Managing Committee. 


Explanation.—({i) “annual audit” means audit of the accounts of ج‎ co- 
Operative society for every co-operative year, 


(ii) “running audit” means audit of the accounts of a co-operative society 
within the co-operative year on monthly or quarterly basis, as is deemed 
necessary by the Registrar, “re-audit’” means audit of the accounts of the co- 


operative society to check up the quality of audit of the society conducted 
by any Audit officer. 


(2) The audit officer shall examine the monetary transactions of a society 
in so far as may be necessary for the purpose of ascertaining whether there 
has been material impropriety or irregularity in the expenditure or in the 
realisation of moneys due to the society and whether any transaction infringes 
any provisions of the Act, rules or bye-laws, or any directions of the Managing 
Committee. In case of difference of opinion between the audit officer and 
the society in regard to the propriety of any of its monetary transactions, the 
Registrar shall decide the matter and the decision shall be final. 


122. Audit objections and audit report.—{1) While conducting the statutory 
audit of a co-operative society, the audit officer may issue, from time to time 
during audit, interim objections to the secretary of the society or to the officer 
performing the duties of the Secretary for compliance or explaining the effects 
and irregularities pointed out in such objections. The Secretary or the officer 
performing the duties of the Secretary, as the case may be, shall return the 
interim obections sheets with the compliance report to the audit officer within 
the time specified by the audit officer. The audit officer shall review the 
compliance report and waive such objections which, in his opinion, have been 
complied with satisfactorily and shall incorporate the remaining objections in 
the annual or running audit report, as the case may be. 


(2) In addition to what has been stated in sub-section (1) of section ۵, 
the audit report shall state— 


(a) whether or not the audit officer has obtained all the information and 
explanations which he required; 


(b) whether or not, in his opinion, the balance sheet and the profit and 


loss accounts referred to in the report are drawn up in conformity 
with the law; 


(c) whether or not such balance sheet exhibits a true and correct account 
of the state of the society’s affairs according to the best of his 


information and the explanation given tn him and as shown by the 
books of the society;

123. Doubtful debt—If a member fails for three consecutive years 
without reasonable cause to pay at least 25 per cent. of each of the instalments 
of principal and interest fixed for repayment of a loan at the time of its issue, 
then notwithstanding that on an examination of his assets and the assets of 
his sureties the debt appears to be covered by the value of such assets, the 
debt may be considered doubtful. 


124. Bad debt.—({1) When the total amount due by a member to a_ ০০- 
operative society by way of principal and interest exceeds the aggregate, of his 
assets and the available assets of his sureties, and the amount due by way of 
arrear interest exceeds three years’ demand, such excess of his total dues over 
the total assets shall be considered bad debt. 


(2) A doubtful debt, if not recovered after action has been taken under 
Chapter X or section 126 to recover it or the recovery of which has become 
barred by limitation, shall be considered bad. 


125. Writing off bad debts—{1) Any debt considered bad shall, if so 
approved by the Registrar, be written off by the general meeting in the order 
below against— 


(a) the bad debt fund, or any fund created out of profits as provision for 
bad debts; 


(b) any other fund created out of profits but not ear-marked for any 
specific purpose; 


(c) the reserve fund constituted under section 56. 


(2) Where the society is a member of a financing bank and is indebted to 
it the Registrar shall consult the financing bank before sanctioning the writing 
off of any debt. 


126. Rectification of defects—A co-operative society shall remove the 
defects pointed out in the audit report and shall submit to the Registrar a 
compliance report within sixty days from the date of receipt of an audit report 
by the society. In special circumstances, the period of sixty days may be 
extended by the Registrar on the request of the society. If the Registrar is 
not satisfied with the compliance report submitted by the society, he shall 
direct it to send further compliance report on the lines specified by him within 
Such time as he may specify, and the society shall make further compliance 
report to the Registrar within the time specified by him. 


127. Inspection of societies by officers of financing bank.—An_ officer of 
a financing bank or a society who— 


(i) is a regular employee of the bank or the society, as the case may be, 
and has received training, to the satisfaction of the Registrar, 
necessary for inspecting a society, and 


41) possesses, such qualifications as the Registrar may, from time to time, 
require for inspection of a society 


may be certified as competent to inspect the co-operative societies,

CHAPTER X‏ 


Settlement of disputes 


128. Disputes and appointment of arbitrators—(1) When the Registrar 
decides to refer a dispute to a board of arbitrators comprising more than one 
arbitrator, he shall— 


(i) issue a notice calling on each of the parties to nominate one person 
as its nominee within such time as he may direct, and where a 
party consists of more than one person, such persons shall jointly 
make only one nomination; 


(11) nominate the third-arbitrator who shall act as a Chairman. 


(2) If a party fails to make a nomination within the appointed time, the 
Registrar may himself make the nomination. 


(3) Where three arbitrators are appointed, the opinion of the majority shall 
prevail. 


(4) If one of the arbitrators fails to attend or refuses to work as an 
arbitrator, the remaining two arbitrators shall proceed with the cases, but in 
case of difference of opinion between them, the Chairman, shall have a casting 
vote. ‘ 


(5) If both the arbitrators nominated by the parties fail to attend or refuse 
to work as such, the remaining arbitrator shall proceed with the case. 


129. Persons qualified to be appointed as arbitrators—The Registrar may 
appoint an arbitrator or arbitrators from— 


(a) officers of any department of the State Government; 
(b) officers, paid staff or members of co-operative societies; 


(c) members, officers or paid staff of the authority constituted under 
section 81; 


(d) members of any local body; or 
(e) Chartered Accountants. 


130. Fee for filing disputes, and payment of fees to arbitrators.—(1) (a) For 
filing a dispute under section 86 the petitioner shall have to pay fees in court- 
fees stamp. 


(b) In monetary disputes, the fee shall be— 
(i) for a claim not exceeding rupees two hundred, two rupees, 


(ii) for a claim above two* hundred rupees, one rupee for every hundred 
rupees or part thereof subject to a maximum of rupees five: 


Provided that in case of a primary agricultural credit societies, primary 
agricultural marketing societies and a central co-operative bank filing disputes 
on behalf of the aforesaid classes of societies, the fee shall be, in monetary 
disputes, two rupees irrespective of the amount of the claim. 


(c) In any dispute other than monetary, the fee shall be rupees ten for 
affairs concerning primary societies other than non-agricultural credit societies, 
and rupees fifty in respect of the affairs of central, apex and primary non- 
agricultural credit societies. 


(2) The arbitrators, not being departmental officers, shall be eligible to get 
fees not exceeding the fee payable in terms of sub-rule (1) and the Registrar 
Shall sanction such fees, where necessary. 


(3) No fee shall be payable to an arbitrators till the dispute is finally settled. 


(4) The Registrar or the Assistant Registrar, as the case may be, shall 
Cause proper account of all receipts and payments under this rule to be 
maintained in a separate register at his office. 


131. Reference of a dispute.—(1) A reference of a dispute to the Registrar 
Shall be made in writing and shall be accompanied by— 


(a) the names and addresses of the parties; 
(b) a statement of the subject-matter of the dispute, and

or by the Registrar, as the case may be.

or the Registrar, as the case may be, reasons for such rejection shall 09 
recorded: 


Provided that no order of rejection shall be made without affording the 
petitioner an opportunity of being heard. 


132. Procedure for disposal of disputes.—({1) In these proceedings, the 
arbitrator, the Board of Arbitrators or the Registrar, as the case may be, shall— 


(a) fix the date, hour and the place of hearing of the dispute, and 
(b) have power to allow representation by agent, guardian or next friend. 


(2) The arbitrator, the board of arbitrators or the Registrar, as the case 
may be, shall issue summons or notices, at least fifteen days before the date 
fixed for the hearing of the dispute, requiring— 


(i) the attendance of the parties concerned and the witnesses, and 


(ii) the production of all relevant books and documents relating to the 
matter in dispute. 


(3) Summons or notices may be served by— 
(i) registered post; or 


(ii) personal service through the secretary or a member of the staff of the 
society or any of the parties to the dispute; or 


(iii) affixing a copy of the summons or notice at the last-known place of 
residence or business of the person concerned, when he refuses to 
sign the acknowledgment or he cannot be traced out even after 
search for a reasonable period. 


(4) Service of summons or notice on the Secretary or the Principal Execu- 
tive Officer, by whatever designation known, shall be regarded as service on 
that society. 


(5) Where the serving officer delivers or tenders a copy of the summons 
personally to the persons summoned or to an agent or other persons on his 
behalf, he shall require the signature of the person to whom the copy is so 


delivered or tendered endorsed on the original summons, as an acknowledgment 
of service. 


(6) The serving officer shall, in all cases in which the summons has been 
served under clauses (ii) and (iii) of sub-rule (3), cause to be endorsed on, or 
annexed to, the original summons a return, stating the time when and_ the 
manner in which, the summons was served, and the name, signature and 
address of the person, if any, identifying the person concerned and witnessing 
the delivery or tender of the summons. 


(7) The sufficiency of proof of service of the summons or notice shall be 
decided by the authority which issued the same. 


(8) In the case of absence of any party to the dispute duly summoned, the 
dispute may be decided ex parte. 


133. Award or decision—({1) The arbitrator shall make a memorandum of 
the statements of the parties who attend and of such witnesses as are examined 
Or cross examined, and upon the evidence so recorded and after considera- 
tion of any documentary evidence produced by either party, shall make an 
award, in accordance with justice, equity and good conscience. He shall 


record his award in writing, sign and date it and shall communicate it ta the 
parties.

134. Withdrawal of a reference by the Registrar—The Registrar may, — 


(a) on the application by any party to an arbitration proceeding pending 
before an arbitrator or arbitrators, or 


@ 
(b) where a Government officer is an arbitrator, in case of resignation, 
transfer, suspension or dismissal of the arbitrator or any of the 
arbitrators,

arbitrator or the Board of Arbitrators appointed and may decide the dispute 
himself by an award in the manner provided in rules 132 and 133 or make 
fresh appointment of arbitrator or arbitrators. 


135. Execution of decision or awards.—(1) In any dispute, the award of 
the arbitrator or of the Registrar shall, upon application, be enforceable by 
any civil court having local jurisdiction in the same manner as a decree of 
such court, as if it were a decree of the court. 


(2) When an award in a monetary dispute has been obtained against a 
society, it shall not be executed except against the assets of the society includ- 
ing amounts due to the society by its members. 


Explanation.—For the purposes of rule 132 to 135, the expression “the 
arbitrator” means the authority which may decide the dispute, whether the 
authority is the Registrar, or an arbitrator or a board of arbitrators. 


136. Disposal of records.—(1) The original records of a dispute proceed- 
ings, after the decision or award has been delivered, shall be kept in such 
place and manner as the Registrar may direct. 


(2) Any document or record tendered by a party may, on application, be 
eee the party after the disposal of appeal, if any, or after the period 
of appeal. 


137. Certified copies—(1) A copy of the decision or award shall, on 
application, be given to a party by the Registrar duly certified by him on 
payment of a fee of forty paise for every foolscap page or part thereof typed 
in double spaces. 


(2) Such copies shall be furnished, within three weeks from the date of 
receipt of the application by the Registrar, who may gee part-time typist- 
copyists for the work, where necessary, on payment of remuneration 201 
exceeding twenty-five paise for cach foolscap page or part thereof, typed in the 
manner as indicated above.

CHAPTER XI 
Winding up and dissolution of co-operative societies 


138. Winding up obligatory on the Registrar—Where the Registrar has 
cause to believe that a co-operative society— 


(i) has not commenced working within a period of twelve months from 
the date of registration; or 


(ii) has not carried on business during the previous eighteen months; 


he shall, after giving the society a notice in such manner as he thinks fit, by 
an order in writing, direct that the society be wound up. 


139. Order for winding up of a co-operative society—When the Registrar 
passes an order under section 89 directing the winding up of a co-operative 
society, he shall— 


(a) publish the order— 


(i) if the liability of the society exceeds ten thousand rupees, in the 
Official Gazette; and 


(ii) in any other case, in such manner in the locality as he may think 
fit; 


(b) communicate the order to the society by registered post, and 


(c) send, by registered post, a copy of the order to the financing bank, if 
any, of which the society is a member. 


140. Appointment and removal of liquidator.—({1) The liquidator shall be 
appointed— 


(a) in case of the societies having annual transactions of rupees five lakhs 
or above, from amongst the Chartered Accountants or the depart- 
mental officers, serving or retired, and 


(b) in any other case, from amongst the departmental officers, serving or 
retired. 


(2) The appointment and removal of a liquidator shall be published— 


(a) if the liability of the society exceeds ten thousand rupees, in the Official 
Gazette; and 


(b) in any ae case, in the locality in such manner as the Registrar may 
think fit. 


141. Remuneration of liquidators.—The liquidator may be allowed such 
remuneration not exceeding two and half per cent. of the assets of the society, 
as the Registrar may decide. Such remuneration may be fixed to cover all 
costs incidental to the liquidation and shall be met out of the assets of the 
society. 


142. Publication of notice.—Immediately after the date on which the order 
directing the winding up of the society takes effect, the liquidator shall publish, 
in such manner as the Registrar may direct, a notice in the form set forth in 
the schedule requiring all claims against the society to be forwarded to him 
within one month of the publication of the notice. 


143. Submission of accounts by the liquidator before the Registrar.— 
(1) The liquidator shall submit to the Registrar an account of the receipts and 
payments, in the form prescribed for cash account for audit, — 


(a) within three months after the close of every co-operative year, 


(b) where an order under section 89 is set aside on appeal, within fifteen 
days from the date of such setting aside and before handing over 
of charge in terms of sub-section (3) of section 99, and 


(c) fifteen days before making a final report to the Registrar in terms of 
sub-section (9) of section 91, when the affairs of the co-operative 
society concerned have been wound up. 


(2) In addition, the liquidator shall also submit to the Registrar such 
accounts, reports and returns, in such form and in such manner, as the 
Registrar may require, from time to time.

144. Meetings of Members and creditors.—The liquidator may at any time 
call meetings of the members, or of the creditors, or joint meetings of the 
members and creditors; and such meetings shall be called, held and conducted 
at such time and place and in such manner as the liquidator thinks fit. 


145. Issue of summons, notice, etc., by a liquidator—({]) The liquidator 
May issue summons to persons whose attendance is required either to give 
evidence or to produce documents. 


(2) The liquidator shall himself arrange for service of summons and shall 
send warrants, if any, for execution to the District or Subdivisional Magistrate 
concerned. 


146. Liquidator to keep notes of deposition.—The liquidator shall keep 
Short notes of the depositions of persons whose evidence he may have taken. 


147. Recovery by certificates.—If the liquidator fails to recover the assets 
of the society ara! and decides to proceed under the Bengal Public Demands 
Recovery Act, 1913, he shall submit to the Collector in the form prescribed 
under the said Act (printed in the Bengal Certificate Manual), a requisition for 
a certificate against each contributor for the amount of his contribution and 
a 08 proceed according to the instructions in the Bengal Certificate 

anual. 


148. Banking Accounts of liquidator —{1) The liquidator shall open an 
account with such bank, as the Registrar may approve, in the name of 016 
''].70 اتن1٥4۹8٤٤٤٣‎ 0185855755555588558 ociety”. 


(2) All moneys received in course of the winding up of the society shall 
be paid into such account at the bank immediately after receipt thereof. 


(3) All payments out of the aforesaid banking account shall be made by 
the liquidator by cheques or withdrawal order signed by him and shall be 
accounted for in the record maintained for the purpose in the office of the 
liquidator. 


149. Distribution of assets—({1) The audit fees due and payable in terms 
of sub-section (7) of section 91, if any, and all costs. charges and expenses 
incurred in the winding up of the society, including the remuneration of the 
liquidator, shall be payable in priority to all other claims. 


(2) After the liabilities other than owned capital as they stood on the date 
of order of winding up are paid off, the assets, if any, left with the liquidator. 
may be employed subject to the approval of the Registrar, for the following 
purposes in the order of priority— 


(i) proportional refund to members of any contributions realised from 
them in addition to their own personal debts; 


(ii) pro-rata refund of share capital; and 


(iii pro-rata payment of dividend on the shares, if any, at a rate not 
exceeding six per cent. per annum for the period of liquidation. 


150. Meetings of members at the conclusion of liquidation proceedings.— 
(1) At the conclusion of the liquidation proceedings the liquidator shall call 
a general meeting of the members at such time and place and in such manner 
as he thinks fit and place before such meeting— 


(1) a summary of his proceedings; 
(ii) a report of the causes of the failure of the socicty. 


(2) The members at such meeting after due consideration of the report 
placed by the liquidator, may by a resolution, request the Registrar to cancel 
ing registration or the order for the winding up of the society, as they think 


If there be a quorum at such meeting and the resolution is carried by three- 
fourths of the members present, it shall be binding upon the Registrar. 


(3) When no general meeting of members can be held, the liquidator shall 
report the fact to the Registrar, and the Registrar may, for reasons to be 


recorded in writing, dispense with the provisions of sub-rule (1) and 
sub-rule (2),

151. Final report of liquidator and termination of proceedings.—(1) After 
the liquidation proceedings of a society have been closed, the liquidator shall 
submit a final report to the Registrar together with a copy of his report and 
the resolution, if any, referred to in rule 150. 


(2) On receipt of the final report from the liquidator, the Registrar shall 
terminate the liquidation proceedings by cancelling either the registration or 
the order for the winding up of the society. 


152. Termination of liquidation proccedings obligatory on Registrar in 
certain cases.—The liquidation proceedings of a society shall be closed within 
a period of two years from the date of the order of winding up: 


Provided that such period can be extended, from time to time, by the 
Registrar, for reasons to be recorded in writing, by an aggregate period of not 
more than three years. 


Explanation.—In the case of a society which is under liquidation at the 
commencement of these rules, the order for the winding up of the society shail 
be deemed to have been passed on the date on which these rules come into 
operation. 


153. Disposal of books, etc., by the liquidator.—Upon the termination of 
liquidation proceedings, all books, registers and accounts belonging to the 
society and all books, accounts and papers relating to the liquidation proceed- 
ings, which are in possession of the liquidator, shall be deposited with the 
Registrar or such person as the Registrar may direct. 


154. The period after which the responsibility of the liquidator, Registrar, 
etc., to cease for custody of documents.—After the expiry of three years from 
the date of the order passed under rule 151, no responsibility shall rest on the 
liquidator, or the Registrar or any person to whom the custody of the docu- 
ments may have been committed, by reason of the same not being forthcoming 
to any person claiming to be interested therein.

three days of its entry in such register, forward such application to un officer 
to be called the public inquiry officer (hereinafter called the officer). 


(2) On receipt of such application, the officer shall, immediately cause 
publication of notice of such application, in such form as may be Set forth in 
the schedule, by beat of drum in the village or villages where the applicant

or the first instalment in respect thereof is to be handed over to the applicant.

or the first instalment in respect thereof, as the case may be, purchase shares

158. Procedure for appointment of distrainer—(1) On receipt of an 
application from a co-operative land development bank, a central co-operative 
bank or a primary co-operative credit society, as the case may be, signed and 
verified by the Secretary and the Manager or any other person duly authorised 
by the Managing Committee in this behalf setting forth full particulars of the 
property required to be distrained, the Registrar shall, if satisfied that the 
particulars set forth in the application are correct, appoint a distrainer: 


Provided that no distrainer shall be appointed unless the applicant deposits 
such security for cost of the distraint and sale, as the Registrar may direct. 


159. Powers and functions of the distrainer.— (1) The distrainer on appoint- 
ment shall serve upon the defaulter a written demand specifying the amount 
for which the distraint is made. The demand shall be dated and signed by 
the distrainer and shail be served on the defaulter by delivering a copy to him 
or some adult male member of his family at his usual place of abode; or when 
such service cannot be effected, by affixing a copy of the demand on some 
conspicuous part of the abode and of his land. 


(2) Simultaneously with the service of notice, the distrainer shall ء6٥‎ 
the property speciled in the application to be attached by affixing an order of 
attachment in the form set forth in the schedule— 


(a) where such produce is a growing crop on the land on which such crop 
has grown; or 


(b) where such produce has been cut or gathered on the thrashing floor 
or place tor treading out grain or the like or fodder stack on or in 
which it is deposited; 


and another copy in a conspicuous manner on the outer door of the premises 
where he resides or works or is known to have last resided, 


(3) Where agricultural produce is attached, the distrainer shall make such 
arrangement for the custody thereof, as he may deem sufficient. 


(4) Subject to such condition as may be imposed by the distrainer, the 
defaulter may tend, cut, gather and store the produce and do any other act 
necessary for maturing or preserving it; if the defaulter fails to do all or any 
of such acts, the distrainer may do all or any of them, either by himself or by 
any person appointed by him in this behalf, and the costs incurred by the 
distrainer shall be recoverable from the defaulter, as if they were included, in, 
or formed part of, the order of attachment; 


(5) Agricultural produce, attached as a growing crop, shall not be deemed 
to have ceased to be under attachment or to require re-attachment, merely 
because it has been severed from the soil. 


(6) Crops, which are perishable and do not admit of being stored, may be 
sold before they are cut, or gathered. 


(7) No distraint shall be made before sunrise and after sunset. 


160. Sale of distrained property.—(l) If within seven days from the date. 
of the service of the demand, the defaulter does not pay the amount for which 
a distraint has been effected, the distrainer may sell, in auction, the distrained 
property or such part thereof in one or more lots as may, in his opinion, be 
necessary to satisfy the demand together with the expenses of the distraint 
and the costs of the sale. 


(2) Before a sale is actually made, the distrainer shall cause proclamation 
of the time and place of the intended sale by beat of drum in the village 
in which the defaulter resides or the produce is kept and 11) such 
other place or places, as the distrainer may consider necessary eto give due 
publicity to the sale: 


Provided that the sale may be made in the nearest bazar or other place of 
public report, if the distrainer is of opinion that a better price is likely to be 
obtained there. 


(3) The sale shall be made to the highest bidder, who shall be required. to 
etd at least fifty per cent. of the purchase money in cash immediately and. the 
alance within a perioc not exceeding five days, and the purchaser shall not 
be permitted to carry away any part of the property until the full amount of 
the purchase money is paid.

ollows:—

distraint, the property attached shall be released. 


161. Investigation of claims, etc.—({l1) Where any written claim is preferred 
by any person other than the defaulter to any right or interest in the distrained 
property, the distrainer may, after being prima facie satisfied with the claim 
refer the claimant to the Registrar and may stay the sale and shall also inform 
the land development bank, the central co-operative bank or the primary co- 
Operative credit societies, as the case may be, of the claim: 


Provided that if the property distrained is of a perishable nature, he shall 
forthwith sell the property in the presence of the claimant and keep in custody 
the sale proceeds. 


(2) The Registrar, on receipt of a claim to 3 distrained property, shall 
forthwith notify the distrainer and also the land development bank, the 
central co-operative bank or the primary co-operative credit society, as the 
case may be, of such claim and may stay the eale. 


(3) The Registrar shall investigate the claim and shall pass such orders as 
he thinks proper, and communicate his orders to the distrainer who shall act 
accordingly: 


Provided that the Registrar may, if he thinks fit, refer the claim to the 
civil court. 


(4) If no application is made to the Registrar within seven days of the 
date of the claim made under sub-rule (1), if any, the distrainer shall, without 
further delay, proceed with the sale. 


162. Private alienation of property after attachment to be void.—When an 
attachment has been made under these rules, any private transfer or delivery 
of the property attached, or of interest therein, and any payment 00 the 
defaulter of any debt or other money contrary to such attachment shall be 
void as against all claims enforceable under attachment. 


163. Appointment of Sale Officer—(l) The Registrar may appoint an 
Officer subordinate to him or any other suitable person to conduct sales o 
property under the provisions of Chapter XII of the Act. 


(2) The appointment of a Sale Officer shall be notified in the area of 
operation of a co-operative land development bank, a central co-operative bank 
or the apex housing society for which he is appointed, in such manner as the 
Registrar may deem proper.:

164. Notice requiring payment from persons interested.—The notice under 
section 103 shall be in the form set forth in the schedule and shall be sent to 
all concerned by registered post with acknowledgment duc. If, however, 
Service by registered letter cannot be effected for any reason, the notice shall 
be delivered by hand taking proper receipt or affixed at the places of residence 
of all concerned. 


165. Procedure for sale of immovable property—{1) An application to a 
Sale Officer for sale of any mortgaged property shall be signed by the secretary 
or the manager of the co-operative land development bank, central co-operative 
bank or apex housing society or any person duly authorised by the managing 
commiitee to do so and shall— 


(a) contain sufficient detdils for the identification of the property, as also 
a copy of the mortgage bond; 


(b) show the names of all persons having interest in the property as laid 
down in section 103; 


(c) contain a report regarding the manner ہ٤٢‎ service of notice under 
section 103; 


(d) specify the amount due for recovery including interest and the 
incurred in the service of the notice, and other contingencies; and 


(e) contain any other particulars which the land development bank, 
central co-operative bank or apex housing society, as the case may 
be, may consider material for the purchases to know in order to 
judge the nature and value of the property. 


(2) On receipt of the application for sale of the mortgaged property the 
Sale Officer shall give notice by registered post to all persons named 11 the 
application that he intends to sell the property after the expiry of thirty days 
from the date of service of such notice unless the amount due (including cost 
to the bank) is paid within that period: 


Provided that if the service of a registered letter cannot be effected on any 
reason, the notice concerned may be affixed in a conspicuous place of his 
residence. 


(3) On the expiry of thirty days from the service of the notice the Sale 
Officer shall proceed to 5611] the property by auction and for that purpose shall 
cause a proclamation of the time and place of the intended sale to be made 
in the language of the district and shall also specify as fairly and accurately 
as possible— 


(a) the property to be sold; 
(b) the annual rent payable for such property, 
(c) the amount for the recovery of which the sale is ordered; and 


(d) any other particulars which the Sale Officer considers material for a 
purchaser to know in order to judge the nature and value of the 
property. 


(4) Every proclamation for the sale of immovable property shall be made 
at some place on or near such property by beat of drum, and a copy of the 
proclamation shall be affixed on a conspicuous part of the office of the land 
development bank, the central co-operative bank or the apex housing society, 
as the case may be. 


(5) The sale shall be made by public auction to the highest bidder. 


(6) The Sale Officer shall have the power to divide a property into lots, if 
he thinks it necessary in the interest of the debtor or the bank or the society. 


(7) Where the property is divided into lots for the purpose of being sold 
99 it shall not be necessary to make a Separate proclamation for each 
ot. 


(8) The sale shall be held in the village or the ward whcre the mortgaged 
property is situate or at the nearest place of public resort, if the Sale Officer 
is of opinion that a better price is likely to be obtained there. 


(9) All costs for the issue of the sale notice and for the proclamation of such 
Sale shall be paid by the land development bank, the central co-operative bank 
or the apex housing society, as the case may be, on a scale fixed by the 
Registrar.

166. Abandonment of sale—(1) Where prior to the actual sale. the 
mortgagor or any person acting on his behalf or any person having interest 
in the mortgaged property tenders payment of the full amount due including 
interest and cost incurred in connection with the sale of the property, the Sale 
Officer shall not proceed with the sale: 


Provided that the sale cannot be abandoned at the instance of the bank 
concerned unless the entire overdue demand is satisfied in full. 


(2) If the Sale Officer considers that the price offered for the property is 
not fair, he may, upon the application of the owner of the property or some 
person authorising to act on his behalf, or the land development bank, central. 
co-operative bank or apex housing society concerned, postpone the sale to 
some other date not later than fifteen days from the date originally fixed, and 
on such date the sale shall be completed unless the price offered is, in the 
opinion of the Sale Officer, grossly inadequate. 


(3) If the price offered is, in the opinion of the Sale Officer, grossly inade- 
quate, the sale shall be postponed to another date, and it shall be sufficient 
roclamation if the time and place of the sale and the nature of the property to 
e sold are announced by beat of drum at some place on or near such property: 


Provided that the Sale Officer shall not postpone the sale more than two 
times on the ground of inadequacy of price: 


Provided further that the Sale Officer shall complete the sale during the 
period of ninety days from the date of receipt of the case. The Registrar may, 
however, extend the date, if considered necessary, by not more than another 
ninety days. 


167. Method of calculating expenses incidental to sale of property.—The 
Sale Officer shall determine in each case the method of calculating the expenses 
incidental to the sale of the property: 


টি that the Registrar may review the case so determined by the Sale 
cer. 


168. Procedure for the receipt, deposit, etc.—({]) On every sale of property, . 


the person declared to be the purchaser shall pay, immediately after such 
declaration, a deposit of twenty-five per cent. on the amount of his purchase 
money to the Sale Officer who shall issue a temporary receipt for such deposit, 
and in default of such deposit, the property shall forthwith be re-sold. 


(2) The balance of purchase money shall be paid by the purchaser to the 
Sale Officer on or before the fifteenth day after the date of sale. 


(3) On payment of the balance of the purchase money, the Sale Officer 
shall grant a final receipt for the entire sale price. 


(4) All money received by the Sale Officer on the sale of mortgaged 
property shall, as soon as possible after the receipt, be deposited in the ০০- 
operative land development bank, the central co-operative bank or the apex 
housing society, as the case may be. 


169. Procedure in default of payment of full amount of purchase money.— 
(1) If the balance of the purchase money, referred to in sub-rule (2) of rule 168, 
is not paid within the specified period, the deposit shall be forfeited to the 
bank or the society, and the property shall be re-sold. 


(2) The defaulting purchaser shall forfeit all claims to the property or to 


7 7 of the deposit of the sum for which the property may subsequently 
e sold. 


(3) Every re-sale, in default of payment of the purchase money within the 
period allowed for such payment, shall be made after 1015 issue of a fresh 
proclamation and in the manner hereinbefore prescribed for the sale. 


(4) Any deficiency of price which may ensue from a re-sale by reason of 
the purchaser’s default and all expenses attending such re-sale shall be 
certified by the Sale Officer, and shall be met out of the forfeited deposit 
referred to in sub-rule (1). The amount, which cannot be so met, shall be 


recoverable from the defaulting purchaser, on application before a civil court 
having jurisdiction: 


_Provided that no such application shall be entertained unless made within 
thirty. days of the date of re-sale.

be due to him.‏ 


(2) In the event oi a dispute regarding the claim to the purchase money 
and compensation, the bank or the society concerned shall withhold payment 
and refer the disputants to the proper court for adjudication of their claim. 


(3) The purchase money and compensation shall remain with the bank or 
the society concerned till the dispute is decided by a court. 


172. Form and method of submission of a report.—The report to the 


Registrar under sub-section (1) of section 106 shall contain the following 
particulars:— 


(1) Name of Sale Officer. 

(2) Date of sale. 

(3) Place of sale. 

(4) Description of property sold. 
(5) Name of purchaser and address. 
(6) Value realised. 


(7) Amount of claim of the bank including interest. 
(8) Cost of sale. 


(9) Application, if any, under section 105 and manner of disposal of such 
application. 


173. Form of notice to be served on landlord by purchaser shall be in the 
form annexed in the schedule—({1) The Registrar shall grant a sale certificate 
to the purchaser in the form set forth in the schedule. 


(2) A purchaser of any mortgaged property shall supply to the Registrar 
a notice, in the form set forth in the schedule, for service on the State of West 
Bengal through the Collector of the district concerned. 


(3) The purchaser shall pay a fee of two rupees for service of notice 
referred to in sub-rule (2). 


(4) The notice shall be served on the State of West Bengal through the 
Collector of the district concerned, as the case may ০৩, . 


174. Delivery of possession by Registrar to purchaser—(1) Where the 
mortgaged property sold is in the occupancy of the mortgagor or of some 
person on his behalf or of some person claiming under a title created by the 
mortgagor subsequent to the mortgage in favour of tha land development bank, 
the central bank or the apex housing society and a certificate in respect thereof 
has been granted under section 108, the Registrar shall, on the application of 
the purchaser, order delivery to be made by putting such purchaser, or any 


person whom he may appoint to receive delivery on his behalf, in possession 
of the property. 


(2) Where the property sold is in the occupancy of a tenant or other person 
entitled to occupy the same and a certificate in respect thereof has been 
granted under section 108, the Registrar shall, on the application of the 
purchaser, and after notice to such tenant or other person, order delivery to 
be made by affixing a copy of the certificate of sale in some conspicuous place 
on the property and proclaiming to the occupant by beat of drum at some 


convenient place that the interest of the mortgagor has been transferred to the 
purchaser.

(3) In regard to the cases dealt with in sub-rules (1) and (2), the provisions 
of rules 97 to 103 of Order XXI of the First Schedule to the Code of Civil 
Procedure, 1907, shall, mutatis mutandis and so far as may be, apply. 


175, Procedure for the disposal of property purchased by land development 
bank.—_({1) Unless otherwise directed by the trustee, a purchasing bank or 
society concerned shall dispose of the property, purchased by it, by public 
auction, on a specified date not later than one year from the date of purchase. 


(2) The sale shall be previously advertised by— 

(a) advertising the property with full details in the local newspaper; 
(b) proclamation by beat of drum in the village where it is situate; and 
(c) publication of the sale notice in the office of— 


(i) Junior Land Reforms Officer concerned, 
(ii) the Collector of the district, and 
(iii) the Gram Sabha in the area in which the property is situate. 


176. Appointment of receiver and his duties, powers, functions and remu- 
neration.—(1) On an application by a land development bank, a central co- 
operative bank or the apex housing society, the Registrar may, by an order in 
writing, appoint a receiver. The receiver so appointed shall be entitled either 
to take possession of the property or collect its produce and income as_ the 
case may be, to retain, out of the money realised by him, his expenses of 
management including his remuneration, if any, as may be fixed by the Registrar 
in consultation with the bank or the society, and to apply the balance in 
accordance with the provisions of sub-section (8) of section 69A of the Transfer 
of Property Act, 1882. 


(2) The receiver shall open an account with such bank as the Registrar 
may approve. 


(3) All moneys received shall be paid immediately into such account. 
(4) The receiver shall duly— 


(a) account for all sums of money which he may receive in respect of 
the property; and 


(b) submit his accounts at the end of every month to the land develop- 
ment bank, the central co-operative bank or the apex housing 


society and at the same time forward a copy thereof to the 
Registrar. 


(5) A receiver appointed under this rule may, for just and sufficient cause 
or on application made by the co-operative land development bank, the central 
co-operative bank or the apex housing society, be removed by the Registrar. 


(6) A vacancy in the office of the receiver may be filled up by the Registrar. 


177. Procedure, if value of property renfered insufficient—(l1) When a 
member fails to give further security required by a land development bank, a 
central co-operative bank or the apex housing society, as the case may be, 
unde: section 114, the bank or the society may, and if directed by the Registrar 
shall, proceed to take action for the recovery of the loan outstandjng in the 
manner provided in Chapter XII of the Act and the rules framed thereunder. 


(2) A security shall be deemed to be insufficient, if the value of the residue 
of the property does not exceed the loan outstanding by one-third of such 
loan or by such other greater proportion, as may be provided in the bye-laws 
of the bank or the society, as the case may be. 


178. Action to be taken, if bank fails to proceed under section 99 or 10] 
or 114.—If on a report of the Registrar or any officer authorised to inspect 
such banks it appears to the trustee of the central land development bank 
that a land development bank has neglected or failed to take action against a 
mortgagor under secticn 99, 101 or 114, as the case may be, the trustce of 
the central land development bank shall be entitled, after giving both the 
mortgagor and the land development bank an opportunity to file any objection, 
to teke action against the mortgagor for the recovery of the loan.

179. Fees payable to Collector for notifying encumbrances.—(1) The fee 
payable to the Collector under clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 117 shall 
not exceed half per cent. of the value of the notified property, subject to a 
maximum of two rupees. 


(2) The fee shall be accompanied by a statement containing material 
particulars in respect of the mortgage deed executed in favour of the bank. or 
the society, as the case may be. 


CHAPTER ۱1 
Enforcement of obligations and recovery of sums due 


180. Restriction on issue of warrants—No warrant for enforcing attend- 
ance of witnesses shall be issued, without the previous sanction of the 
Registrar, by an audit officer, an arbitrator, a liquidator or any other person 
conducting an enquiry or inspection under Chapter IX of the Act. 


181. Procedure for conditional attachment of property—(1) An applica- 
tion to the Registrar for a conditional order of attachment shall contain— 


(a) full details of the property to be attached, its estimated value and the 
claim of the society; and 


(b) evidence in support of the contention that the person or the co-opera- 
tive society concerned is about to remove or dispose of the 
property. 


(2) Order of attachment, if any, passed by the Registrar shall be served by 
such person as the Registrar may empower. The person so empowered shall 
follow, as far as possible, the procedure laid down in Order XXI of the First 
Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. 


182. Power under section 126.—District Auditor of Co-operative Societies 
and Co-operative Development Officers may exercise the power under 
Section 126, when the claim does not exceed Rs. 2,000, and Inspectors of 


Co-operative Societies may exercise the said power, when the claim does not 
exceed Rs. 1,000. 


183. Procedure of disposal of proceedings drawn up by the Registrar 
under section 127.—(1) When the Registrar holds an enquiry under section 127, 
he shall draw up proceedings against the officer concerned, showing the 
charges against him and shall— 


(i) supply the officer concerned with a copy of the proceedings and a 
summary of the evidence which, prima facie, appears; 


(ii) call on the officer to furnish his explanation within a fortnight; 
(iii) receive and record such evidence as may be adduced; and 


(iv) record a decision as early as possible but not later than three months 
from the date of drawing up proceedings. 
e, 


184. Culpable negligence.—Negligence in the following matters shall be 
deemed culpable within the meaning of clause (b) of sub-section (1) of 
Section 127, namely— 


(i) investment, custody and employment of funds [and use or disposal 
of stores or other assets or properties] contrary to the provisions 
of the Act, rules or bye-laws or any written direction of the 
Registrar given in accordance therewith; 


(ii) failure to remedy audit defects and irregularities, when directed by 
the Registrar under section 80; and 


(iii) failure to fil disputes against defaulters and to execute any decree 
or award within the period of limitation. 


185. Penalty for certain misdemeanour under section 128.—If no cause is 
shown within a specified time or the cause shown is not considered satisfac- 


tory, the Registrar may order a penalty for every contravention referred to 
in— 


(i) clauses (a) and (b) of section 128—a sum not exceeding fifty rupees; 


Part I] 


۰ 


THE CALCUITA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, JANUARY 30, 1974 


ete সি 


(ii) clauses (c) and (d) of section 128—a sum not exceeding one-half of 
the amount of the loan (in addition to enforcing immediate repay- 
ment of the entire loan to the society or the financing bank 
concerned). 


186. Officer responsible for carrying out the direction of Registrar.—(1) 
In deciding under section 129 which officer is to be held responsible for the 
carrying out of his directions, the Registrar shall always consider the secretary 
or the Chief Executive Officer of the society, by whatever designation he may 
be called, to be responsible unless there is anything in the bye-laws, or in any 
resolution of the general meeting or the managing committee by which a 
particular duty is entrusted to any officer other than the secretary or the 
Chief Executive Officer. 


(2) In accordance with sub-rule (1), the Registrar may call on such person, 
as he may hold responsible, to carry out any of his directions within such time 
as he may specify, and on his failure, may take action against him under 
Section 129. 


CHAPTER XIV 
Jurisdiction, Appeal and Revision 


187. Co-operative Tribunal.—(1) The co-operative tribunal, referred to 
in section 133, shall consist of not more than three members of whom there 
shall be a President, when such tribunal shall consist of more than one 
member; and the President shall be either a serving or retired High Court 
judge or a serving or retired member of the West Bengal Higher Judicial 

ervice. 


(2) A person shall not be qualified for appointment as a member of the 
co-operative tribunal unless— 


(a) he : a serving or retired member of the West Bengal Higher Judicial 
ervice, 


(b) he has served as Registrar of Co-operative Societies or Additional 
Registrar of Co-operative Societies in any State, or 


(c) for at least ten years he has been a practising lawyer in any court in 
West Bengal, and since the last five years actively associated with 
the co-operative movement in the State. 


188. Court-fee stamp necessary on application for reference or appcal.— 
An application for reference or a memo of appeal to the prescribed authority, 
Other than the co-operative tribunal referred to in section 133, shall bear a 
court-fee stamp of two rupees: 


Provided that no such court-fee stamp shall be necessary in the case of an 
appeal preferred against the decision of a society under section 59 refusing to 
admit as member any person applying for membership. 


CHAPTER XV 
Offences, 1৯611910165 and Procedure 


189. Certified copics of entries in books.—A copy of any entry in a book 
of a co-operative society may be certified by a declaration written at the foot 
of such copy that it is a true copy of such entry, that such entry is contained 
in one of the ordinary books of the society (to be named) and was made in 
the usual and ordinary course of business, and that such book is still in the 
custody of the society; such certificate shall be dated and_ signed by the 
Secretary, Chairman, the Executive Officer or the Chief Executive Officer of 
the society by whatever designation he may be called. 


190, Procedure and condition for obtaining copies of documents.— 
Certified or uncertified copies of any document which a member of the public 
has a right to inspect under the Act, the rules or the bye-laws of a co-opera- 
tive society or which a member of such society may require shall, on 
application, be supplied, within a month, from the date of such application on 
payment of a sum calculated at twenty-five paise for each hundred words or 
a part thereof.

191. Fees for inspection of public documents filed in the office of the 
Registrar.—({1) Any member of the public may, on payment of a fee of one 
rupee for cach occasion of inspection, with the permission of the Registrar, 
inspect, for any lawful purpose, any public documents (exclusive of documents 
privileged under sections 123, 124, 129 and 131 of the Indian Evidence Act, 
1872), filed in the office of the Registrar and, in particular, the following 
documents namely:— 


(a) certificate of registration of a co-operative society; 


(b) bye-laws of a co-operative society and amendment effected in such 
byc-laws; 


(c) order directing the ‘winding up of a co-operative society; 
(d) order cancelling the registration of a co-operative society; 
(e) annual returns; 

(f) register of co-operative societies. 


(2) Certified copies of any document which any person has a right under 
sub-rule (1) to inspect shall be supplied within three weeks from the date of 
application for the same, on payment of— 


(i) three rupees for certificate of registration; and 


(ii) a sum calculated at the rate of forty paise for each hundred words or 
a part thereof of the copy or extract of any other document. 


192, Payment ‘of ‘fees.—(1) Untess the State Government otherwise 
directs, all feces, payable to it under the Act or the rules except audit fees, 
Shall be paid in court-fee stamps. 


(2) Dues and fees payable to a co-operative society shall be paid in cash, 
by cheque or by bank draft under proper receipt. 


‘CHAPTER XVI 


Miscellaneous 


193. Penalty.—Any person committing a breach of any of the rules of the 
West Bengal Co-eperative Societies Rules, 1974, shall, at the instance of the 
Registrar of any co-operative society with the approval of the Registrar, on 
conviction by a Magistrate having jurisdiction over the place where such 
Person resides, be punishable with fime which may extend to five hundred 
rupees, and where the breach is a continuing one, with further fine which ma 
extend to ten rupees for every day after the first during which the breac 
continues subsequent to such conviction.

the bye-laws of the bank to make loans for all or any of the purposes specified in 
rule 156, granting either before or after the commencement of the West Benga! 
Co-operative Societies Act, 1973, a loan to the person mentioned therein with his 
eonsent, for the purpose of carrying out the work specified therein, for the benefit 
of the land or for the productive purpose mentioned therein, shall, for purpose® 
of the said Act, be conclusive of the following matters, that is to say— 


(a) that the work described or the purpose for which the loan is granted, is 
an improvement or productive purpose, as the case may be, within the 
meaning of rule 156 ; 


(b) that the person had at the date of the order a right to make such improve. 
ment or incur expenditure for productive purpose, as the case may be, 
and 


(c) that the improvement is one benefiting the land specified and the productive 
purpose concerns the land offered in security, or any part thereof us 
may be relevant.

at issue will be decided in their absence and such persons will have no claim what- 
goever against the property for which the loan applied for, and sanctioned, till 
such time as the loans together with interest thereon or any other dues arising out 
of the loan are paid in full by the loanee.

NOTIFICATION 
No. 155-Mines 
Calcutta, the 30th January, 1974 


Im exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 15 of 
the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957 (Act 67 
of 1957), the Governor 18 pleased hereby to make the following rules 
regulating the grant of quarry leases, mining leases and other mineral 
concessions in respect of minor minerals and for purposea connected there- 
with, namely: 

CHAPTER I 


CGoneral 


1. Short title and commencement: (i) These rules may 09 called the 
West Bengal Minor Minerals Kules, 1973. 


(ii) They shall extend to the whole of West Bengal. 


(iti) They shall come into force with effect from the date of publication 
in the Calcutta Gazette. 


9. Limitation of application of rules: Nothing in these rules shall 
affect the provisions of any Centrg] Act, or regulations or rules made there- 
under, for the purpose of regulation and development of mines and minerals 
and of the safety of the persons working in the mines, or anything done 
or any action taken under the provisions of the West Bengal Minor Mineral 
Rules, 1959.

9, Priority: (1) If more than one application for a mining lease 
regarding the same land is received, preference shall ordinarily be given 
to the application received first, unless the State Government, for ony 
veazons to be recorded in writing, decides to grant a mining lease to an 
applicant, whose application was reccived later in preference to an applicant

(2) No applicant shall claim any priority by virtue only of the fact 
that he had previously worked in the area under application, 


10. Area of Mining Lease: (1) No persun shall acquire in the State 
one or more mining leases covering a total area in excess of 3 sq. kilometers. 


Explanation: Yor the purpose of this rule a person acquiring, by or 
in the name of another person or with any person jointly in interest with 
him, a mining lease, which is intended wholly or partly for himself, shall 
be deemed to be acquiring the whole of it himself: 


Provided that if the State Government is of opinion that in the interest 
of mineral development it is necessary so to do, it may for reasons to be 
recorded in writing, permit any person to acquire one or more mining leases 
in excess of the aforesaid maximum: 


Provided further that this restriction shall not apply to the West Bengal 
Mineral Development and Trading Corporation Limited. 


(2) The length of an area held under a mining lease shall not ordinarily 
exceed four timeg its breadth and the area shall as far as possible be 
compact and regular in shape.

12, Renowal of Mining Lease: (1) An application for renewal of a

calendar months before the date, on which the lease is due to expire, through

or part of the area covered by the original lease for which renewal is 
prayed for,

(3) An application for renewal of mining lease shall be disposed of 
within nine months from the date of its receipt.

of the lease, the period of that 16846 shall be deemed to have been extended 
for 0 further period of six months or ending with the date of receipt of 
orders of the State Government thereon, whichever is shorter.

14. Security Deposit: (1) The applicant shall deposit before execution 
of the mining lease as security for the due observance of the terms and 
conditions of the lease a sum of Rs.1,000 in the manner os may he 
directed by the State Government, which shall be refundable to him after 
the expiry of the period of the lease, unless the whole or o part of it is

Government. 


(2) No interest shall run on the security deposit. 


15. Lease to be executed within six months: When an order has beer 
made for the grant of a mining lease, the deed of lease shall be executed 
within six months from the date of the order granting the lease and if no 
such lease is executed within the aforesaid period, the order sanctioning 
the lease shall be deemed to have been revoked: 


Provided that the State Government, if it is satisfied that the applicant 
18 not responsible for the delay in the execution of deed of lease, may 
permit the execution of the deed of lease after the expiry of the aforesaid 
period of six months. 


16. Survey of the area leased: When a mining lense is granted, 
arrangement may be made at the expense of the lessee, for survey and 
demarcation of the area granted under the lease. 


17. Transfer of Lease: (1) The lessee shal! not, without the previous 
consent in writing of the State Government— 


(a) assign, mortgage, or in any other manner, transfer the mining 
lease, or any right, title or interest therein, or 


(b) enter into or make any arrangement, contract or understanding, 
whereby the lessee will or may be directly or indirectly financed 
to a substantial extent by, or under which the lessee’s operations 
or undertakings will or may be substantially controlled by, any 
person or body of persons other than the lessee: 


Provided that the State Government shall not give its written consent 
unless : 


(a) the lessee has furnished an affidavit along with his application for 
transfer of the mining lease specifying therein the amount that 
he has already taken or proposes to take as consideration from 
the transferee ;

clauses (a) and (b) of sub-rule (1) shall apply to the holder of a mining 
lease granted before such commencement.

CHAPTER IV 


27. Application of these rules to all renewals: Where a mining lease 
vranted before the commencement of these rules is renewed after the 
promulgation of these rules, these rules shall apply automatically to such 
renewal. 


28. Power to rectify apparent mistakes: (1) Nothing in these rules 
shall be deemed to limit or otherwise affect the inherent power of the State 
Government to rectify any clerical, arithmetical, accidental and similar 
other types of errors in any order passed by it or to direct the rectification 
of any such error in any instrument to which the State Government is a 
party: 


Provided that no such order which affects the lessee or {he applicant 
for lease shall be passed without giving such lessee or applicant an 
opportunity of being heard. 


(2) When an order has been passed under sub-rule (1) for rectification 
of an instrument, the lessee shall execute the deed of rectification within 
six months from the date of communication of the order to him. 


(3) If no deed of rectification is executed by the lessee within time- 
limit prescribed by sub-rule (2), the State Government shall have the 
liberty to determine the lease after giving the lessee three months’ notice.

29. Change in individual Constituting partnership firm, etc.: (1) A 
partnership firm, a company, which ig a private company as defined in the 
Indiun Companies Act, 1956 (I of 1956), or an association or body of 
individuals, whether incorporated or not, shall intimate promptly to the 
State Government or to an officer appointed for the purpose by the State 
Government any change that may take place in the individuals constituting 
such partnership firm, company, association or body or in ‘their addresses. 


(2) In case of contravention of the provisions contained in sub-rule (1), 
a port or whole of the security deposit deposited in connection with any 
lease or leases held by ‘the said firm, company, association or body may be 
forfeited by the State Government or by such officer. 


30. Penalty: Any person extracting any minor mineral without a 
proper lease or licence granted under these rules or in contravention of the 
provision of rule 31 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which 
may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand 
rupees or with both. 


ol. Extraction of minéral from own land: No lease will be required 
to be taken by a person, who extracts any minor mineral from his own land, 
either for use in any cottage industry owned by him, viz., pottery, clay 
modelling, etc., or any other industry specified in a notification issued by 
the State Government or for his personal use for any other purpose, 
provided that such extraction shall be subject to the following conditions 
and also to such further conditions, as the State Government may impose 
by any general or special order from time to time:— 


(a) The mineral so extracted shall not be disposed of by sale or other- 
wise without the prior permission in writing of the District 
Magistrate or Additional District Magistrate (Estate Acquisi- 
tion), or Deputy Commissioner or Additional Deputy 
Commissioner of the district, or Subdivisional Officer or 
Subdivisional Land Reforms Officer of the subdivision and 
except on payment of fees at the rate of 40 paise per cubic metre 
or at such reduced rate as may be fixed by the officer concerned. 


(b) The mineral so extracted shall not be converted into bricks or tiles, 
except where such bricks and tiles are required for his own use. 


(c) No extraction shall be done at or from a place within 45 metres 
from any railway line, except with the previous written 
permission of the railway administration concerned, or from any 
reservoir, public road, canal or other public works or buildings 
or inhabitated site, except with the previous written permission 
of the District Magistrate or Additional District Magistrate 
(Ketate Acquisition) or Deputy Commissioner or Additional 
Deputy Commissioner of the district or 90151810178] Officer or 
Subdivisional Iand Reforma Officer of the subdivision.

33. Refund: If an, application for the grant or renewal of a mining 
18989 is refused to be granted or is deemed to huve been refused under 
rule 7 or 1f 6119 applicant refuses to accept the lease on account of any 
special condition imposed therein under swb-rule (3) of rule 19, the 
application fees deposited under sub-rule (2) of rule 6 and sub-rule (2) of 
rule 12, وہ‎ the case may be, shall La refunded: 


— —— 


Provided that where an application for grant of lease or grant of renewal 
of lease is refused on account of any lapses on the part of the applicant, 
the fees paid by the applicant shall be forfeited to the State Government. 


33. Appeal: (1) Any person aggrieved by an order made by the 
District Authority or by any officer duly authorised by the District Authority 
in exercise of the powers conferred upon him by these rules, may, wifhin 
thirty days from the date of communication of the order to him, prefer on 
aypeal against the order. 


(2) The memorandum. of appeal shall be made to the State Government, 
if the order appealed ugainst has been passed by the District Authority, 
and to the District Authority, if the order appealed against has been passed 
by any officer subordinate to the District Authority. 


(3) Each memorandum of appeal shall be accompanied by a Trensury 
Challan showing the deposit of a fee of Rs.20 in the same manner as 
prescribed in sub-rule (3) of rule 5 in any Government Treasury or Sub- 
Treasury of the district concerned or in any branch of the State Bank of 
India or in the Reserve Bank doing treasury business to the credit of the 
State Government under the head of Account: ‘SX X XII—Miscellaneous— 
Provincial—Social and Developmental Organisation.’’ 


(4) An appeal for revision may be entertained even after the said perjod 
specified in sub-rule (1), if the appellant satisfies the appellate authority 
that he had sufficient reasons for not preferring the appeal within the 
prescribed period. 


(5) The order passed on appeal shall be final and there shall be no se:ond 
appeal. 


Explanation: For the purpose of this rule, when the District Authority 
or the officers authorised for the purpose have failed to dispese of an 
application for the grant of quarry permit within the period specified in 
respect thereof in these rules, the District Authority or the officer authorized 
shall be deemed to have made an order refusing the grant of such permit 
on the date on which such period expires.

34. Roview: The State Government may, vn application from an 
aggrieved party, within thirty days from the date of communication, or on 
86৪ own motion, withm six months from the date of passing, of an order, 
review the order on the ground of discovery of ٥۸ new and important matter 
not known to it when the order wag passed or on any other grotnd considered 
expedient for mineral development. 


36. Premature applications: (a) Any application for long-term lease 
in respect of any area, where a lease is subsisting, shall be premature 
and shall not be considered by the State Government unless tle application 
has teen made within three months before the expiry of the subsisting lease. 


(b) Any application for mining ‘lense in respect of any area, which bas 
een notified by the State Government as reserved for exploitation in the 
public sector or for the Wert Bengal Mineral Development and Trading 


Corporation Limited, under rule 36, shall be premature and shall not be 
considered. 


36. Reservation of areas for exploitation in the public sector: The 
‘State Government may, by notification in Official Gazette, reserve any area 
or areas in West Bengal for exploitation in the public sector or for the West 
Bengal Mineral Development and Trading Corporation Limited, and on 
such notification no application for any mining lease in the area shall be 
granted to ay person other than a State Government Department or 
body corporate owned or controlled by the State Government. 


37, Relaxation of rules: If the State Government is of opinion that 
public interest so reqitires, ij may relax any of the provisions of these rules 
in any particular case and may grant ھ‎ mining lease or authorise the grant 


of mining lease or quarry permit on terms and conditions other than those 
prescribed under these rules, 


38. Repeal and savings: (1) The West Bengal Minor Minerals Rules, 
1959, are hereby repealed. 


(2) Notwithstanding such repeal anything done, any action taken, any 
application made or any prosecution started under the said rules shall be 
deemed to have been done, taken, made or started, as the case may be, 
ander the corresponding provisions of these rules.

Procedure for issue of quarry permits for removal of minor minerals 
under rule 24 of West Bengal Minor Minerals Rules, 1973 


}, The quarry permits should be issued by the District Authority or 
-y Officers authorised by him in this behalf, hereinafter referred to as the 
Issuing Authority.

the reasons for the refusal shall be communicated to the applicant.
