92. Penalty for misconduct ai polling stations.—(1) Any person who during 
the hours fixed for the poll at any polling station misconducts himself or fails 
to obcy the lawful direction of the Presiding Officer may be removed from the 
polling station by the Presiding Officer or by any police officer on duty or by 
any person, authorised in this behalf by such Presiding Officer. 


(2) The powers conferred by sub-rule (1) shall not be exercised so as to 
prevent any voter who is otherwise entitled to vote at a polling station from 
having an opportunity of voting at that station. 


(3) If any person who has been so removed from a polling station re-enters 
the polling station without the permission of the Presiding Officer, he shall, on 
conviction, be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty 
rupees. 


(4) An offence punishable under sub-rule (3) shall be cognizable. 


93. Officers, etc., at election not to act for candidates or influence voting.— 
(1) No person who is a Returning Officer, or an Assistant Returning Officer 
or a Presiding Officer or polling officer at an election or an officer or clerk 
appointed by the Returning Officer or the Presiding Officer to perform any duty 
in connection with an election shall, in the conduct or the management of the 
election, do any act (other than the giving of his vote) for the furtherance of 


‘the prospects of the election of a candidate. 


(2) No such person as aforesaid, and no member or a police force, shall 
endeavour— 


(a) to persuade any person to give his vote at an election, or 
(b) to dissuade any person from giving his vote at an election, or 
(c) to influence the voting of any person at an election in any manner. 


(3) Any person who contravenes the provisions of sub-rule (1) or sub-rule (2) 
shall, on conviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may 
extend to six months or with fine which may extend to rupees five hundred or 
with both. 


(4) An offence under sub-rule (3) shall be cognizable. 


94. Breaches of official duty in connection with election.—(1) If any person. 
to whom this rule applies is without reasonable cause guilty of any act or 
omission in breach of his official duty, he shall, on conviction, be punished with 
fine which may extend to five hundred rupees. 


(2) An offence punishable under sub-rule (1) shall be cognizable. 


(3) No suit or other legal proceedings shall lie against any such person for 
damages in respect of any such act or omission as aforesaid. 


(4) The persons to whom this rule applies are the Returning Officers, Assistant 
Returning Officers, Presiding Officers, polling officers and any other persons 
appointed to perform any duty in connection with the maintenance of list of 
voters, the reccipt of nominations or withdrawal of candidatures, or the recording 
or counting of votes at an election and the expression “official duty” shall, for 
the purposes of this rule, be construed accordingly, but shall not include duties 
imposed otherwise than by or under this Act. 


95. Penalty for Government servants for acting as election agent, polling 
agent or counting agent.—If any person in the service of the Government acts 
as an election agent or a polling agent or a counting agent of a_ candidate 
at an election, he shall, on conviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term 
which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to five hundred 
rupees. 


96. Removal of ballot paper from polling station to be offences.—(1) Any 
person who at any election fraudulently takes, or attempts to take a ballot 
paper out of a polling station or wilfully aids or abets the doing of any such 
act, shall, on conviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may 
extend to one year or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or 
with both.

(2) If the Presiding Officer of a polling station has reason to believe that 
any person is committing or has committed an offence punishable under sub- 
rule (1), such officer may, before such person leaves the polling station, arrest 
or direct a police officer to arrest such person and may search such person or 
cause him to be searched by a police officer : 


Provided that when it is necessary to cause a woman to be searched the 
search shall be made by another woman with strict regard to decency. 


(3) Any ballot paper found upon the person arrested on search shall be made 
over for safe custody to a police officer by the Presiding Officer, or when the 
search is made by a Police Officer, shall be kept by such officer in safe custody. 


(4) An offence punishable undcr sub-rule (1) shall be cognizable. 


97. Other offences and penalties therefor.—(1) A person shall be guilty 
of an electoral offence if at any election he— 


(a) fraudulently defaces or fraudulently destroys any nomination paper; or 


(b) fraudulently defaces, destroys or removes any list, notice or other 
document affixed by or under the authority of a Returning Officer; 
or 


(c) fraudulently defaces or fraudulently destroys any ballot paper or the 


Official mark on any ballot paper; or any official envelope used in 
connection with voting by voters on election duty; or 


{d) without due authority supplies any ballot paper to any person or 
receives any ballot paper from any person or is in possession of 
any ballot paper; or 

(e) fraudulently puts into ballot box anything other than the ballot paper 
which he is authorised by law to put in; or 


(f) without due authority destroys, takes, opens or otherwise interferes with 
any bollot box or ballot papers then in use for the purposes of the 
election; or 


(g) fraudulently or without due authority, as the case may be, attempts 
to do any of the foregoing acts or wilfully aids or abets the doing 
of any such acts. 


(2) Any person gyilty of an offence under this rule, shall— 


(a) if he is a Returning Officer, an Assistant Returning Officer or a Presiding 
Officer at a polling station or any other officer or clerk employed 
on official duty in connection with the election, on conviction, be 
punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one 
year or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or with 
both. 


(b) if he is any other person, on conviction, be punished with imprisonment 
for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may 
extend to two hundred and fifty rupees or with both. 


(3) For the purposes of this rule a person shall be deemed to be on official 
duty if his duty is to take part in the conduct of an election or part of an 
election including the counting of votes or to be responsible after an election 
for the used ballot papers and other documents in connection with such election, 
but the expression “official duty” shall not include any duty imposed otherwise 
than by or under these rules. 


(4) An offence punishable under sub-rule (2) shall be cognizable. 


98. Maintenance of secrecy of voting.—(1) Every officer, clerk, agent or 
other person who performs any duty in connection with the recording or count- 
ing of votes at an election shall maintain, and aid in maintaining, the secrecy 
of voting and shall not (except for some purpose authorised by or under any 
law) communicate to any person any information calculated to violate such 
secrecy. 


(2) Any person who contravenes the provisions of sub-rule (1) shall, on 
conviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three 
months or with fine which may extend to rupees five hundred or with both.

Supplement—Offficial Papers 
BOARD OF SECONDARY EDUCATION, WEST BENGAL 


NOTIFICATION 
The 7th February 1974 


The following regulations made by the West Bengal Board of Secondary 
Education under sub-section (3) of section 27 read with sub-section (3) of 
section 25 of the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education Act, 1963 (West 
Ben. Act V of 1963), which the Governor has been pleased to approve of, 
after having made therein certain additions, alterations and modifications after 
considering the views expressed by the- West Bengal Board of Secondary Educa- 
tion under sub-scction (4) of section 27 of the said Act, are hereby published 
85 و وک‎ by sub-section (5) of that section, namely : 


REGULATIONS 


1. Short title and commencement.—(1) These regulations may be called the 
West Bengal Board of Secondary Education (Regional Examination Councils) 
Regulations, 1973. 

(2) They shall be deemed to have come into force on the Ist day of 
September 1973. 


2. Definitions.—In these regulations, unless there is anything repugnant in 
the subject or context,— 

(a) “the Act” means the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education Act, 
1963 (West Ben. Act V of 1963); 

(b) “Board” means the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education 
established under the Act; 

(c) “centre” means an examination centre for holding examinations of such 
candidates enrolled for any examination of the Board as may be 
allotted to it; 

(d) “Examination” means School Final Examination, Higher Secondary 
Examination, examination in a single subject or Compartmental 
Examination or Supplementary Higher Secondary Examination or 
Supplementary School] Final Examination, or any other examinations, 
conducted by the Board; 

(6) “Examinations Committee” means a committee constituted by the Board 
under section 18 of the Act; 

(f) “President” means the President of the Board; 


(g) “‘Secrctary” means the Secretary of the Board. 


203 


204 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, FE RUARY 8, 4 


SSS এ 


হস 


3. The number, composition and territorial jurisdiction.—(1) There shall be 
four Regional Examination Councils, one each for the following regions, namely : 


(i) Calcutta, 

(ii) Burdwan, 

(iii) Midnapore, and 
(iv) North Bengal. 


(2) Each Regional Examination Council shall consist of the following 
members, namely : 
(i) The President—Ex-oflicio; 
(ii) The Secretary—Ex-officio; 
(iii) The Director of Public Instruction, West Bengal or his nominee 
(Ex-officio); 
(iv) Three members of the Board to be elected by the Board in a meeting; 
(v) Three members to be nominated by the President of the Board from 
amongst educationists; 
(vi) Three persons to be nominated by the State Government. 


(3) The Regional Examination Councils mentioned in sub-regulation (1) shall, 
respectively, comprise of the following districts, namely : 

(1) Calcutta: The districts of Calcutta, 24-Parganas, Murshidabad, Nadia, 
Howrah and Serampore subdivision of the district of Hooghly; 

(2) Midnapore: The district of 11101100010) 

(3) Burdwan: The districts of Burdwan, Bankura, Birbhum, Purulia and 
Hooghly minus Serampore subdivision; 

(4) North Bengal: The districts of Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri, Cooch Behar, 
West Dinajpore and Malda. 


4. Terms of office of members.—A member other than an ex-officio member 
shall hold office for a period of three years: 


Provided that the elected members shall cease to hold office if they cease to 
be members of the Board. 


5. Resignation.—A member may resign his office by writing under his hand 
addressed to the President. 


6. Filling of casual vacancies.—If any member dies or resigns his officc 
Or ceases to be a member for any other reason the vacancy shall be filled up 
by a fresh nomination or election under sub-regulation (2) of regulation 3 and 
the member so nominated or elected shall hold office for the unexpired period 
of the term of office of the member whose place he fills. 


7. Powers and duties of Regional Examination Councils.—Each Regional 
Examination Council shall exercise such powers and perform such duties of the 
Examinations Committee of the Board as may be entrusted to it by notification 
by the Board accordng to the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 25 of the 


Act. 

8. Existing regulations to remain in force.—Existing instructions and regula- 
tions relating to conduct of examinations in so far as they are not inconsistent 
with the provisions of these regulations shall remain in force until otherwise 
directed and shall be binding on the Regional Examination Councils. 


9. Interpretations.—If any question arises relating to the interpretation of 
any of these regulations, such question shall be rcferred to the Board and the 
decision of the Board thereon shall be final. 


S. M. CHATTERIJI, 
President, 


West Bengal Board of Secondary Education.

PART I—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government

ea ns ae Soman 


GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
HOME DEPARTMENT 


Transport 
NOTIFICATION 


No. 1381-WT.—6th February 1974.—In pursuance of the provisions of sub- 
section (3A) of section 63 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Act 4 of 1939), 
the Governor is pleased hereby to publish a draft of the following reciprocal 
transport agreement which the State of West Bengal and Union Territory of 
Delhi propose to enter into, for the information of all concerned likely to be 
affected thereby. 


Notice is hereby given that the proposed agreement and any representation 
in connection therewith reccived by the Deputy Secretary, Home (Transport) 
Department, Government of West Bengal, by the 16th March 1974, at the 
latest shall be taken into consideration by the Transport Commissioner and 
ex-officio Secretary, Home (Transport) Department, Government of West 
Bengal, on or after the 25th March 1974, at 11 a.m. in the office chamber of 
the Transport Commissioner and cx-ofticio Secretary, Home (Transport) 
Department, Government of West Bengal, at Writers’ Building, Calcutta-7 7 


Draft Reciprocal Transport Agreement 


Preamble 


In view of the rapid economic development in the country and with a view 
ما‎ encouraging movement of transport vehicles on inter-State routes between 
West Bengal and Delhi and to regulate and control their operation, it 5ا‎ 
necessary to enter into a reciprocal transport agreement. 


2. Now, thereofre, the Government of the two States hereby enter into 
an agreement on the terms and conditions as set out hereafter. 


3. This agreement, upon its ratification by the two State Governments, 
shall come into force from a date to be mutually agreed upon between the 
Transport Commissioner, West Bengal and the Director of Transport, Delhi. 


308 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, FEBRUARY 9) 1974 


مگمے سے 
ےوہ دھکُمسےمأمس-ےحوند - oS‏ —- 


4. This agreement shall be followed till such time as a new agreement 
between the two States is arrived at or the existing agreement is rescinded after 
the issue of six months’ notice by either side. 


5. In this agreement,— 


(i) 1০ in relation to Delhi means the Delhi Administration, 
an 


Qi) “State” in relation to Delhi means the Union Territory of Delhi. 


Taxation 


6. (a) There shall be single point motor vehicles taxation in respect of 
vehicles covered by substantive permits within the agreed quota and counter- 
signed by the Transport Authority of the reciprocating State. 


(b) No motor vehicle tax shall be leviable in the reciprocating State in 
respect of vehicles covered by special permits issued under section 63(6) of 
the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, by the other State. 


(c) Temporary permits for motor vehicles issued during the pendency of 
renewal of substantive permits under section 62(d) of the said Act shall be 
countersigned and the principle of single point taxation shall be applicable. 


(d) There shall be no exemption from payment of goods and passengers 
tax in respect of any class of motor vehicle entering into the other State on 
countersignature of substantive permit or temporary permit. 


(e) There shall be double point motor vehicle taxation in respect of vehicles 
covered by all kinds of temporary permits other than those issued under 
se hie 2(d) and 63(6) of the said Act by the State Transport Authority, 
Delhi. 


In cases of similar temporary permits issued by the State Transport 
Authority, West Bengal, the vehicles shall be subject to double point taxation 
in accordance with the provision of Delhi Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1962, 
1.5. the Delhi tax shall be payable if a temporary permit is issued for a period 
exceeding 90 days. 


Public Carriers (Substantive Permits) 


7. (a) It is agreed that 50 public carrier permits belonging to each State 
Shall be countersigned by the State Transport Authority of the other State. 
in the recommendation of the State Transport Authority of the home State 
Such countersignatures shall be granted for Delhi-Calcutta via the shortest 
route to be indicated in the permit. 


(b) The permits so countersigned will be subject to the following 
conditions:— 


(i) The public carriers operating under countersignature shall not be used 
for picking up and setting down goods between any two points 
lying exclusively within the territory of the reciprocating State, 
i.e., In such cases, vehicles shall be prohibited ও Carrying on 
any business or transporting goods exclusively within the territory 
of the other State and shall be subject to such conditions as may 
be imposed under sections 56 and 50 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 
1939, as the concerned Transport Authority may deem fit to impose. 


(ii) The ladcn weight limits for roads fixed in the respective State shall 
not be exceeded. 


Public Carriers (Temporary Permits) 


8, Temporary permits for 50 vehicles valid for a period not exceeding 30 
days may be issued by the Transport Authorities of each State without prior 
concurrence by the State Transport Authority of the other State. 


These temporary permits shall be issued on single point taxation basis. In 
addition to these 50 temporary permits, further 100 temporary permits may 
be issued by the State Transport Authority of each State on payment of tax 
due to the other State. 


[PART ] 


পপ وسے۔ چسچھہے۔ےہسےے ہے سے سے لت ست‎ টু 


Parr 1] 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, FEBRUARY 9, 1974 


These temporary permits shall be subject to the following conditions:— 


(a) That public carriers operating under these permits shall not be used 
for picking up goods at any point in the reciprocating State and 
dropping them at another point in the reciprocating State. In other 
words intra-State transport of goods in the reciprocating State shall 
not be undertaken. 


(b) Laden weight restrictions for carrying loads fixed by either State shall 
not be exceeded. 


(c) The Transport Authority issuing such 100 permits sball ensure that 
all the taxes of the reciprocating State are paid in advance by 
demand drafts before these are issued. Copies of such permits or 
statements containing all particulars of such temporary permits 
together with demand dratt and other relevant information shall 
be sent to the Secretary, State Transport Authority of the recipro- 
cating State at weekly intervals mentioning the number and date 
of the demand drafts and amounts remitted. 


Private Carriers (Regular Permits) 


9. It is agreed that permits for 5 private carriers shall be countersigned by 
the State Transport Authority of the reciprocating State. Such counter- 
signature shall be for specified routes or area connecting specified terminals by 
the shortest routes in either State subejct to the conditions that goods of 
specified nature only shall be carried. 


Private Carriers (Temporary Permits) 


10. It is agreed that private carrier permits valid for a period not exceed- 
ing 30 days may be issued by the Transport Authorities of either State without 
prior concurrence. Such temporary permits shall be valid for specific route 
or area without restriction on the number of trips during the period of validity. 
These permits shall be issued subject to the condition that goods of specified 
nature only shall be carried. 


Taxi Cabs/Tourist Cabs (Substantive Permits) 


11. In the interest of development of tourist and commercial _ trade, 
contract carriage permits (motor 0805 and tourist cabs) of reciprocating State 
Shall be countersigned without restriction of number for any area 17 the 
reciprocating State on the basis of single point taxation. 


Contract Carriage (Omnibus/Taxi Cabs/Tourist Cabs) 


12. (a) Temporary permits for Contract Carriage (Omnibus/Taxi Cabs/ 
Tourist Cabs) may be issued as per need without prior concurrence of the other 
State for the following purposes:— 


(1) Carriage of marriage parties and such other parties like educational 
excursion parties; 


(81) Pilgrimage parties and tourist parties. 
(b) These temporary permits shall be subject to the following conditions:-— 


(i) Passengers in excess of ithe seating capacity specified under ۶ 
registration certificate shall not be carried and no_ standing 
passenger shall be allowed. 


(11) The contract carriage (Omnibus) shall be hired by single party and 
Shall be used for a single return journey. 


(iii) Each such temporary permit shall clearly specify the date of outward 
journey and the date of return journey. In case any party engaging 
a contract carriage on temporary permit wishes to change the date 
of return journey subsequent to the issue of the permit, it shall 
obtain permission in writing to that effect from the Transport 
Authority within whose jurisdiction the contract carriage happens 
to be at that time. 


(iv) aa of . temporary permits shall be sent to the Secretary, State 
ransport Authority of the reciprocating States as soon as possible 
after their issue.

(v) The fare shall be charged in accordance with the rate prescribed by 
the home State of the permit issuing authority which shall be 
mentioned in the permit. 


(c) The authority issuing such temporary permits shall ensure that all taxes 
of i reciprocating State are paid in advance by Demand Drafts payable as 
under:— 


(i) In the case of Motor Vehicles Tax, the Taxing Officer, Calcutta and 
the Secretary, S.T.A., Delhi. 


(ii) In the case of goods and passenger tax to such authority as may be 
designated in this behalf by the Director of Transport, Delhi and 
the Transport Commissioner, West Bengal, as and when such a tax 
is leviable in either State. 


(iii) The Demand Drafts shall be sent to the aforesaid authority at weekly 
intervals with the following information:—

Corridor Facilities 


13. In order to facilitate movement of vehicles beyond the jurisdiction of 
West Bengal and Delhi corridor facilities are ageed to on the following 
conditions:— 

(i) Substantive public carrier permits in respect of vehicles availing 
corrider facilities shall be countersigned by the State Transport 
Authorities of respective States and shall be exempted from double 
point taxation on reciprocal basis up to the number specified under 
the agreement. 

(ii) Vehicle passing through the corridor shall neither pick up nor drop 
down goods within the corridor State. In other words, it 57811 
be “sealed wagon” traffic. 

(iii) The total laden weight of the vehicle at no time shall exceed the 
laden weight restrictions as may be in force in the corridor State 
under section 74 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939. 

(iv) The vehicles taking advantage of the corridor facilities shall pass by 
the shortest direct route. 


General 


14. Transport Authorities of West Bengal and Delhi shall accord recogni- 
tion to the Tax-token, Registration Certificate, Counductor’s License, Certificate 
of fitness, etc., in respect of transport vehicles plying on inter-State routes in 
accordance with this Agreement. 


In witness whereof the parties hereto have signed this agreement the day 
and year first written above. 
S.C. Pandey, 
Director of Transport, 
Delhi.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


HOME DEPARTMENT 


Transport 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 1659-WT /3T-32/72.—l2th February 1974.—In 
pursuance of the provisions of sub-section (3B) of 
section 63 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Act 4 
of 1939), the Governor is pleased hereby to publish 
the following reciprocal transport agreement arrived 
at between the Government of West Bengal and the 
Government of Uttar Pradesh, after previous publi- 
cation of the draft of the same under notification 
No. 18581-WT, dated the 4th December 1973 at 
pages 3395-3397 of Part I of the “Calcutta Gazette, 
Extraordinary” of the 6th December 1973, as 
required by sub-section (3A) of sectjon 63 of the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1939. 


RECIPROCAL TRANSPORT AGREEMENT 


Whereas, in view of the rapid economic develop- 
ment of the country and with a view to encouraging 
ovement of transport vehicles on _ Inter-State 
routes between Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, 
and regulate and control their operation, it 15 
necessary to enter into a reciprocal agreement ; 


Now, therefore, in supersession of all previous 
agreements in the matter of road transport, the 

overnments of Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, 
hereby enter into a fresh agreement on the terms 
and conditions set out herein below. 


۹3148 


This reciprocal agreement shall be valid for a 
period of three ycars. For reasons to be given in 
writing by either State Government, this agreement 
can be revoked on three months’ notice and sus- 
pended on one month’s notice. The agreement 
embodied in this agreement shall come into force 
from the date to be mutually fixed by the Trans- 
port Commissioner, Uttar Pradesh and the Trans- 
port Commissioner, West Bengal, and from the 
Same date all previous agreements will stand super- 
seded. This agreement shall be subject to revisjon 
every six months or periodically at the instance of 
either State. 


1. Public Carriers (Substantive Permits): 
(a) It is agreed that public carrier’s permits 
for 225 goods vehicles shall be counter- 
signed by the transport authorities of either 
State. The countersignature shall be valid 
for the entire State permitting operation on 
National and State Highways only with 
deviation up to 30 Kms. from these roads to 
reach a manufacturing concern or an indus- 
trial centre. 


(b) Public Carriers operating on inter-State routes 
on countersignature shall not be used as 
inter-State transport within the territory of 
the countersigning State. 


2. Petrol Tankers (Substantive Permits): The 
permits for petrol tankers owned by oil com- 
panies or their authorised agents or con- 
tractors and exclusively used for the trans- 
port of petrol and petroleum products, shall 
be freely countersigned as and when recom- 
mended by the transport authorities of

——— 


either State for operation in the whole of 
the reciprocating State. Such permits will 
be over and above the agreed quota of public 
carrier and private carrier permits. 


3. Public Carriers (Temporary Permits): (a) In 


order to. meet special temporary needs, ft Is 
agreed that temporary public carrier permits 
may be issued for a maximum period of 30 
days by either State in accordance with the 
provisions of section 62(b) and (c) of the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, for plying on 
Inter-State routes, between the two States 
without any restrictions of their numbers. 
Such temporary permits shall be issued by 
any 01105910669 without prior concurrence of 
the rzefiprocating State. A temporary 
permit so issued shall be subject to the 
following conditions :— 


(i) It may be issued for all National and State 


Highways with deviation of 30 K.m. on 
either side without any restriction on the 
number of trips during its period of 
validity. 


(ii) The vehicle operating under the permit shall 


not be, used as inter-State transport with- 
in the’ jurisdiction of the’ reciprocating 
State. 


4. Private Carriers (Substantive Permits) £ 


Private carrier permits recommended 101 
countersignature by the transport authority 
of either State shall be countersigned by the 
other State without any restriction on their 
number subject to he condition that goods 
of specified nature shall onlv be carried. 


Recommendations for c:.untersignature in respect 


of private carriers shall be made after a 
thorouh scrutiny of bona fides of the 
business of the applicants in the other 
State. 


Such vehicles shall not be used as inter-State 


transport within the jurisdiction of ٤ 
countersigning State. 


5. Private Carriers (Temporary Permits): 


a) Temporary permits valid for a period 
٦ ا‎ 30 days may be issued by the 
Transport Authority of one State without 
prior concurrence of the Transport Autho- 
rity of the other State without any restric- 
tion of their number as and when necessary. 
A temporary permit so issued shall be for a 
specified direct route or a specified area 
without any restriction on the number of 
trips during the validity of the permit. 


(b) Such temporary permits shall be used for 


the carriage of specified goods and for the 
bona fide use of the applicants only.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948 (West Ber. 
Act 1] of 1948) was amended by the promulgation of the West Bengal Land 
(Requisition and Acquisition) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (West Bengal 
Qrdinance No. XIV of 1973) so that— 


@) requisition and acquisition of land can be made for the purpose of 


increasing employment opportunities for the people by establishing 
commercial estates and industrial estates in different areas; and 


(ii) on account payment of compensation in advance can be made 09 
mitigate the hardship of the affected persons. 


2. The Bill seeks to enact the provisions of the aforesaid Ordinance. 


CALCUTTA, 


Phe 14ih February, 1974. GURU PADA KHAN, 
Member-in-charge. 


FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM. 


Under clauses 2 and 3 of the West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisi- 
tion) (Amendment) Bill, 1974, it is proposed to amend the West Bengal Land 
(Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948 (West Bengal Act II of 1948) so as to 
enable the State Government to requisition and acquire land under the 
aforesaid Act for the purpose of increasing employment opportunities for the 


people by establishing commercial estates and industrial estates in different 
areas. 


2. It is not possible to estimate at this stage the expenditure that the 
State Government may have to incur for requisitioning and acquisition of land 
under the Act for the aforesaid purpose as it is difficult to say how much land 
would be requisitioned and acquired by the State Government for the said 
purpose. 


3. Under clause 4 of the Bill, it is proposed to amend the Act so as_ to 
authorise, with retrospective effect, advance (on account) payment of compen- 
sation up to 80 per cent. of the amount likely to be determined as 
compensation under the Act, after possession of any land has been obtained by 
requisitioning and the State Government decides to acquire the land. 


4. This 70109515101) does not involve any additional financial liability on the 
State Government. On the other hand, it will save the State Government 


from payment of a considerable amount in the shape of interest payable to the 
persons interested. 


CALCUTTA, 


The 14th February, 1974. GURU PADA KHAN, 
Member-in-charge. 


By order of the Governor, 
K. K. MOITRA, 
Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The life of the West Bengal Premises Requisition and Control (Temporary 
Provisions) Act, 1947 (West Ben. Act V of 1947), is due to expire after the 
31st March, 1974. As the housing problem in the State is still acute and as 
it is often extremely difficult to find accommodation for টা purposes by 
private treaty, it is necessary that the powers obtained under the Act should 
be retained for a further period of five years, that is to Say, up to the 3lst day 
of March, 1979. 


2. The Bill has been framed with the above object in view. 


CALCUTTA, GURU PADA KHAN, 
The !4th February, 1974. Member-in-charge. 


FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM. 


Under clause 2 of the Bill the life of the West Bengal Premises Requisition 
and Control (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1947 (West Ben. Act V of 1947), is 
sought to be extended by a further period of five years beyond the 3lst 
March, 1974. The Act, by itself, does not entail any financial liability on 
the State Government. Although the initial responsibility for payment of com- 
pensation to the landlords for premises requisitioned under the Act rests on 
the State Government, the entire cost is ultimately recoverable from the persons 
in occupation of the requisitioned premises. 


CALCUTTA, GURU PADA KHAN, 
The 14th February, 1974. Member-in-charge.

shall be paid to the owner and every person interested in

scribed.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


With a view to facilitating re-excavation of private derelict tanks and 
ensuring supply of irrigation water therefrom to adjoining lands, the Governor 
was pleased to promulgate the West Bengal Tanks (Acquisition of Irrigation 
Rights) Ordinance, 1973 (West Bengal Ordinance No. VIII of 1973) as the 
State Legislative Assembly was not in session and the matter was considered 
very urgent. 


2. The Bill seeks to enact the provisions of the said Ordimance.

FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM 


Clause 8 of the Bill provides for payment for acquisition of the right of 
using water of any derelict tank at the rate of Re. 1 per 0.4 hectare of the 
total area of the tank. It is not possible to estimate at this stage the total 
arca of such derelict tanks whose irrigation rights will be acquired under the 
present legislation. The amount to be paid will obviously be very small.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The life of the West Bengal Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) 
Act, 195] (West Ben. Act VIII of 1951), 1১: due to expire after the 3lst March, 
1974. The Act provides for continuance of requisition in respect of properties 
requisitioned under the Defence of India Act, 1939 (35 of 1939) and held 
under requisition for a public purpose, and their subsequent acquisition. As 
a considerable area of land and a number of buildings are subject to conti- 
nued requisition under the Act and as it has not been possible either to de- 
requisition the lands and buildings or to acquire them permanently, it has 
become necessary to keep the Act alive for a turther period of two years 
up to the 315 March, 1976. 


2. The Bill has been framed with the above object in view. 


CALCUTTA, GURU PADA KHAN, 
The 14th February, 1974. Member-in-churge. 


FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM. 


Under clause 2 of the Bill, the life of the West Bengal Requisitioned Land 
(Continuance of Powers) Act, 1951 (West Ben. Act VIII of 1951), is sought to 
be extended by a further period of two years up to the 3lst March, 1976. The 
Bill, by itself, does not involve any additional liability although compensation 
will have to be paid in accordance with the provisions of the Act for keeping 
the properties under continued 52 as also for acquisition when such 
properties are permanently acquired. 


2. It is not possible to estimate at this stage the expenditure that the 
State Government may have to incur for keeping the properties under requisi- 
tion or for acquiring them as it is difficult to say when and which of the 
properties under requisition would be released from requisition or acquired 
permanently under the provisions of the Act. 

CALCUTTA, GURU PADA KHAN, 


The 14th February, 1974 Member-in-charge.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


No person can carry on rice-milling operations with the aid of power, either 
in a rice mill or in a paddy-husking machine without a licence under the Rice- 
Milling Industry (Regulation) Act, $958 (Central Act 21 of 1958). The provi- 
sions of the Act not being stringent enough, unlicensed mills have continued 
to come up and aperate in West Bengal for the purpose of facilitating profiteer- 
ing in mce. It has, therefore, been found necessary to make some ol the 
provisions of the Act more stringent in their application to West Bengal so 
= to prevent effectively commission and recurrence of offences against the 
aw. 


In order to bring about the desired change an Ordinance called the Rice- 
Milling Industry (Regulation) (West Bengal Amendment) Ordinance, 1974 
(West Bengal Ordinance No. II of 1974), was promulgated on the 22nd January, 
1974 and published in the “Calcutta Gazette, Extraordinary,” of the 25th 
১ 1974. The Ordinance has amended the Act, in its application to 

est Bengal, so as to make the offence of running an unlicensed mill both 
cognizable and non-bailable and to invest the enforcement machinery with 
powers to seize and/or seal such an unlicensed mill and its accessories and 
available stocks of rice and paddy used in contravention of the law. 


The Rice-Milling Industry (Regulation) (West Bengal Amendment) 9111, 
1974 seeks to replace the Ordinance.

Bill No. 7 of 1974 
THE WEST BENGAL INDUSTRIAL INFRA-STRUCTURE 
DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION BILL, 1974. 


A = 
BILL 


to make special provision for securing development of trade, 
commerce and industries on well-planned basis in_ the 
State of West Bengal, and for that purpose to establish 
an Industrial Infra-structure Development Corporation, 
and for matters connected therewith or incidental there- 
to. 


WHEREAS it 1s expedient to make special provision for 
securing development of trade, commerce and industries on 
well-planned basis in the State of West Bengal, and for that 
purpose to establish in Industrial Infra-structure Develop= 
ment Corporation, and for matters connected therewith or 
incidental thereto ; 


It is hereby enacted in the Twenty-fifth Year of the 
Republic of India, by the Legislature of West Bengal, as 
follows :— 


CHAPTER I 
Preliminary 


1. (2) This Act may be called the West Bengal Industrial 
Infra-structure Development Corporation Act, 1974. 


(2) It extends to the whole of West Bengal. 


(3) This Act except the provisions of Chapter ۷ shall 
come into force at once. The provisions of Chapter V shall 
come into force on such date as the State Government may, 
by notification, appoint and for this purpose different dates 
may be appointed for different areas to be specified in the

all books of accounts and other books maintained by it and

(4) The auditor may, in relation to the accounts of the

he shall state,— 


(a) in the case of books of accounts and other books main- 
tained by the Corporation, whether in his opinion 
the accounts exhibit a true and fair view of the 
state of affairs of the Corporation at the end of the 
year, and 


(b) in case he had called for an explanation or information 
from the Corporation, whether it has been given' 
and whether it is satisfactory. 


(6) As soon as the accounts of the Corporation are audited, 
the Corporation shall send a copy thereof together with the 


copy of the report of the auditor thereon to the State Govern- 
ment. 


(7) The State Government shall cause the accounts of the 
Corporation, together with the audit report thereon forwarded, 
to it under sub-section (6), to be 1910. annually before’ the 
Legislative Assembly. 


26. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in section 25,

tion or to a particular period. 


(2) When an order is made under sub-section (J), the Cor- 
poration shall present or cause to be presented for audit such 
accounts and shall furnish to the person referred to in sub- 
section (1) such information as the said person may require for 
the purpose of audit. 


(3) Without prejudice to anything contained in the preced- 
ing sub-sections, and in section 25, the Comptroller and 
Auditor-General of India may, if so requested by the State 
Government, examine, and report upon, the accounts of the 
Corporation, and any expenditure incurred by him in connec- 
tion with such examination and report shall be payable by 


the Corporation to the Comptroller and Auditor-General of 
India.

38. (2) No person shall— 


(a) erect any new building, or 
(b) alter any existing building, or 


(c) undertake any specific development of land, 
in any industrial estate entrusted to thé Corporation (herein- 
after in this Chapter referred to as the industrial estate) except 
with permission from, and in accordance with the terms and 
conditions settled by, such Corporation. 


(2) On receipt of any application from a person submitted 
in the prescribed form and manner, for permission referred 
ta in’ sub-section (J), the Corporation may, after such inquiry 
as it may deem fit, grant such permission subject to such terms 
and conditions as may he settled by it. 


39. (1) If the Corporation, upon report from any of its 
Officers or from other information in its possession or after 
holding a local inquiry, is satisfied that the owner of any land 
in any industrial estate has failed— 


(9) to provide any.amenity in relation to such land which, 
in the opinion of the Corporation, is required to 
be provided in the interest of development of in- 
dustry, trade and commerce within such area, or 


(৮) to carry out any specific development of the land for 
which permission has been obtained from _ the 
Corporation under sub-section (1) of section 38, 


the Corporation may serve upon such owner a notice requiring 
him to provide such amenity or carry out such development, 
as ethe case may be, within such time as may be specified in 
the notice. 


(2) If any such amenity is not provided or any such 
development is not carried out within the time specified in 
the notice, then the Corporation may itself provide the 
amenity or carry out the development or have it provided or 
carried out through such agency as it deems fit: 


Provided that before taking any action under this sub- 
section, the Corporation shall afford reasonable opportunity 
to the owner of the land to show cause as to why such action 
should not be taken. : 


(3) All expenses incurred by the Corporation or the agency 
employed by it, in providing such amenity or carrying out 
such development, together with interest at such rate not 
exceeding six and a quarter per centum per annum as the 
State Government may, by order, fix, from the date when a 
demand for the expenses is made until payment, shall be 
recoverable by the Corporation from the owner. 


40. (/) Where the erection of any building in an industrial 
estate has been commenced or is being carried on, or has 
been completed, or any existing buidling is altered, in con- 
travention of the terms and conditions settled by the Cor- 
poration, any officer of the Corporation empowered by it in 
this behalf may, in addition to any prosecution that may bc 
instituted under this Act, make an order directing the owner 
to demolish such erection or to so alter the same as to con- 
form to the said terms and conditions within a period of 
three months from the date of the order: 


Provided that no such order shall be made unless the 
owner has been given a reasonable opportunity to show cause 
why the order should not be made. 


(2) Any person aggrieved by an order under sub-section 
(7) may appeal against that order, within thirty days trom 
the date thereof, to a Committce of the Corporation set uo 
for the purpose by regulations made in this behalf. Such 
Committee may, following the procedure provided by regula- 
Ons made in this behalf, confirm, modify or set aside the 
order.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


About eighty-four per cent. of the industrial establishments working in the 
State of West Bengal are located in the Calcutta industrial area which includes 
portions of the districts of Howrah and 24-Parganas. The balance of sixteen 
per cent. are spread out over the remaining portion of the Stale. To remove 
this regional imbalance in the growth and development of industries in the 
State, the Government of West Bengal brought into operation the West Bengal 
Incentive Scheme, 1971, offering a package of financial incentives to attract 
enterpreneurs in the backward districts of the State. The Central Government 
have also introduced a scheme of granting fifteen per cent. subsidy on capital 
assets in the districts of Purulia, Nadia and Midnapore which have been 
declared as backward districts. To enable the flow of finances to come from 
public financing institutions at concessional rates, the Central Government have 
declared the entire State of West Bengal except Culcutta and the districts of 
Howrah and 24-Parganas as backward areas, but al] these special efforts and 
financial concessions have not proved themselves to be sufficiently adequate and 
attractive to lure the entrepreneurs away into the backward districts. 


In the above context, it has been keenly felt that to facilitate the establish- 
ment, growth and development of industries in the backward districts, the 
State Government should, in addition to aforesaid special steps, simultaneously 
build up adequate jnfra-structures in the backward districts in the shape of 
developed industrial areas with sufficient supply of water, electric powers, good 
roads and communications, buildings, sheds, sewerages and other kinds of 
modern civic facilities and amenities to attract entrepreneurs in a big way, and 
with this end in view the West Bengal Industrial Infra-structure Development 
Corporation Ordinance, 1973 (West Bengal Ordinance No. 1X of 1973), was 
promulgated by the Governor of West Bengal and published in the Calcutta 
Gazette, Extraordinary, of the 16th November, 1973 and a statutory corporation 
called the West Bengal Industrial Infra-structure Development Corporation has 
been set up with effect on and from the 19th November, 1973. The functions of 
দর shall mainly extend to the backward districts of the State and 
sha سس‎ 


(a) generally to develop industrial infra-structure for expeditious and 
orderly establishment, growth and development of industries, trade 
and commerce on well-planned basis in the State, 


(b) to develop industrial areas for the purpose of new growth centres and 
make the same available for industrial and commercial undertakings 
and trading concerns to enable them to establish 11310501105 and to 
carry on trade and commerce thereon, 


(c) to undertake development work, in respect of any particular area 
(covered by growth centre) in relation to— 
(i) reclamation and improvement of lands, 
(ii) water supply, 
(iii) drainage, 
(tv) captive power generation and supply, 
(v) roads, 
(vi) transport and communication, 
(vti) housing accommodation, and 


(viii) making provisions for other kinds of modern facilities and ameni- 
ties to make growth centres particularly suitable and attractive 
for growth of industrial and commercial undertakings therein. 


It is desirable that the corporation shall have also power to acquire, ۵۹ 
and transfer any property, as such corporation may deem necessary, for the 
discharge of any of its aforesaid proposed functions. The State Government 
may also make grants, loans and advances to such a corporation to enable it 
to discharge its proposed functions efficiently. Such corportion may also be 
empowered to borrow money in the open market or from bank or anv other

The present Bill has been brought to replace the West Bengal Industrial 
Infra-structure Development Corporation Ordinance, 1973 (West Bengal Ordi- 
nance IX of 1973), by enactment of the West Bengal Industrial Infra-structure 
Development Corporation Act, 1974. (in order the said Ordinance shall be 
deemed to have been validly done or taken under this Act as if this Act had

FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM. 


The functions of the West Bengal Industrial Infra-structure Development 
Corporation, amongst other things, include acquisition of lands, development 
of such lands for industrial arcas for the purposes of new growth centres, and 
to make such areas available for industrial and commercial undertaking and 
trading concerns to enable them to establish industries and to carry on trade 
and commerce thereon. It would be one of the main functions of the corpora- 
tion to provide such industrial areas with sufficient supply of water, electric 
power, good roads, drainage, housing accommodation, buildings, sheds, sewer- 
ages and other kinds of modern civic amenities to attract entrepreneurs to the 
backward districts in a big way. It has been further proposed that the State 
Government may make some subvention, grants, loans and advances to the 
شسوہ ود‎ corporation. It has been also provided that the corporation shall 

ave powers to borrow money in the open market and from banks and other 
financial institutions with or without the State Government guarantee. Provi- 
sions have been also made for the State Government paying the compensation 
for acquisition of lands by the proposed corporation. 


While the firm estimates about the amount of compensation that may be 
required to be paid by the State Government for acquisition of lands for the 
corporation for development are yet to be worked gut, a tentative provision of 
Rs. 30 lakhs has been provided in the State Annual Plan, 1974-75, for payment 
of compensation for acquisition of 600 acres of land in the first phase in new 
growth centres having immediate possibilities for industrial development. 
Having considered the development programme of the corporation for the 
year 1974-75, provisions of Rs. 50 lakhs for development of land and administra- 
tive expenses of the corporation and Rs. 27.90 lakhs for Haldia water supply 
scheme to be implemented by the corporation have also been provided in the 
State Annual Plan, 1974-75, in addition to the amount of Rs. 2 lakhs released 
as loan to the corporation during the year 1973-74. Besides, it has been tenta- 
tively agreed that the State Government will be able to raise from the open 
market a loan of Rs. 110 lakhs during the year 1974-75. 


The scheme incorporated in the proposed Bill is proposed to be implemented 
in different phases extending over a number of years in accordance to the 
respective needs of the backward districts and overall availability of resources 
for the said purpose. 


The scheme has been included in the State Fifth Five-Year Plan and a total 
outlay of Rs. 7 crores—Rs. 2.50 crores for payment of cost of acquisition 01 
lands and Rs. 4.50 crores for administrative and development expenses of the 
corporation—has already been recommended for the Fifth Plan period. The 
expenditure from the consolidated fund of the State on account of the proposed 
corporation is likely to increase from year to vear as the tempo and volume of 
work of the proposed corporation develop with the passage of time. 


CALCUTTA, T. K. GHOSH, 
The 15th February, 1974. Member-in-charge.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


Under the existing provisions of the Calcutta Manicipal Act, 1951, Commis- 
sioner of Corporation ot Calcutta is the only officer authorised to hear and 
dispose of building cases regarding removal, demolition, alteration and 
stoppage of unlawful building work. The number of such cases has become 
very large and it is difficult for the Commissioner to dispose of such cases 
singly. Delegation of Commissioner's power to Deputy Commissioners and to 
any specially appointed officers is considered necessary. 


2. The Commissioner or any such officer as aforesaid is authorised to allow 
a person, who has constructed a structure without any sanctioned plan, to 
submit 3 proper plan and also to sanction such plan. 


3. The Bill seeks to achieve the objectives desired in the foregoing 
paragraphs.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The West Bengal Medical and Dental Colleges (Regulation of Admission) 
Act, 1973 (West Bengal Act XXXVI of 1973), came into force in this State 
with effect from the academic session 1973-74. The Act provides, .nter alia, 
for districtwise distribution of the seats in the Medical and Dental Colleges in 
West Bengal on the basis of the population of the districts of West Bengal 
(Calcutta comprised within the territorial jurisdiction of the Calcutta Corpora- 
tion is also a district for the purpose of this Act), with a view to ensuring 
adequate medical facilities in the districts of West Bengal. 


Certain practical difficulties with regard to candidates’ ‘normal residence’ 
11) the districts and also their educational qualifications were experienced, while 
implementing the provisions of the Act for the academic session 1973-74. The 
Act, in its present form, does not enable the normal residents of West Bengal, 
who are at present residing outside this State for some reason or other, or the 
students of Bengali origin, who had migrated to India from the erstwhile East 
Pakistan prior to 25th March, 1971, or the sons and daughters of employees of 
Central, State or Union Territory Governments or of Statutory/Corporate 
undertakings of such Government, who are for the time being stationed in this 
State, to apply for admission to the Medical and Dental Colleges in West 
Bengal. The Act also does not specify the educational qualification, which 
the candidates have to possess for such admission. 


The present Bill seeks to remove the difficulties with regard to candidates’ 
normal residence, as aforesaid, to specify the educational qualifications of the 
candidates and also to suitably modify the preamble and the long title of the 
Act of 1973 in keeping with the objects of the Act. 


A. K. PANJA, 


Member-in-charge.

Land Acquisition

CALCUTTA.—No. 3077-L.A.(II) /6P-6/70. — 22nd 
February 1974.—Whereas the functions of the Central 
Government under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 
(I of 1894) in relation to the acquisition of land for 
the purposes of the Union have been entrusted to 
athe State Government by Notification No. 20/1/55- 
Judl.(1), dated the 14th May 1955, issued by the 
Government of India in the Ministry of Home Affairs 
under clause (I) of article 258 of the Constitution of 
"India, as S.R.O. 1074 and published at page 868, 
Part II, section 3 of the “Gazette of India’, dated 
215 May 1955; 


And whereas it appears to the Governor that land 
is likely to be needed for a public purpose, namely, 
for the construction of Dharamtala Post Office 
Building, it is hereby notified that a piece of land 
comprising southern portion of premises Nos. 43 
and 43/1, Dharamtala Street (Lenin Sarani) and 
measuring, more or less, 0.0788 of a hectare (0.1942 
of an acre) and bounded on the— 


North—By the remaining portion of premises 
Nos. 43 and 43/1, Dharamtala Street (Lenin 
Sarani) including passage right from Dharam- 
tala Street (Lenin Sarani); 

East—By premises Nos. 44 and 44/1, Dharamtala 
Street (Lenin Sarani) and 12, Mott Lane 
(Manilal Saha Lane); 

South— By Mott Lane (Manilal Saha Lane), 

West--By premises Nos. 14 Mott Lane (Manilal 
Saha Lane) and 42, Dharamtala Street (Lenin 
Sarani), 


is likely to be needed for the aforesaid public pur- 
pose at the public expense within the aforesaid Ward 
No. 52 (old) of the Calcutta Municipality, in the 
City of Calcutta. 


This Notification is made under the provisions of 
section 4 of Act I of 1894, read with the said Notifica- 
tion, to all whom it may concern. 


A plan of the land may be inspected in the office 
of the First Land Acquisition Collector, Calcutta, 
at No. 5, Bankshall Street, Calcutta. 


In exercise of the powers conferred by the afore- 
said section read with the said Notification, the 
Governor is pleased to authorise the officer for the 
time being engaged in the undertaking, with their 
Servants and workmen, to enter upon and survey 
the land and do all other acts required or permitted 
by that section. 


Any person interested in the above land, who has 
any objection to acquisition thereof, may, within 
thirty days after the date on which public notice of 
the substance of this Notification is given in the 
locality file an objection in writing before the First 
Land Acquisition Collector, Calcutta, at ‘No. 5, 
Bankshall Street, Calcutta.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The object of the present Bill is to continue the provisions of the Bengal 
Finance (Sales Tax) (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1973, which was 
promulgated on the 23rd September, 1973 with a view to amending the Bengal 
Finance (Sales Tax) Act, 1941 to provide for a special mode of recovery under 
the Bengal Finance (Sales Tax) Act, 1941 analogous to garnishee proceedings 
prescribed under sections 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure and 226 of the 
Income Tax Act, 1961 and 8150 to facilitate the functioning of the 
Special Certificate Courts set up under the Commercial Taxes Directorate. 


No additional expenditure is envisaged in order to give effect to the 
provisions of the Bill.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The object of the present Bill is to continue the provisions of the Bengal 
Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974, which was 2 
on the 4th January, 1974 with a view to amending section 56 of the Bengal 
Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1944 for disclosure of information relating to 
assegsment, recovery, remission, refund, etc., to an officer of Central Govern- 
ment or the State Government for the purpose of audit of receipts and refunds 
of tax imposed under the said Act. 


No additional expenditure is envisaged in order to give effect to the 
provisions of the Bill.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


HOME DEPARTMENT 
Transport 
NOTIFICATION 


No. 2152-WT /3T-21/72.—25th February 1974.— 

pursuance of the provisions of sub-section (3A) 
of section 63 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Act 
4 of 1939), the Governor is pleased hereby to publish 
a draft of the following reciprocal transport agree- 
ment which the States of West Bengal and Punjab 
propose to enter into, for the information of all 
concerned likely to be affected thereby. 


Notice is hereby given that the proposed agree- 
ment and any _ representation in connection there- 
with received by the Deputy Secretary, Home 
(Transport) Department, Government of West 
Bengal, by the 2nd April 1974 at the latest shall 


be taken into consideration by the Transport 
Commissioner and ex-officio Secretary, Home 
(Transport) Department, Government of West 


Bengal, on or after the 8th April 1974, at 11 am. 
in the office chamber of the Transport Com- 
missioner and ex-officio Secretary, Home (Trans- 
port) Department, Government of West Bengal, at 
Writers’ Buildings, Calcutta-700001. 


Reciprocal Agreement between the State of West 
Bengal and the State of Punjab in respect of 
Movement of Transport Vehicles on Inter-State 
Routes between Punjab and West Bengal. 


Preamble : 


Whereas an agreement was made _ between the 
Government of West Bengal and the Government of 
Punjab in the month of February 1963, for the 
Operation of road transport services between the 
two States; and 


Whereas the aforesaid agreement expired in the 
month of February 1965, and status quo ante had 
been maintained since then in anticipation of revision 
and renewal of the agreement ; and 


Whereas it is necessary to renew the agreement 
for facilitating the movement of goods between the 
two States and assisting tourists of one State to visit 
the other whenever necessary ; 


Now, therefore, it is hereby agreed between the 
Government of West Bengal and the Government of 
Punjab as follows :— 


1, Preliminary.—TI.. * zreement shall come into 
force immediately after the requirements of publica- 
tion and consideration of representations, envisaged 
under sub-section (3A) of section 63 of the Motor 
Vehicles Act, 1939, are fulfilled and shall be effective 
for a period of five years in the first instance from 
the date it is brought into force. It shall be subject 
to revision every six months or periodically at the 
instance of ejther State. For reasons to be given in 
writing by either State Government, it may be 
revoked on three months’ notice and suspended on 
one month's notice. Such revocation or suspension 
will not, however, affect plying of vehicles covered by: 
a permit already issued and/or ca under 
this agreement. Permanent permits shall be counter- 
signed for the entire period of their validity in spite 
of the fact that such period may extend beyond 
validity of the agreement. 


2. Public Carriers—It is agreed that public 
carrier’s permits for 60 goods vehicles shall be 
countersigned by the Transport Authorities of either 
State. The countersignature shall be valid for the 


390(a) 


390(b) 


entire State permitting operation on all National 
State Highways, only with deviation up to 30 Kilo- 
metres from these roads to reach a manufacturing 
concern or an industrial centre. The countersigna- 
ture so granted shall be subject to the following 
conditions :— 


(a) That such countersigned vehicles shall not 
be engaged طز(‎ intra-State movement of 
goods within the jurisdiction of the counter- 
signing State and shall not pick up such 
goods lying wholly within the jurisdiction 
of the countersigning State. 


(b) That countersignature shall be subject to 
the provisions of section 56 of the Motor 
Vehicles Act. 


3. Private Carriers.—(1) It is agreed that private 
carrier's permits for 10 goods vehicles shall be 
countersigned by the Transport Authorities of 
either State. Such countersignature shall be for the 


entire area of the reciprocating States subjects to, 


the following conditions :— 


(a) Private carriers of 91010 State operating 
under this Agreement shall not ply for hire 
or reward and shall not pick up or set 
down goods within any two points lying 
wholly in the jurisdiction of the counter- 
signing State. 


(b) Goods specified in the private ٥ 
permit only shall be carried. 


(2) Recommendations for the countersignature of 
private carrier’s permits shall be made by the State 
Transport Authority concerned only after it is 
Satisfied from a thorough enquiry that countersigna- 
ture is required for a bona fide private purpose. 


4. Temporary permits.—(A) Public carriers and 
private carriers—Temporary permits for 75 
public carriers and 10 private carriers may be issued 
in a month by the State Transport Authority of 
either State without prior concurrence of the other 
State Transport Authoritv subject to the following 
conditions:— 


(a) The permits shall be issued ما‎ strict 
conformity with the provisions of section 
62 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939. 


(b) The permits shall be valid for a period not 
exceeding 30 days but during this period 
vehicles can perform any number of trips 
between the two States. 


(c) The pecrmits shall be valid for the entire 
State permitting operation on all National 
and State Highways, only with deviation 
up to 30 kilometres from these roads to 
reach a manufacturing concern or an 
industrial centre. 


(d) Copies of temporary permits issued by 
either State Transport Authority shall be 
forwarded forthwith to the other State 
Transport Authority. 


(e) Vehicles of one State shall not pick up or 
Set down goods within any two points lying 
تم‎ in the jurisdiction of the other 

tate.

5. Taxation—The principle of single-point

the movement of motor vehicles through the

Government of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh:— 


(i) Vehicles shall traverse the territories of 
Bihar and Uttar Prodesh through the 
shortest practicable route if no route is 
Specified for the purpose by the Govern- 
merits concerned. 


(ii) Vehicles shall neither pick up nor set down 
goods within Bihar or Uttar Pradesh. 


(iii) The Governments of Bihar and Uttar 
Pradesh shall have the right to prescribe 
the time within which vehicles shall pass 
through their jurisdiction. 


(iv) The Governments of Bihar and Uttar 
Pradesh shall be at liberty to take such 
action as may be permissible under the law 
for any breach of the above conditions ۹ 
of any provision of the law. 


(2) The Governments of West Bengal and Punjab 
shall move the Governments of Bihar and Uttar 
Pradesh for their concurrence to the conditions 
Stated above and for the countersignature, subject 
to these conditions of, permits issued by the two 
State Transport Authorities. 


7. General.—Each State shall accord recognition 
to tax, tokens, registration certificates, certificates 
of fitness of vehicles, conductors, licences, authorisa- 
tions to drive transport vehicles, etc., issued by the 
other State in respect of vehicles operating, or to be 
Operated, on Inter-State routes in accordance with 
this agreement. 


R. P. OJHA, 


Secy. to the Govt. of Punjab, 
Transport Department. 


M. M. KUSARI, 


Transport Commissioner and 
Ex-Officio Secy., Home (Transport) 
Department, Govt. of West Bengal. 


By order of the Governor, 
D. CHAKRABARTI, 
Dy Secy, to the Govt. of West Bengal.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The West Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 (West Ben. Act XX 
of 1949), provides for preparation and not for revision of reoord-of-rights in 
respect of non-agricultural lands and enjoins that the relevant provisions of 
the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 (VIII of 1885), will apply in this regard. The 
Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885, has, however, already been repealed. With a view 
to facilitating revisional settlement operation in respect of non-agricultural lands 
it has, therefore, become necessary to amend the said Act suitably laying down 
the procedure to be followed and, providing for other ancillary matters. It is 
also necessary to remove certain anomalies present in the said Act which are 
related to the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act, 1953 (West Ben. Act I of 
1954), and other Acts. 


2. The Bill has been framed with the above objects in view.

On behalf of tie Company a preliminary objec.

Accordingly, the case was taken up for hearing 
on the preliminary objection raised by the Com- 
pany. The preliminary objection has been taken 
in paragraph | of the Company's written state- 
mcnt and it runs as follows :-— 


“The said firm did not receive any demand in 
wiiting from the workman for reinstnte-

and as such the claim for such reinstate-

Findings, 


It appears that the Company issued a charge. 
sheet io the werkman, dated 4th April 1972 and 
put him wnder suspension pending  enuuiry. 
Subsequently he was dismissed from the service 
with eifect ‘rom 13th June 1972. All these facts 
are admitted on both sides. 


Now, as it appears, that over the suspension 
of the workman the Union raised a dispute with 
the management by their letter, dated 1401 June 
1972 (Ext. B). Earlier the workman personally 
raised a ‘leinand with the management over his 
suspension hy his letter, dated 10th June 1972 
(Ext. fF). There were also conciliation procced- 
ings before the Labour Commissioner over the sus- 
pension of the workman, during the pendency of 
which the werkman was dismissed from the service 
with effect from 13th June 1972. The issue under 
reference telates to the termination of employment 
of the concerned worhman, or in other words, his 
dismissal from service. 


The question is whether any dispute was raised 
with the management either by the workman 
fiimself or by the Union on his behalf regarding 
the dismissal, before the matter was referred to 
the Labour Commissioner, In paragraph 19 of 
the Unton’s Written Statement, it has been alieged 
that a dispute was raised with the management 
over the dismissal of the workman by a letter, 
dated 22nd june 1972. The Union's case is that 
on 22nd June 1972 the concerned workman along 
with P. W. 2 Panchanan Singh Roy, the Joint 
Secrelary of the Union, went to O. P. W. 2 Sunil 
Kumar Dey, one of the Partners of the Press witit 
4a copy o1 016 letter, dated 22nd June 1972 and 
requested him for the reinstatement of the work- 
man, Sunil iiumar Dey, however, refused to rein- 
slate 1116 workman and also to accept the letter. 
Accordingly, on the very same day, the leffer was 
sent tn the Company by post under certificate of 
posting (vide Exts. 1 and t/a). O. ۲ W. 2 Sunil 
Kumat Dey denied this fact categorically and 
so also 0. 7, W. 1 Anil Kumar Dey, 07 
partner of the Press. Anil Kumar Dey went to

The certificate 01 posting Ext. 1/a, however, shows 
that on 2Zud June 1972 a letter was sem to the 
Press by post. Bul even assuming that the Con-

it was sent to the Company after the dispute in 
question was already referred to the Labour 
Commissioner by the Union. Ext. 8 15 the 
relevant letter, dated 21st June 1972, which was 
sent (0 the Labour Commissioner raising a dis- 
pure 0৮1 the dismissal of the concerned workman. 
The letter is under the signature of Shri 
Panchanan Singh Roy, the Joint Secretary of 
the Union. Shri Singh Roy deposed before me 
as P. W. 2, and on being cross-examined ne stated 
that on 2151 June 1972 he wrote a letter {o the 
Labour Commissioner and Ext, H was thai 10111. 
(Git may be mentioned here that Ext. H was calied 
{or from the Labour Commissioner's Office). 
'f is neither the evidence of the workman nor 01 
Shri Panchanan Singh Roy that before 22nd June 
1972 any diSpute was raised with the management 
either verbally or in writing over the dismissal 
of the concerned workman. On the other iiund the 
evidence adduced before me will show that over 
the aismissal of the workman the first dispule that 
was allegedly raised with the management was 
on 2200 June 1972 and not earlier than that. But 
as we have already seen, that on 2151 June 1972 
a dispute over the dismissal of the concerned 
workman had already been raised with the [.apour 
Commissioner (Ext. H) so, it is clear that béfore 
the dispute was raised with the Labour Commis 
sioner, no dispute was raised with the manage 
ment and if at all any dispute was raised willi the 
management it was after the reference of the 
matie: to the Labour Commissioner. This clearly 
brings the case within the mischief of the Sindhu 
Resetilement Corporation Case as_ repouried in 
1965 1 L. ہا‎ J. 834 where it has been laid duwn 
by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that a mere demand 
co এ Government without the dispute being’ raised 
by the workmen with their employer cannot be- 
come an Industrial Dispute. The view taken by thie, 
Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above case was also 
accepied by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in a 
case reported in 1970 F L. R. Vol. 20 page 343 
where jit has been laid down that a demand by the. 
workmen must be raised at first on the manage- 
ment and rejected by them before an industrial 
dispute can be said to arise an exist and thai the 
making of such a demand to the conciliation ofticer 
and its Communication by him to the management, 
who rejects the same, is not sufficient to consiitute 
an industrial dispute. 


That being so, it must be held that the present, 
dispute bas not assumed the character of an ہا‎ 
dustrial Dispute. 


The learncd Lawyer appearing on behalf of the 
Union referred me to a decision of the Hon'ble 
Patna High Court as reported in A, I. R. 1970 
Patna 295, in support of his contention that a 
demand and a refusal o! it are not always neces- 
sary to make a dispute an industrial dispute 
The Hon'ble Patna High Court, as I find. di 
not lay down any general principle contrary to 


PART IC] THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, FEBRUARY 27, 1974 29402) 
SS লস ললঙ জল Sere 


the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supremc 
Court in Sindhu Re-settlement Corporation’s case. 
The Hon'ble Court simply observed that in the 
[8015 of the case before it any specific demand 
to tie management and its refusal by it was not 
necessary. There, the workmen put forward a 
den:and before the management requesting the 
management to allow them to work, put the 
management would not allow them to work. The 
resultant of this dispute was an industrial dispute 
75:10 the alleged lock-out. The Hon'ble Court 
observed that in the aforesaid circumstances no 
further demand of that dispute was necessary. 
But here, the facts are entirely different. The 
concetned workman raised a dispute with the 
manugement over his suspension but no dispule 
was raised over his dismissal, which is now 1115 
issue before us. That being so, the case clearly 
comes within the mischief of the Sindhu ۰ 
ment Corporation's case. 


‘Thus, on a consideration of the facts and cir- 
cuinstances stated above, it must be held that the 
dispute under reference has not assumed the 
character of an industrial dispute, inasmuch as no 


Carlicr dispute was raised with the management 
vefore the matter was taken up ein oe 


Commissioner for conciliation. 


The reicrence should, therefore, be held to be 
had in law and as such it is not necessary to 
entcr into the merits of the case. 


The preliminary objection taken by the Com- 
pany accordingly succeeds. 


This is my award.

fitteen Commissioners of Khardah 7৮1 1n 
the district of 24-Parganas had been so long

including the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman 
have now tendered resignation ; 


And whereas in the circumstances, the Governor 
is of the opinion that the affairs of the said 
Municipality cannot be managed in accordance 
With law; 


And whereas the Governor is further of the 
opinion that 16 1s desirable in the public interest 
to appoint an Executive Officer to carry on the 
administration of the said Municipality ;

conferred by sub-section (1) ofsection 67A of

of 1982) the Governor is pleased hereby 09 
declare that the said Municipality shall have an 
Fixecutnve Officer for a period up to the 30th June, 
1974, with effect from the date on which the 
Executive (Officer may assume charge of his office.

Government of West Bengal 
HOME DEPARTMENT 
Transport 
NOTIFICATION 


No. 2224-W.T./6R-14/73.—26th February 1!974.—In exercise of the 
power conferred by section 68 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Act 4 of 
1939), the Governor is pleased to make, after previous publication as required 
by sub-section (1) of section 133 of the said Act, the following amendments 
in the Bengal Motor Vehicles Rules, 1940, published with notification No. 
1930PI., dated the 2151 September 1940, at pages 2655-2829 of Part I of the 
“Calcutta Gazette” of the 10th October 1940, as subsequently amended 
(hereinafter referred to as the said rules), namely: 


Amendments 
In the said rules,— 


(1) in rule 2, after clause (n), insert the following clauses, namely :— 


“(o) ‘composite permit’ means a permit issued under section 56 of the 
Act, in respect of a public carrier goods vehicle for operation 
on National Highways and State Highways passing through, or 
terminating in, the State of West Bengal and other States and 
Union Territories in pursuance of a Special Reciprocal 
Agreement entered into by the State of West Bengal with other 
States and Union Territories; 


(p) ‘Special Reciprocal Agreement’ means an agreement entered ٥۵ 
by the State of West Bengal with other States and Union 
Territories for the purpose of issuing composite permits under 
section 56 of the Act by the State Transport Authority or a 
Regional Transport Authority of any of the signatory States to 

romote long distance and inter-State transport of goods by road 
tween those States and Union Territories ; 


304(1) 


39402) THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY FEBRUARY 28, 1974 


EEN Si SS ہے _ سہ ہے _ سس‎ ১১ ০০০ 
© tore = os سےمہے‎ ee Rn গা 


(q) ‘signatory State’ means a State or a Union Territory which 15 a 
party to a Special Reciprocal Agreement.”; 


(2) after rule 63, insert the following rule, namely : 


“63A. Grant of composite permits: (1) The State Transport Authority, 
West Bengal, shall be the competent authority to issue composite permits. 


(2) A composite permit issued by the State Transport Authority or a 
Regional Transport Authority of any of the signatory States other than the 
State of West Bengal shall be valid in the State of West Bengal without 
countersignature of the Regional Transport Authorities or the State Transport 
Authority of the State of West Bengal. 


(3) A composite permit shall be granted only ا٦‎ relation to a_ public 
carrier goods vehicle,— 


(a) which at the time of grant is not more than two years old reckoned 
from the date of its first registration as new; and 


(b) which has a registered laden weight of not less than 10,000 Kgs. 


(4) An authorisation under a Special Reciprocal Agreement in the Form 
SRA-AUTH shall be granted to every public carrier goods vehicle, in 
respect of which a composite permit is issued under the signature and seal 
of the competent authority of the State of West Bengal on an application 
made in writing in the Form SRA-AUTH-A. 


(5) The following shall be the conditions of every composite permit: 


(a) While operating in any area outside the State of West Bengal, goods 
shall not be picked up or set down between any two points lying 
wholly within the jurisdiction of the reciprocating States, i-.e., in 
such cases the vehicle shal] be prohibited from carrying any intra- 
State business. 


(b) The vehicle shall be painted in the colour specified by the State 
Transport Authority, West Bengal, at the time of issuing the 
permit and shall carry special markings to be similarly specified. 
A board showing the following inscription shall be carried 
prominently in front of the vehicle at the top above the ‘PUBLIC 
CARRIER’ board, the colour of the letters and the background 
being specified by the State Transport Authority, West Bengal, at 
the time of issuing the permit: 


Inscription 


COMPOSITE PERMIT 


(Under Special Reciprocal Agreemenf) 
51100 187 مم امم‎ 


(*Here write the names of the States 
and Union Territories applicable) 


REESE FS cee i উস eT 


(c) Each vehicle covered by a composite permit shall have two drivers. 
The vehicle shall be provided with a seat across the full width 
of the vehicle, behind the driver’s seat, providing facility for the 
spare driver to stretch himself and sleep. 


(d) The vehicle shall at all times carry Bill/Bills of Lading in Form SRA- 
LAD. The goods conveyed shall be in conformity with the 
declaration in the Bill/Bills of Lading. 


(e) Quarterly returns in Form SRA-QLY shall be submitted by the 
permit-holder to the Secretary, State Transport Authority, West 
Bengal, with as many copies 25 may be specified at the time 
issuing the permit by the State Transport Authority, to reach 
him not later than the 30th day of the month succeeding the 
quarter concerned.
