87. Penalty for confravention of any order regarding requisition.—If any 
person contravenes any order made under rule 82 or rule 85 he shall, on convic- 
tion, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year 
or with fine which may extend to rupees one thousand or with both. 


88. Promoting enmity between different classes in connection with election. 
—Any person who in connection with an election under these rules promotes 
or attempts to promote on grounds of religion, race, caste, community or language 
feelings of enmity or hatred between different classes or citizens of India shall 
on conviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to 
one year, or with fine which may extend to rupees one thousand or with both. 


89. Prohibition of public meetings on day before or on day of election.— 
(1) No person shall convene, hold or attend any public meeting within any 
constituency within twenty-four hours before the date of commencement of the 
poll or on the date or dates on which a poll is taken for an election in that 
constituency. 


(2) Any person who contravenes the provision of sub-rule (1) shall, on convic- 
tion, be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees. 


90. Prohibition of canvassing in or near polling stations—{1) No person 
shall, on the date or dates on which a poll is taken at any polling station, commit 
any of the following acts within the polling station or in any public or private 
place within a distance of one hundred metres of the polling station, namely :— 


(a) canvassing for votes; or 

(b) soliciting the vote of any voter; or 

(c) persuading any voter not to vote for any particular candidate; or 

(d) persuading any voter not to vote at the election; or 

(e) exhibiting any notice or sign (other than an official notice) relating to 
the election. 


(2) Any person who contravenes the provisions of sub-rule (1) shall, on 
eonviction, be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty 


rupees. 
(3) An offence punishable under this rule shall be cognizable. 


91. Penalty for disorderly conduct in or near polling stations.—(1) No 
persons shell, on the date or dates on which a poll is taken, at any polling 
station— 


(a) use or operate within or at the entrance of the polling station. or in 
any public or private place in the neighbourhood thereof, any 
apparatus for amplifying or reproducing the human voice, such as 
a meghaphone or loudspeaker; or 


(b) shout, or otherwise act in a disorderly manner, within or at the entrance 
of the polling station or in any public or private place in the 
neighbourhood thereof, so as to cause annoyance to any person 
visiting the polling station for the poll, or so as to interfere with 
the work of the officers and other persona on duty at the polling 
station. 


(2) Any person who contravenes, or wilfully aids or abets the contravention 
of the provisions of sub-rule (1) shall, on conviction, be punished with fine 
which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees. 


(3) If the Presiding Officer of a polling station has reason to believe that 
any سس‎ is committing or has committed an offence punishable under this 
rule he may direct any police officer to arrest such person, and thereupon the 
police officer shall arrest him. 


(4) Any police officer may take such steps and use such force, as may be 
reasonably necessary for preventing any contravention of the provisions of sub- 
rule (1) and may seize any apparatus used for such contraventions.

92. Penalty for misconduct at polling stations —({1) Any person who during 
the hours fixed for the poll at any polling station misconducts himself or fails 
to obey the lawful direction of the Presiding Officer may be removed from the 
polling station by the Presiding Officer or by any police officer on duty or by 
any person, authorised in this behalf by such Presiding Officer. 


(2) The powers conferred by sub-rule (1) shall not be exercised so as to 
prevent any voter who is otherwise entitled to vote at a polling station from 
having an opportunity of voting at that station. 


(3) If any person who has been so removed from a polling station re-enters 
the polling station without the permission of the Presiding Officer, he ehall, on 
conviction, be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty 
rupees. 


(4) An offence punishable under sub-rule (3) shall be cognizable. 


93. Officers, etc., at elecsion not to act for candidates or influence voting.— 
(1) No person who is a Returning Officer, or an Assistant Returning Officer 
or a Presiding Officer or polling officer at an election or an officer or clerk 
appointed by the Returning Officer or the Presiding Officer to perform any duty 
in connection with an election shall, in the conduct or the management of the 
election, do any act (other than the giving of his vote) for the furtherance of 
the prospects of the election of a candidate. 


(2) No such person as aforesaid, and no member or a police force, shall 
endeavour— 


(a) to persuade any person to give his vote at an election, or 
(b) to dissuade any person from giving his vote at an election, or 
(c) to influence the voting of any person at an election in any manner. 


(3) Any person who contravenes the provisions of sub-rule (1) or sub-rule (2) 
shall, on conviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may 
extend to six months or with fine which may extend to rupees five hundred or 
with both. 


(4) An offence under sub-rule (3) shal] be cognizable. 


94. Breaches of official duty in connection with election.—(1) If any person 
to whom this rule applies is without reasonable cause guilty of any act or 
omission in breach of his official duty, he shall, on conviction, be punished with 
fine which may extend to five hundred rupees. 


(2) An offence punishable under sub-rule (1) shall be cognizable. 


(3) No suit or other legal টি shall lie against any such person for 
damages in respect of any such act or omission as aforesaid. 


(4) The persons to whom this rule applies are the Returning Officers, Assistant 
Returning Officers, Presiding Officers, polling officers and any other persons 
appointed to perform any duty in connection with the maintenance of list of 
voters, the receipt of nominations or withdrawal of candidatures, or the recording 
or counting of votes at an election and the expression “official duty” shall, for 
the purposes of this rule, be construed accordingly, but shall not include duties 
imposed otherwise than by or under this Act. 


95. Penalty for Government servants for acting as election agent, polling 
agent or counting agent.—If any person in the service of the Government acts 
as an election agent or a polling agent or a counting agent of a candidate 
at an election, he shall, on corviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term 
which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to five hundred 
rupees. 


96. Removal of ballot paper from polling station to be offences.—(1) Any 
person who at any election fraudulently takes, or attempts to take a ballot 
paper out of a polling station or wilfully aids or abets the doing of any such 
act, shall, on conviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may 
extend to one year or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or 
with both.

(2) If the Presiding Officer of a polling station has reason to believe that 
any person 15 committing or has committed an offence punishable under sub- 
rule (1), such officer may, before such person leaves the polling station, arrest 
or direct a police officer to arrest such person and may search such person or 
cause him to be searched by a police officer : 


Provided that when it is necessary to cause a woman to be searched the 
search shall be made by another woman with strict regard to decency. 


(3) Any ballot paper found upon the person arrested on search shall be made 
over for safe custody to a poe officer by the Presiding Officer, or when the 
search is made by a Police Officer, shall be kept by such officer in safe custody. 


(4) An offence punishable under sub-rule (1) shall be cognizable. 


97. Other offences and penalties therefor—(1) A person shall be guilty 
of an electoral offence if at any election he— 


(a) fraudulently defaces or fraudulently destroys any nomination paper; or 


(b) fraudulently defaces, destroys or removes any list, notice or other 
document affixed by or under the authority of a Returning Officer; 
or 


(c) fraudulently defaces or fraudulently destroys any ballot paper or the 
official mark on any ballot paper; or any official envelope used ia 
connection with voting by voters on election duty; or 

{d) without due authority supplies any ballot paper to any person or 
receives any ballot paper from any person or is in possession of 
any ballot paper; or 

(6) fraudulently puts into ballot box anything other than the ballot paper 
which he is authorised by law to put in; or 


(f) without due authority destroys, takes, opens or otherwise interferes with 
any bollot box or ballot papers then in use for the purposes of the 
election; or 

(g) fraudulently or without due authority, as the case may be, attempts 
to do any of the foregoing acts or wilfully aids or abets the doing 
of any such acts. 


(2) Any person guilty of an offence under this rule, shall— 


(a) if he is a Returning Officer, an Assistant Returning Officer or a Presiding 
Officer at a polling station or any other officer or clerk employed 
on official duty in connection with the election, on conviction, be 
punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one 
ae or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or with 

th. 


(b) if he is any other person, on conviction, be punished with imprisonment 
for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may 
extend to two hundred and fifty rupees or with both. 


(3) For the purposes of this rule a person shall be deemed to be on official 
duty if his duty is to take part in the conduct of an election or part of an 
election including the counting of votes or to be responsible after an election 
for the used bailot papers and other documents in connection with such election, 
but the expression “official duty” shall not include any duty imposed otherwise 
than by or under these rules. 


(4) An offence punishable under sub-rule (2) shall be cognizable. 


98. Maintenance of secrecy of voting. —(1) Every Officer, clerk, agent or 
other person who performs any duty in connection with the recording or count- 
ing of votes at an election shall maintain, and aid in maintaining, the secrecy 
of voting and shall not (except for some purpose authorised by or under any 
law) communicate to any person any information calculated to violate such 


secrecy. 


(2) Any person who contravenes the provisions of sub-rule (1) shall, on 
conviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to thres 
months or with fine which may extend to rupees five hundred or with both.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


For the proper development of the body and the soul, the labour, like any 
other human being, are required to inculcate a spirit of healthy community and 
socia! life, and for this, it is necessary for them to have reasonable scope and 
opportunity for various forms of recreation and entertainment, games ana 
sports, excursions, tours and other activities of corporate nature. The need 
was being felt for long for constituting a statutory Labour Welfare Fund with 
a view to promoting the aforesaid activities and other forms of welfare for the 
labour and their dependants. The matter was considered by the Committee on 
Labour Welfare set up by the Central Government, and this committce 
recommended setting up of statutory Labour Welfare Fund under a tripartite 
board in each State for promoting labour welfare in the appropriate manner. 
In the States like Maharashtra, Punjab, Gujarat and বির statutes for this 
purpose have already been enacted. This Government also propose to accept 
the recommendation of the aforesaid committee and hence this Bill providing 
for constitution of a Labour Welfare Fund under a tripartite board to be 
utilised for specified labour welfare measures. At the initial stage, the factories, 
tramways, motor transport undertakings and commercial establishments employ- 
ing not less than ten persons are proposed to be covered, but powers are 
conferred on the State Government to extend the statute to other establish- 
ments by order. 


CALCUTTA, GOPAL DAS NAG, 
The 6th February, 1974. Member-in-charge. 
FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM. 


In terms of sub-clause (2) of clause 9 of the Bill the State Government is 
required to contribute to the Labour Welfare Fund to be constituted under sub- 
clause (7) of clause 3 thereof at the rate of Re. 1! per annum for every workman 
employed in an “establishment”. The total number of employees working in 
“establishments” covered by the Bill, in terms of clause 2(5) thereof, is com- 

uted to be about 11 lakhs. The total amount of annual expenditure from the 
tate Exchequer is, therefore, likely to be about Rs. 11 lakhs. This will be a 
recurring expenditure and will vary according to rise or fall in the number of 


employees. 

2. Under clauses 15 and 16 of the Bill Government will appoint a Welfare 
Commissioner and some Inspectors. No precise estimate of expenditure on 
this account is possible at this stage. lf and when any expenditure on_ this 
account is incurred for administration of the legislation when enacted, State 
Government shall go to the Legislature through normal budget for sanctioning 
the necessary expenditure. 

CALCUTTA, GOPAL DAS NAG, 


The 6th February, 1974. Member-in-charge.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


It has become necessary to amend the West Bengal Land Reforms Act, 
1955, to provide for— 
(a) maintenance and preservation of orchards ; 


(b) enlargement of the definition of “irrigated area” so that fresh lands 
coming under irrigation after 1377 B.S. as also lands irrigated by 
State river-lift irrigation projects can come under the definition ; 


(c) determination of the ceiling area in respect of a trust or institution 
of a public nature, established exclusively for a charitable or 
religious purpose or both by taking into account the number of 
its centres or branches established prior to the 7th August, 1969, 
the date referred to in section 147 ; 


(d) minimising the scope of vesting of portions of plots in the State ; 


(e) exclusive jurisdiction of the officer or authority mentioned in sub- 
section (J) of section 18 to decide the question as to whether a 
person is or is not a bargadar so that cultivation by a bargadar 
cannot be terminated through recourse to Civil or Criminal Courts; 


(f) partial application of the provisions of section 23B to the hilly 
portions of the district of Darjeeling so that while small raiyats 
owning not more than 1.214 hectares of land on a family basis 
will get the benefit of exemption from revenue, there will not be 
any re-assessment of revenue under that section in cases of those 
raiyats who are not so exempted ; 


(g) withdrawal of restrictions imposed on attachment and sale of movable 


properties and of immovable propertics other than homestead in 
execution of certificates for recovery of arrears of revenue ; 


(h) splitting up of mixed khatians comprising agricultural and non- 
agricultural lands so as to constitute separate holdings or tenancies, 
as the case may be, apportionment of the revenue or rent on the 
basis of area, recording of a non-agricultural tenant holding 
agricultural land as a raiyat and preparation of record-of-rights 
on one man-one mauza-one khatian basis ; 


(i) bar to the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters relating to alteration 
of any entry in the finally published record-of-rights; and 


(j) other ancillary matters. 
2. The Bill has been framed with the above objects in view. 


CALCUTTA, GURU PADA KHAN, 
The 5th March, 1974. Member-in-charge. 


FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM. 


Clause 8 of the Bill seeks to extend special concession to the rdiyats in the 
hilly portion of the district of Darjeeling. There will be no re-assessment of 
revenue and no surcharge will be required to be paid. The raiyats who are not 
exempted from paying revenue will continue to pay revenue at the same rate 
at which it was payable immediately before commencement of the West 
Bengal Land Reforms (Second Amendment) Act, 1969. The amount of 
additional revenue which would have been available had the revenue in the 
hilly areas been re-assessed, fannot be estimated correctly as no such ire- 
assessment had actually been done. It is, however, expected that the loss in 
the anticipated revenue in the hilly areas of Darjeeling would be more or less 
compensated as a result of enlargement of the definition of “irrigated area” 
proposed to be made by clause 3 of the Bill and consequent re-assessment of 
revenue in such areas. 


CALCUTTA, GURU PADA KHAN, 
The 5th March, 1974. Member-in-charge.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The object of the Bill is, inter alia, to enhance different rates of fees under 
the West Bengal Lifts and Escalators Act, 1955 (West Ben. Act V of 1955), 
so as to cover the expenditure of the Lifts and Escalators Wing of the Direc- 
torate of Electricity, West Bengal, as the fees realised under the said Act 
during the last decade fell far short of the expenditure incurred in connection 
with the administration of the said Act. The amendments proposed in_ the 
Bill are made in such a way that for further enhancement of fees in future, 
subsequent amendment of the Act itself would not be necessary and only 
modification of the rules thereunder would suffice. 


The Bill also seeks to amcnd the present Act to provide for conversion 
of Food Pound Second Unit used in the said Act into Centimetre Gram 
Second Unit as required in terms of the West Bengal Standards of Weights 
and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1958 (West Ben. Act XXIII of 1958). 


A. B. A. GHANI KHAN CHOUDHURY, 
Member-in-charge. 


CALCUTTA, 
The 27th February, 1974. 


FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM. 


The revised rates of different tees are expected to yield not only the 
present expenditure but are also expected to yield a surplus of Rs. 16,000 per 
annum which would meet the cost of future expansion of the activities of the 
Lifts and Escalators Wing of the Directorate of Elcctricity, West Bengal 


A. B. A. GHANI KHAN CHOUDHURY, 
Member-in-charge.

the proviso to Article 309 of the Constitution of India, the Governor is pleased 
to direct that the following amendments shall be made in the West Bengal 
Serviccs (Revision of Pay and Allowance) Rules, 1970, published with Finance 
Department Notification No, 5212-F., dated the 30th December 1970, as amended 
trom time to time, namely— 


Amendments 


In Schedule J, Part B, to the said rules the following modifications shall be 
made :-— 


(1) In Departments having Engineering cadres there shall be an_ inter- 
mediate Selection Grade on Rs. 825—50—875—60—1,415 a: 15 
per cent. of the cadre of Assistant Engineers in the existing revised 
scale of Rs. 475—30—685—35—1,000—50—1,150. 


(2) There shall also be an intermediate Selection Grade on Rs. 1,535—60— 
1,775 at 10 per cent. of the cadre of Executve Engineers in he 
existing revised scale of Rs. 825—50—875—60—1,475. 


(3) In the cadre of Sub-Assistant Engineers in the scale of Rs. 300—10— 
420—15—600 with higher initial start at Rs. 330 per month, there 
shall also be a Selection Grade at 10 per cent. of the cadre in the 
scale of Rs. 425—15—500—20—700—25—825. 


(4) Sub-Assistant:Engineers having Engineering degree shall have an initial 
start in the existing scale of Rs. 300—600 at the stage of Rs. 360 
per month. They will also get the benefit of age relaxation for direct 
recruitment either through the Public Service Commission or for ad 
hoc appointments.

Rules

2. Notwithstanding anything contained in any rules relating to pay and 
recruitment to any of the services mentioned hereunder, the West Bengal Junior 
Civil Service (Executive), the West Bengal Junior Commercial Tax Service, the 
West Bengal Junior Agricultural Income-tax Service, the West Bengal Junior 
Excise Servicc and the West Bengal Jun‘or Educational Service shall each form 
a single service with the corresponding State Service with a senior scale of 
Rs. 475—30—685—35—1,000—-50—1,150 and a junior scale of Rs. 425—15—

the Senior Scale after six years of service in the Junior Scale provided their

Scale will be fixed therein under the provisions of rule 42(1)(i) of West Bengal 
Service Rules, Part I, increased by one increment in the Senior Scale.

in any way affect the interests of the candidates who are already under recruitment

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
LABOUR DEPARTMENT 
NOTIFICATION 


No. 1117-I.R./EIL/1A-6/74.—22nd February 1974.—Whereas the Governor 
is of opinion that employment in the Engineering factories in West Bengal 
employing 10 to 49 workmen (hereinafter referred to as the said employment), 


is essential for maintaining supplies and services essential to the life of the 
community; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred by sub-rule (1) of 
Rule 119 of the Defence of India Rules, 1971, (hereinafter referred to as the 
said Rules), the Governor is pleased hereby to declare the said employment 


to be an employment to which Rule 119 of the Defence of India Rules, 1971, 
applies. 


ORDER 


No. 1118-I.R./EIL|1A-6/74. — 22nd February 1974. — Whereas by the 
Government of West Bengal, Labour Department Notification No. 1117-LR., 
dated the 22nd February 1974 under sub-rule (1) of Rule 119 of the Defence 
of India Rules, 1971 (hereinafter referred to as the said Rules), employment 
in the Engineering factories m West Bengal employing 10 to 49 workmen 
(hereinafter referred to as the said employment), has been declared to be an 
employment to which Rule 119 of the said Rules apply; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred by sub-rule (4) of 
Rule 119 of the said Rules, the Governor is pleased to regulate basic wages 
and dearness allowance in respect of persons who are workmen as defined in 
clause (s) of Section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Act 14 of 1947), 
and are engaged in such employment (hereinafter referred to as the said work- 
men), in the manner indicated in the Annexure attached hereto.

it is found that there was no clear abseuce of

exclude the two intervening Sundays and also 25th

It is not a case of absence without permission, not 
exceeding eight consecutive days which constitite 
a major misdemeanour according to the Standing. 
Orders. The workman has not been charged witir 
Such a misdemeanour and also not subjected to 
any €nquity prescribed for the purpose. The 
learned Counsel for the Company placed before 
me a certain decision of the Hon'ble High Court 


at Calcutta arising out of Civil Rule No. 773(W) 


of 70. The facts of that case were however 
altogether different. In that case the workman 
went On leave disobeying the employer's direction 
to appear before a Medical Board and therefore, 
obviously against the order of refusal of that leave. 
So, that case does not help the Company before 
me in this case. 


It cannot but therefore be concluded that there 
has not been any automatic termination of 
employment for any unauthorised absence of

more than 10 days in the inStant case, as efro- 
neously communicated by the employer by their

has not, therefore, lost his lien in the service or 
his right to get reinstatement with back wages. 


Before conclusion, it should, however, be noted 
that the contention of the Union that the Standing 
Order is not applicable to this as not being the 
Standing Orders of the Company has no force in 
if. The Standing Order shows that this is also 
the Company's Standing Order. The 10118 
Ext, ٣. which is duly certified, shows that the 
Company in reference iS a member-firm of the 
Engineering Association. The testimony of the 
Personne] Officer Mr. Prosad also shows that. 
Clause (4) Of section 3 Of the Industrial Banploy- 
ment Standing Orders Act also enjoins that a group 
of employers of a similar establishment may 
submit a joint draft of Standing Orders, as in the 
instant case, and section 13A of the said Act also 
provides for clarification fegarding Standing 
Orders at the instance of either the employer or

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS, 


The present Bill seeks to amend the Bengal Finance (Sales Tax) Act, 
1941, and the West Bengal Sales Tax Act, 1954, with a view to imposing 
an additional surcharge on dealers under the said Acts, having certain 
higher turnover and also proposes to effect certain minor amendments in 
the Bengal Finane (Sales Tax) Act, 1941, in relation to exempted goods. 


No additional expenditure is envi-aged to give effect to the provisions 
of the 13111.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


Under section 66 of the Bengal Municipal Act, 1932, the municipalities 1n 
the State had the absolute power of creating posts where the salary or the 
maximum of the pay scale did not exceed Rs. 200 per month and of making 
appointments thereto without the sanction of Government. Though _ the 
municipalities were mostly over-staffed and running deficits, they frequently 
recruited additional hands by creating new posts without any regard for their 
financial stringency. Again, according to the judgment passed by the Calcutta 
High Court in 1971, the municipalities had also the power, under the said 
section, of revising the pay scales of their employees without the sanction of 
Government. Some municipalities had since revised the pay scales of their 
employees in such a way that their emoluments had been raised out of all 
proportions to the paying capacities of these local bodies. Thirdly, municipa- 
lities used to grant special pays and allowances at varying rates to their staff 
without any rational basis and thereby had been increasing their financial 
liabilities. And, lastly, by way of Puja relief, these local bodics had been making 
large scale ex-gratia payments annually to their employees notwithstanding the 
fact that there is no provision for making such ex-gratia grants in the Bengal 
Municipal Act, 1932 and that the municipaliti¢és have no money for the purpose. 
Further, to meet the increasing demands of employees for larger ex-gratia pay- 
ments every year, the municipalities had been forced to divert Development 


Grants and other funds. These local bodies, on their own, are unable to stop 
or control such financially ruinous practices. 


By using their legal powers widely and through imprudent financial manage- 
ment, as explained above, the municipalities had themselves brought about 
their financial doom. Disproportionately large expenditure on staff establish- 
ment which consumes most of the income of the municipalities, is their main 
financial trouble which renders them incapable of undertaking development 
works and providing due civic services to the rate-payers in spite of substantial 


financial assistance from the Government in the shape of subventions, grants 
and loans. 


2. In the above context, Government considered it necessary in the public 
interest as well as in the interest of financial stability of the municipalities that 
the powers of creating any posts or revising the pay scales of the municipal 
employees or of granting special pays or allowances including ex-gratia pay- 


ments to the municipal staff should be subjected to prior sanction of Govern- 
ment so that all municipal funds might not be 


unnecessarily spent on staff 
but a portion be utilized fer the benefit of civic population. The Bengal 
Municipal (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (West Bengal Ordinance No. XII of 
1973), was promulgated by the Governor and published on 150 December, 1973, 
to meet the purpose. 


The object of the present Bill is to continue the provisions of the said 
Ordinance. 


CALCUTTA, SUBRATA MUKHOPADHAYA, 
The 14th March, 1974.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS, 


The main objective of the Comprehensive Area Development Project is to 
bring about total development of agriculture and other allied matters 
including cottage industries of the State in a planned and phased manner in 
order to increase the production of agriculture, dairy, poultry, fishery and 
cottage industries, thereby removing the poverty of the villagers, attain 
economic self-sufficiency of the area and revitalise the rural economy of West 
Bengal. It is also the objective of the Comprehensive Area Development 
Project to ensure maximum benefits of such production to the poorer section 
of the State, such as, small and marginal farmers and also to reduce economic 
disparity amongst different persons. West Bengal is rich in natural resources ; 
there is also huge idle man-power. The objective of the Comprehensive 
Area Development Project is to bring revolution in the rural economy of the 
country by engaging the idle man-power in the utilisation of resources 
hitherto untapped. 


‘he benefits accruing from the programme will be additional yield of 29 
lakh tonnes of clean rice valued at Rs.362 crores and increased production of 
jute, oilseeds, wheat, cotton, etc., through modernisation of agriculture, 
adoption of package of practices, extension of irrigation, and improvement 
of drainage, intensive supply of better inputs, co-ordination of different 
functional agencies and departments of the Government. In order to ensure 
fair and economic price to the cultivators radical improvement will be made 
in marketing, providing infra-structures, such as, roads, bridges and setting 
up of modern warehouses. 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, MARCH 19, 1974 


LS تو‎ ey ir a gg, 5 _— —<—s পপ = —— سے سوب سس سے‎ ০ 4 শট পি ہد‎ পেশি ee ee 
পাস a کھےپہہسمح ۔ کس حجچجمھّ لے ہے مسب چو ہم‎ এ 


An increased yield of 29 lakh tonnes of rice will mean that the deficit 
of the State will not only be wiped out but also there will remain some 
surplus. Dependence of West Bengal on other States for pulses and oilseeds 
will also be minimised. The programme will generate additional full-time 
employment for 8.2 lakh persons. Per capita income of the bottom 70 per 
cent. of the chronically proverty-stricken peasant households composed of 
landless agricultural labourer families, share croppers, etc., owning no land or 
less than 2.6 acres per family will increase by at least 200 per ecnt., thus 
covering the 9 lakh peasant households out of the total of about 12 lakh 
peasant households. By increased production of basic raw materials and 
setting up of a large number of cottage industries and opening of service 
centres, it will be possible to evolve a far closer union between industry and 
agriculture. The entire socio-economic picture of the villagers is also likely 
to change. The massive indebtedness of the agriculturists will be reduced to 
the minimum by opening Debt Settlement Boards, which will settle all 
outstanding debts. 


2. The method envisaged for such radical transformation is entirely 
democratic. This State, the district and the project level bodies will formulate 
the policies and implement them for attaining these objectives. The District 
Planning Committees, Zilla Parishads, the District Magistrates, Principal 
Agricultural Officers and the Block Development Officers all have been 
involved in the programme by associating them closely with these committees. 
For this purpose they have been equipped with adequate powers which 
include capacity to borrow money from the financial institutions. The Project 
Director, who will be in-charge of the block of 10,000 acres will be the 
nucleus of the programme. He will have sufficient powers to ensure that the 
farmers follow the pattern of agricultural programme and utilise the 
resources placed at the disposal of the farmers and that full advantage of the 
improved infra-structure is taken. 


3. The main strategy of the programme is to select compact blocks of 
10,000 acres each by stages to cover the entire State gradually. The expenses 
for the District and State Level Organisations as well as the Project Head- 
quarters will be borne by the Government in the initial five years. Invest- 
ment per block of 10,000 acres will be approximately Rs.2.30 crores.

FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM. 


It is proposed to establish for the State of West Bengal a Corporation 
called ‘The West Bengal Comprehensive Area Development Corporation’. 
The Corporation shall be responsible for drawing up and implementation of 
projects for comprehensive development of selected areas in the State with a 
view to increasing agricultural production and improving animal husbandry, 
dairy, poultry, etc. and extension of cottage industries and ensuring maximum 
benefits to the cultivatora and other poorer section of the rural people. 


2. The Corporation shall consist of a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and 
a number of other members not exceeding 25 one of whom shall be appointed 
as the Executive Vice-Chairman (Chief Executive Officer). The Corporation, 
in its turn, shall constitute for each district Comprehensive Area Develop- 
ment Council with a view to siding and advising the Corporation with regard 
to the projects undertaken in the district. For each project there shall be a 
Project Director and an Advisory Board to 19 appointed by the Corporation. 
The Project Director shall be in overal!] and immediate charge of implementa- 
tion of a project. 


3. Under clause 12 of the Bill there is provision for the State Govern- 
ment to make grants and advance loans to the Corporation for the purpose 
of this Act from time to time.

The Hooghly River Bridge Act, 1969, was enacted in order to provide for 
the construction, maintenunce and control of bridges across the r.ver 


Hooghly falling within the hmits of the Port of Calcutta. 


With a view to facilitate acquisition of land for purpose of construction 
of Second Bridge over river Hooghly, the Hooghly River Bridge (Amendment) 
Ordinance, 1973 (West Bengal Ordtnance No. XV of 1973), was promulgated 


by the Governor on the 28th December, 1973. 
The Bill seeks to enact the provisions of the said Ordinance.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


At present the members of the State Legislative Assembly are entitled to 
various .allowances for enabling them to discharge their duties as such 
‘members. 


2. As the existing facilities including their salaries are considered 
inadequate, it has been proposed to give each member an additional allowance 
termed as compensatory allowance at the rate of rupees two hundred per 
month. 


3. The Bengal Legislative Assembly (Members’ EKmoluments) 
(Amendment) Bill, 1974, has been drafted with this object in view. 


G. 5. SOHANPAL, 
Member-in-charge. 
CaLCUTTA, 
The 20th March, 1974. 


FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM. 


With a view to giving all members of the West Bengal Legislative 
Assembly a compensatory allowance at the rate of Rs.200 per month it is 
proposed to amend the Bengal [eyislative Assembly (Members’ Emoluments) 
Act, 1937 (Ben. Act IT of 1937). Accordingly an amendment Bill has been 
prepared. 


There are at present 281 members in the West Bengal Legislative 
Assembly including one nominated by the Governor in terms of article 333 
of the Constitution of India. Among them there are 26 Ministers, Ministers 
of State and Deputy Ministers and one Speaker and one Deputy Speaker. 
These persons do not come under the purview of the Act in question. So the 
total financial implication in view of the proposed amendment per year is 
(253 × 12 x 200) = R3.6,07,200.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
HOME DEPARTMENT 


Transport 
NOTIFICATION 


No. 3282-W.T.—20th March 1974.—In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (3B) of section 63 of the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Act 4 of 1939), the Governor is pleased hereby to publish the following Reciprocal Agreemont 
for the North Zone Permit Scheme for goods vehicles covering the States of Bihar, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, 
Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Preadesh and West Bongal and the Union Territories of Chandigarh 
wnd Delhi, after its previous publication as required by sub-section (3A) of the said section, und to direct’ that the 
StateWransport Authority, West Bengal, shall give effeot to it. 


Agreement 


This agreement made this 3lst day of December one thousand nine hundred and seventy-three between the Go- 
vernor of Bihar of the one Part, the Governor of Haryana of the second Part, the Governor of Himachal Pradesh of 
the third Part, the Govornor of Jammu and Kashmir of tho fourth Part, the Governor of Punjab of the fifth Part, the 
Govegnor of Rajasthan of the siath Part, the Governor of Uttar Pradesh of the seventh Part, the Governor of West 
Bengal of the eighth Part, the Presidont of India for and on behalf of the Union Territory of Chandigarh of the 
ninth Part, the President of India for and on behalf of the Umon Territory of Delhi of the tenth Part. 


WHEARAS it is expedient in view of the rapid economic development of the country to oncourage the long dis- 
tance and inter-State transport of goods by road and whereas it is necessary for this purpose too provide fur 
adequate inter State services for the transport of goods by road and to regulate, co-ordinate and control their 
pperation, it is necessary in the interests of the public m genovral to enter into special reciprocal agreoments between 
the States of (1) Bihar (2) Haryana (3) Himachal Pradesh (4) Jammuand Kashmir (5) Punjab (6) Rajasthan 
[7) Uttar Pradesh (8) West Bongal (9) Chandigarh and (10) Delhi.

IT 1S NOW AGREED BY AND BETWEEN THE ABOVE PARTIES AS FOLLOWS : 
a 


I. That this Reciprocal Agreement shall come into force from the Ist January 1974 and shall دحا‎ valid up to 
318: December 1975. It may he renewed for such further period as may be mutually agroed to by all the signatories: 
to this Agreement. For reasons to be given in writing by any of the signatory States, this reciprocal agreement may 
be revoked on three months notice. Such revocation shall, however, abridge and modify the operation of this agree- 
ment only in so far as it relates to the withdrawing State subject to the condition that permits already issued under 
this agreement will continue to be valid till the expiry of those permits irrespective of withdrawal by tho State or 
States from this agreement. 


TI. The total number of vehicles for which composite permits shall be issued shall not exceed 200 for each of 
the States of Bihar, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, West* 
Bengal, Chandigarh and Delhi. While the States of Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh shall issue 200 
permits, the number of outside vehicles from each State entering Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh shall 
be limited to 100. The composite permits issued by the competent Transport Authority of each signatory State shall 
be valid on all National and State Highways chosen for operation. ۸ list of the National and State Highways in each 
signatory State is appended hereto as Annexure VI. ‘The competent Transport Authority shall also issue to each of 
such permit holders an authorisation in the form annexed to this agreement (Annexure I) and such authorisation 
shall correspond to the period for which the advance payment has been received provided that the authorisation at 
one time shall not exceed a period of one year. 


It shall, however, be open to any public carriers plying under such authorisation to deviate from tho specified 
routes to the extent not exceeding 30 kms. on eiher side of the speified routes. 


111. (i) Each applicant for a composite permit shall have to choose a minimum of four States, i.e., the Home 
State and any three other States out of the remaining nine for operation with effect from the date of this Agreement. 


(ii) If a composite permit holder chooses to oxclude a contiguous State for operation through which his vehicle 
must have to pass to reach any other State chosen for operation within the Scheme, the holder of the permit shall 
have to pay full taxes to the ‘transit State’. 


(iii) A composite permit holder of a State shall be allowed to operate in any other State, separately covered under 
a bilateral agreement, but the same vehicle will not be allowed to be used both for the comporite permit scheme as 
also the bilateral agreement scheme in the same State. 


(iv) An option once exercised by a composite permit holder will not be allowed to be changed before a period of. 
one year. 


IV. A public carrier operating under this agreement shall be free to operate without rostriction of routes in the 
Home State whoroas while operating in any area outside the Home State such a public carrier shall not pick up or 
set down goods hetween any two points lying wholly within the jurisdiction of the reciprocating States, i.o., in such 
cases vehicles shall be prohibited from carrying any Inter-state business. 


V. A public carrier operating under this agreement shall be subject to the following limitations and rest rictions:—y 


(1) No vehicle may be authorised under this agreement which— 
(8) has an RLW less than 10,000 kgs. in the case of rigid chassis vehicle or a tractor-trailer combination ; 


(b) is more than two years old on the date of grant of the authorisation and which is more than 7 years old 
at any time; 


(c) doves not carry the prescribed markings and distinguishing particulars and is not painted in the prescribed 
colour scheme as provided in the Schedule annexed hereto (Annaxure V) ; 


(d) is not fitted with a body in conformity with tho pattern as specified in the Schedule annexed hereto 
(Annexure ৬), 


(2) A public carrier plying under this agreement shall at all times carry a bill of Lading in the form prescribed 
in the Schedule annexed (Annexure III). Carriage of goods not in conformity with the declaration in 
tho Bill of Lading shall be construed as infringement of the condition of the permit making the permit 
holder liable under section 60 of the Motor Vehicles Act. 


(3) Such vehicles shall conform to and comply with all provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, as well as the pro- 
visions of the Motor Vehicles Rules framed by the Home State subject to such rostrictions as may be 


imposed by the State Governments from time to time under the provisions of the Motor Vehiclos Act. 
1939.

Abstract of conditions of composite permit 


1. This authorises the operation of the vehicle on all the National and State Highways in the signatory State 
chosen for operation othor than the Home State. A list of National and State Highways is annexed hereto. 
The vehiclo shall also be valid on such other National Highways and State Highways as may be notified from time 
to time by tho Union Government or the State Governments concerned and which are endorsed on the permit. 


The vehicle shall also bo authorised to deviate up to 30Kma. on either side of the specified routes. 


2. While operating in any arca outside the Home State such a public carrier shall not pick or sct down goods 
between any two points lying wholly within the jurisdiction of the reciprocating State, رم(‎ in »uch cases vehicles 
8181] be prohibited from carrying any intra-State business. 


3. Tho vohiole shall be painted in chocolate colour with broad white borders and a board showing the following 
inscription in white letters in black background shall be carried prominently above tho “Public Carrier’’ board. 


Inscription 


Permit under Special Reciprocal Agreement valid in Bihar, Haryana, Himachal] Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir 
Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Chandigarh and Delhi. 


(States not applicable to be cut out) 


Tho vehicle shall be provided with a soat across the full width of the vehicle behind the driver's scat. providing for 
spare driver to stretch himself and sleep. 


4. The vehicle shall at all times carry the Bill/Bills of Lading (in the manner directed by the State Transport 
Authority, Home State), covering the goods in the vehicle. 


&. The vehiclo shall conform and comply with all the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act as well the provisions 
of the Motor Vehicles Rules framed by the Home State, subject to such restrictions as may be imposed by the State 
Governments from time to timo under the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939. 


6. Tho vehicle shall at all times carry the original permit documents and the authorisation issued under this 


Agreement. 


7. A composite permit-holder plying under such an authorisation shall be liable to pay an annual tax of a sum, 
of Re. 200 per vehicle to the Chandigarh Administration and Rs. 700 per vehicle to such of the States of Bihar, Haryana, 
Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal for which he has 
opted in addition to the Motor Vehicles Tax and Goods Tax, if any, of the Home State. This will be irrespective of 
the R.L.W. of the vehiole and shall be paid in advanoe before the 15th of March every yoar. No annual tax will 
bo payable by outside vehioles in respect of Delhi. 


8. (i) Each applicant for a composite permit shall have to choose a minimum of four States, that is the Home 
state 000 any three other States out of the remaining nino, for operation, with effect from the date of this Agreement 


(ii) If a composite permit-holder chooses to exclude a contiguous State for operation through which his vehicle 
must have to pass to reach any other State chosen for operation within the Scheme, the holder of the permit shall 
have to pay full taxes to the “‘transit State’? unless otherwise exempted. 


(iii) An option ance exercised by a composite permit-holder will not he allowed to be changed before a period of

tion of tax or penalty as arrears of‘land revenue, 
the Commissioner may, at any time or from time 
to time, by notice in the prescribed form require 
any person from whom money is due or may 
become due to the dealer or any person who holds 
or may subsequently hold money for or on account 
of the dealer, to deposit in the Treasury under the 
appropriate head of account either forthwith 
upon the money becoming due or being held or at 
Or within the time specified in the notice (not. 
being before the money becomes due or is held) 
so much of the money as is sufficient to pay the 
amount due by the dealer in respect of arrears 
or the whole of the money when it is equal to or 
less than that amount. 


(2) A notice under this section may be issued to any 
person who holds or may subsequently hold any 
money for or on account of the dealer jointly 
with any other person and for the purposes of this 
section, the shares of the joint-holders in such 
account shall be presumed, until the contrary is 
proved, to be equal. 


(3) A copy of the notice shall be forwarded to the 
dealer at his last address known to the Com- 
missioner, and in the case of a joint account to all! 
the joint-holders at their last addresses known to 
the Commissioner. 


(4) Save as otherwise provided in this section, every 
person to whom a notice is issued under this sec- 
tion shall be bound to comply with such notice, 
and, in particular, where any such notice is issued 
to a post office, banking company or an_ insurer, 
it shall not be necessary fof any pass book, deposit 
receipt, policy or any other document to be pro- 
duced for the purpose of any entry, endorsement 
or the like being made before payment is made, 
notwithstanding any rule, practice or requirement 
to the contrary. 


(5) Any claim respecting any property in relation to 
which a notice under this section has been issued 
arising after the date of the notice shall be void, 
as against any demand coatained in the notice. 


(6) Where a person to whom a notice under this section 
is sent proves to the satisfaction of the Commis- 
sioner that the sum demanded or any part thereof 
is not due to the dealer or that he does not hold 
any money for or on account of the dealer or that 
the money demanded or ana part thereof is not 
likely to be due to the dealer or be held for or on 
account of the dealer, then, nothing contained in 
this section shall be deemed to require such per- 
son to deposit any such sum or part thereof, as 
the case may be. 


(7) The Commissioner may, at any time or from time to 
time, amend or revoke any notice issued under 
this section or extend the time for making any 
payment in pursuance of such notice. 


(8) The Treasury shall grant a receipt for any amount 
paid in compliance with a notice issued under this 
section, and the person so paying shall be fully 
discharged from his liability to the dealer to the 
extent of the amount ৪০ paid.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
DEPARTMENT OF PANCHAYATS 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 4349-Panch.—23rd March 1974.—In exercise 
of the power conferred by section 3 of the West 
Bengal Panchayat Act, 1973 (West Ben. Act XLI of 
1973), the Governor js pleased hereby to declare, 
for the purposes of the said Act, the Mauzas, part 
of the Mauza, group of contiguous Mauzas or part 
thereof specified in the column (1) of the Schedule 
below to be a Gram and to specify in the correspond- 
ing entries in columns (2) and (3) of the said 
Schedule the name by which such Gram shall be 
known and the local limits of such Gram.

PART I—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government 
Treasury, etc. 
GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


OFFICE OF THE COMMISSIONER OF POLICE, 


CALCUTTA 
ORDER 


Dated the 25th March 1974 
Whereas information has been’ received from 
credible sources that violent 
likely to take place resulting in large-scale distur- 
bahces of the public tranquillity and breach of the 
peace in the area mentioned in the schedule below 
in the suburbs of the town of Calcutta; 


And whereas I, 9. C. Chaudhuri, Commissioner of 
Police, Calcutta, and a Magistrate of the First Class 
have been specially empowered by the State 
Government under notification No. 8628-GA, dated 
the 7th December 1972, to act under section 144 of 
He Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act 5 of 
1898) ;- 


And whereas in my opinion there 15 sufficient 
ground for proceeding under the said section for 
ingmediate prevention of disturbances of the public 
tranquillity and breach of the peace within the 
said area in the suburbs of the town of Calcutta; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred 
by! sub-section (1) of section 144 of the Code of 
Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act 5 of 1898), read 
with sub-section (3) of the said section, I, the said 
S. C. Chaudhuri, Commissioner of Police, Calcutta, 
and a Magistrate of the First Class, do hereby 
prphibit from the twenty-fifth day of March 1974, 
until further orders any assembly of five or more 
persons, or any procession, or the carrying of any 
lathis or other dangerous weapons, or the doing of 
any act which is likely to cause a disturbance of 
the public tranquillity and breach of the peace 
within the said area in the suburbs of the town of 
Calcutta. 


demonstrations are . 


Printed and published by the Superintendent, Government 48 West Bengal, 
af

The area within the jurisdiction of Entally 
police-station in the suburbs of the town of Calcutta 
bounded on the—

with Munshi Bazar Road up to its junction ٠ 
with Canal South Road and Canal South 


Road up to its Junction with Pagladanga 
Road ;

with D. C. Dey Road; 


South—By D. C. Dey Road, Chingrhata Lane,

with Seal Lane, Seal Lane, Pottery Road up

Convent Lane, Palmer Bazar Road, Munshi 
Bazar Road up to its junction with South 
Sealdah Road. 


(All the roads included.) 


Eplanation.—In this Order, the “suburbs of the 
town of Calcutta” means the suburbs of the town 
of Calcutta as defined by a notification under section 
1 of the Calcutta Suburban Police Act, 1866 (Ben. 
Act II of 1866). 


Given under my hand and seal this the twenty-fifth 
day of March 1974.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


DEPARTMENT OF PANCHAYATS 
NOTIFICATIONS 


No. 4349(13)Panch.—23rd March 1974.—In 
exercise of the power conferred by section 3 of 
the West Bengal Panchayat Act, 1973 (West Ben. 
Act XLT of 1973), the Governor is pleased hereby 
to declare, for the purposes of the said Act, the 
Mauza, part of mauza, group of contiguous mauzas 
or parts thereof specified in column (1) of the 


Schedule below, to be a Gram, and to specify in 
the corresponding entries in columns (2) 


and (3) of the said Schedule the name by which 
such gram shall be known and the local limits of 
such Gram.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The object of the Bill is to provide for the appropriation out of the 
Consolidated Fund of West Bengal of all moneys required for the year 
1974-75 to meet— 


(a) the grants made by the Assembly, and 


[PART 


SS 


(1) the expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of West — 


Bengal but not exceeding, in any case, the amount shown in the 
financial statement previously laid before the House. 


2. Under the Constitution of India no money can be withdrawn from 
the Consolidated Fund of West Bengal except in accordance with an 
appropriation made by law. 


SANKAR GHOSE, 


Member-in-charge. 


CaLcurta, 
The 27th March, 1974. 


By order of the Governor, 


K. K. MOITRA,

PART I—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government 
Treasury, etc. 


GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT 
Judicial 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 2980-J..-20th March 1974,—Whereas it is necessary to reorient the 
scheme for legal aid, to provide greater benefit to poor people in respect of legal 
aid; 

Now, therefore, in supersession of the scheme for legal aid to poor persons, 
as approved by this Department Order Nos. 7055-J. and 7056-J., both dated the 
17th July 1965, and as subsequently amended by this Department Order 
Nos. 7521-J. and 11200-J., dated the 19th August 1966 and the 20th December 
1967, respectively, the Governor is pleased hereby to make the following rules 
for providing legal aid to the poor persons in this Statc: ۱ 


1. These rules may be called the Legal Aid to the Poor (West Bengal) 
Rules, 1974, and shall come into force from the Ist April 1974. 


~. Means test for deciding eligibility for legal aid: A person having an 
average yearly income not exceeding an aggregate of Rs. 2,400 is eligible for 
receiving legal aid : 

Provided that Government may relax the means test in suitable cases : 


Provided further that no means test will be applicable in the cases of serving 
or retired members of the Defence personnel domiciled in West Bengal, subject 
to the Army Act, 1950, or the Air Force Act, 1950, or the Navy Act, 1957, 
and the members of their families. The concession will not, however, be admissible 
in the cases of dismissed members of the Defence personnel or those who resigned 
or retired at their own requcst.

3. Classes of persons who may be given legal aid: (a) Civil cases. —The 
following classes of persons may be given legal aid: 


Persons whether figuring as plantiffs, defendants, appellants, respondents, 
applicants or opposite parties. 


(b) Criminal cases——The following classes of persons may he given legal 
aid : 


Persons charged with an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for 
five years Or mofe, Or persons sentenced to death, or imprisonment 
for five years or more, whether in a court of a Magistrate, a Tribunal, 
a Sessions Court or a Court of Appeul. 


(c) Maintenance cases (both in civil and criminal courts).—Persons entitled 
to receive allowances for their maintenance under the Code of Criminal Procedure 
and under Civil Laws, may be given legal aid in cases and suits for obtaining 
such allowances. 


4. Classes of cases in which legal aid may be given: (a) Civil cases.—All 
suits, applications and cases except those relating to Elections. 


(b) Criminal cases and Maintenance cases.—Legal aid will be admissible in 
the cases mentioned in paragraphs 3(b) and 3(c) respectively of rule 3 


5. The authorities competent to decide the questions whether a person is 
eligible for aid and whether he has a proper case to be taken up: (a) For the 
High Court, Calcutta, Original Side and Appellate Side and other courts in the 
Presidency Town of Calcutta, the Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, will be entrusted 
with the work of deciding the questions relating to the grant of legal aid in respect 
of all classes of cases civil and criminal : 


Provided that the Society shall take in as its members two nominees of the 
State Government. 


Applications for legal aid in the abovementioned courts may be addressed 
to the Secretary, Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, having his office in the New 
Secretariat Buildings, Calcutta. 


\ 
(b) For the districts——In each district there will be a Legal Aid Committee 
consisting of— 


id 


(i) the District Magistrate (or any other suitable officer to be nominated 
by the District Magistrate in his place)—Chairman. 


(ii) The Government Pleader—Member. 


(iii) The Public Prosecutor (where there is separate post of Public 
Prosecutor )}—Member. 


(iv) The President, District Bar Association—Member. 
(৮) and (vi) Two nominees of the State Government—Members. 


(vii) A whole-time salaried lawyer to be selected by the State Government— 
Member-Secretary. 


The Committee will be provided with a clerk and a peon. The control and 
supervision of the office of the Committee will vest in the Chairman of the 
Committee. 


Applications for legal aid with full details of the case and supporting 
documents, if any, may be addressed to the Member-Secretary of the Legal 
Aid Committee and routed through the Block Development Officer, in rural 
areas and the Subdivisional Officer in the Municipal areas. The Block Develop- 
ment Officer|Subdivisional Officer, after such enquiry, as may be deemed 
necessary, shall record his opinion as to whether the applicant satisfies the 
means test prescribed under this scheme. The Block Development Officers| 
Subdivisional Officers may, if required, nominate other suitable officers, e.g., 
the Social Welfare Officers to hold the enquiries. The Block Development 
Officer|Subdivisional Officer will send to the Member-Secretary, Legal Aid 
Committee, once in a month the applications in respect of which necessary 
enquiry about the means of the applicants has been completed, together, with 
his reports about the results of such enquiry. In criminal cases, the applica- 
tions for legal aid will, however, be forwarded to the Member-Secretary, Legal

Aid Committee, immediately after the enquiry about the means of the applicant 


is completed. Applications not satisfying the means test need not be forwarded 
to the Legal Aid Committee. 


On receipt of the applications for legal aid, the Member-Secretary of the 
Legal Aid Committee will examine the merits of the cases and the justifiability 
of granting legal aid on such merits. If necessary, he may hear the applicants 
personally and call for relevant documents from them for such examination. 
The Member-Secretary will lay before the Committee, which will ordinarily meet 
once in a month, the applications together with his opinion about the justifi- 
ability of the grant cf legal aid in each case. Legal aid will be sanctioned ۷ 
the Chairman of the Committce in those cases which are :orroye? .ا‎ the 
Committee for such aid. 


In criminal cases, the Chairman of the Committee muy, wiuhout waiting tor 
the meeting of the Committee, sanction legal aid after considering the opinion of 
the Member-Secretary and the Public Prosecutor, who is also a member of the 
Committee. Such cases, shall, however, be mentioned before the Committee 
in due course. The orders regarding the grant of legal aid shall specify in 
each case the nature and extent of such aid. When legal aid is sanctioned to 


a person, no such aid will be ordinarily admissible to the opposite party in the 
same case. 


-6. Forms of legal aid: The legal aid may be given under this scheme 
in the form of— 


(a) payment of court-fces, process fees, expenses of witnesses and all other 
charges payable or incurred in connection with proceedings in any 
court; or 


{b) representation at the cost of the Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, or the 
Legal Aid Committee in a district, as the case may be, by a legal 
practitioner provided by the said Society or Committee under this 
scheme in proceedings in which the aided person is to be so 
represented; or 


(c) free certified copies of judgments and orders; or 


(d) free preparation of appeal paper books, including free printing and 
translation of documents, wherever necessary. 


7. Selection of lawyers for conducting cases: (a) High Court and other 
courts in the Presidency Town of Calcutta——Lawyers should be selected by the 
Legal Aid Society, Calcutta. 


(9) In the districts —The Member-Secretary of the Legal Aid Committee will 
select a lawyer from a panel of lawyers drawn up by the Legal Aid Committee. 


(c) (i) For cases in the High Court, lawyers’ fees will be settled and paid by 
the Legal Aid Society, Calcutta. Such fees should not exceed 5 Gms. per day, 
provided that when the duration of the work does not exceed three hours, a fee 
of not more than 3 Gms. will be payable. 


(ii) For cases in other courts in Calcutta and in the districts, lawyers’ fees will 
be paid by the Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, and the Legal Aid Committees, 
respectively, on certification of such fees by the trying courts and the Secretaries 
of the said Society and Committees. Such fees should not exceed Rs. 25 per 
day according to the nature of the case, provided that a fee not exceeding Rs. 
12 will be payable when the duration of the work does not exceed three hours. 


8. Grants by the State Government to the Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, and 
the Legal Aid Committees in the Districts: The State Government will make 
such grants, recurring and non-recurring, to the Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, and 
the Legal Aid Committces in the districts as it may deem fit, for meeting the 
expenses of Icgal aid and establishment and contingencies of the said Society 
and Committees. 


The Secretary, Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, will draw the grant sanctioned 
by Government from the Calcutta Treasury, after the bill is countersigned by the 
Secretary or the Joint Secretary of the Judicial Department. 


The Chairman of the District Legal Aid Committee will draw the grant 


sanctioned by Government from the District Treasury after the bill is counter- 
signed by the Secretary or the Joint Secretary of the Judicial Department.

The Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, and the District Legal Aid Committees 
may 8150 receive unconditional voluntary contributions from outsiders in 
furtherance of the cause of legal aid. : 


9. Keeping and Operation of Fund: The funds at the disposal of the 
Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, and the District Legal Aid Committees shall be kept 
in the State Bank of India. The funds shall be operated on behalf of the Legal 
Aid Society, Calcutta, by the Secretary thereof and on behalf of the District Legal 
Aid Committec by the Chairman thereof, who shall be responsible for the proper 
maintenance of accounts. 


(10) Audit of Accounts: The accounts of the Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, 
and the District Legal Aid Committees shall be audited by the auditors of the 
Acountant-General, West Bengal, and reports of the audited accounts shall be 
submitted to the Judicial Department of Government annually. 


11. Submission of annual estimates: The Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, and 
the District Legal Aid Committees shall submit to the Accountant-General, West 
Bengal, the Finance Department and the Judicial Department in October, each 
year revised and budget estimates of expenditure and receipts. Dctailed reports 
of the activities of the Society and the Committees shall also be submittcd to the 
Judicial Department of Government for each financial year in April of the year 
following. 


12. Recovery of legal expenses: Costs awarded in favour of a person who 
receives Legal aid, shall be realised and credited to the State Revenues and an 
equivalent amount shall be contributed by the State Government as grant-in-aid 
to the Legal Aid Society or the Legal Aid Committce, as the case may be. 


13. Withdrawal of legal aid: The grant of legal aid may be withdrawn at 
any stage at the discretion of the Legal Aid Society, Calcutta, or the District 
Legal Aid Committee, as the case may be, for the improper conduct of the person 
receiving such aid, or his subsequent lack of interest in the case, or subsequent 
acquisition of property by him or subsequent increase in his income above the 
limit of Rs. 200 per month. 


14. Special provision: The State Government may, in a fit case, issue 
orders to settle any question relating to legal aid not covered by this scheme. 


By order of the Governor, 
B. N. MAITRA, 
Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal.

THE TAXES ON ENTRY OF GOODS INTO CALCUTTA 
METROPOLITAN AREA (AMENDMENT) BILL, 1974. 


A 
BILL 


to amend the Taxes on Entry of Goods into Calcutta 
Metropolitan Area Act, 1972. 


WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the Taxes on Entry of 
Goods into Calcutta Metropolitan Area Act, 1972, for the 
purposes and in the manner hereinafter appearing ; 


AND WHERBAS previous sanction of the President under 
the proviso to clause (b) of article 304 of the Constitution 
of India has been obtained ; 


It is hereby enacted in the Twenty-fifth Year of the 
লন of India, by the Legislature of West Bengal, as 
follows: — 


1. This Act may be called the Taxes on Entry of Goods 
into Calcutta Metropolitan Area (Amendment) Act, 1974. 


2. In the Schedule to the Taxes on Entry of Goods into 
Calcutta Metropolitan Area Act, 1972 (hereinafter referred 
to as the said Act), in serial No. 4, in item (5), for the words 
‘‘nuts, excluding betel nuts’, the words ‘‘nuts, includin 
ground nuts, cashew-nuts and walnuts but excluding bete 
nuts” shall be, and shall be deemed always to have been, 
substituted.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The object of the present Bill is to continue the provisions of the Taxes on 
Entry of Goods into Calcutta Metropoiitan Area (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973, 
by which the relevant item of the Schedule to the Taxes on Entry of Goods 
into Calcutta Metropolitan Area Act, 1972, has been amended with retrospec- 
tive effect by insertion of ‘groundnut’ and also ‘cashew nuts‘ and ‘walnuts’ 
রিল in the Schedule. This amendment was effected by promulgation of 
the said Ordinance and this became necessary in order to remove doubts. 

No additional expenditure is envisaged for giving effect to the provision of 
the said Bill.

Whereas for the prevention of assembly of five 
or more persons, or any procession, or the 
carrying of any lathis or other dangerous. weapons, 
or the doing of any act which is likely to cause 
a disturbance of the public tranquillity and 
breach of the ‘peace, I, 8. C. Chaudhuri, Commi- 
asiover of Police, Calcutta, and a Magistrate of 
the First Class, being specially empowered by the 
State Government under Notification No. 8628- 
G.A., dated the 7th December 1972, to act under 
section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 
1898 (Act 5 of 1898), issued an order under the 
৭810 section on the 25th March 1974, in respect of 
area within the jurisdiction of Entally police- 
stution in the Suburbs of the town of Calcutta as 
mentioned in the Schedule thereto; 


And whereas apprehension of disturbances of 
the public দা and breach of the peace no 
longer exists except in the areas mentioned in the 
Schedule below; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power 
conferred on me by sub-section (4) of section 144 
of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act 5 
of 1898), I, the said S. 0. Chaudhuri, Commi- 
asioner of Police, Calcutta, und a Magistrate of 
the First Class do hereby with immediate effect 
regcind the aforesaid order, dated the 25th March 
1974, except in the areas mentioned in the Schedule 
below, where the said prohibitory orders, dated 
the 25th March 1974, shal] continue to remain in 
force,

West Bengal Act XII of 1974 
THE WEST BENCAL APPROPRIATION ACT, 1974. 


[Passed hy the West Bengal Legislature. ] 


{Assent of the Governor was first published in the Calcutta 
Gazette, Extraordinary, of the 380th March, 1974.] 


An Act to authorise payment and appropriation of certain 
sums from and out of the Consoludated Fund of West 
Bengal for the services and purposes of the year ending 
on the thirty-first day of March, 1975. 


WHEREAS it is expedient to authorise payment and 
appropriation of certain sums from and out of the 
Consolidated Fund of West Bengal for the services and 
purposes of the year ending on the thirty-first day of March, 
1975; 


It is hereby enacted in the Twenty-fifth Year of the 
সা of India, by the Legislature of West Bengal, as 
follows :— 


1. This Act may be called the West Bengal Appropria- 
tion Act, 1974. 


2. From and out of the Consolidated Fund of West 
Bengal there may be paid and applied sums not exceeding 
those specified in column 3 of the Schedule amounting in the 
aggregate to the sum of rupees six hundred and sixty-eight 
crores, eighty-one lakhs and ninety-one thousand towards 
defraying the several charges which will come in course of 
payment during the year ending on the thirty-first day of 
March, 1975, in respect of the services and purposes specified 
in column 2 of the Schedule. 


3. The sums authorised to be paid and applied from and 
out of the Consolidated Fund of West Bengal by this Act 
shall he appropriated for the services and ? সি expressed 
in the Schedule in relation to the year ending on the thirty- 
first day of March, 1975.

West Bengal Act XIII of 1974 
THE WEST BENCAL APPROPRIATION (No. 2) Act, 


[Passed by the West Bengal Legislature. ] 


{Assent of the Governor was first published in the Calcutta 
Gazette, Extraordinary, of the 30th March, 1974. ] 


An Act to authorise payment and appropriation of certain 
further sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of 
West Bengal for the services and purposes of the year 
ending on the thirty-first day of Marah, 1974. 


WHEEEAS it is expedient to authorise payment and 
appropriation of certain further sums from and out of the 
Consolidated Fund of West Bengal for the services and 
2000 of the year ending on the thirty-first day of March, 


It is hereby enacted in the Twenty-fifth Year of the 
Republic of India, by the Legislature of West Bengal, as 


follows :— 


1. This Act may be called the West Bengal Appropria- 
tion (No. 2) Act, 1974. 


2. From and out of the Consolidated Fund of West 
Bengal there may be paid and applied sums not exceeding 
those specified in column 3 of the Schedule amounting in the 
aggregate to the sum of rupees two hundred thirty-three 
crores eighty lakhs thirty-seven thousand nine hundred and 
eleven towards defraying the several charges which will 
come in course of payment during the year ending on the 
thirty-first day of March, 1974, im respect of the services and 
purposes specified in column 2 of the Schedule. 


3. The sums authorised to be fe and applied from and 
out of the Consolidated Fund of West. Bengal by this Act 
shall be appropriated for the services and purposes expressed 
in the Schedule in relation to the year ending on the thirty- 
first day of March, 1974.

NOTIFICATION 


MURSHIDABAD-MALDA.—No. 5864-L.Ref—29th March 1974.—Whercas the areas contained within the 
external boundaries of the village maps of the previous survey for the mauzas specified in Schedule A below within 
the police-station® Farakka and Samserganj of the district of Murshidabad, and within the polico-station Kuliachak 
of the district of Malda have become unsuitable as units of survey and record due to the change of course of the river 
Ganges or Padma ; 

And whereas the Scttlement Officer has, after ascertaining as far as possible, the opinions of the landlords and 
tenante concerned, duly submitted to the Board of Revenue a proposal for the determinution of the areas specified in 
Sched¥le B below as units of survey and record (hereinafter roferred to as the said units) ; 


And whereas the Board of Revenue havo by their Order No. 21751 3. & S., dated the 27th October 1985, sanctioned 
the adoption of the said units in framing the records of rights under the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act, 1953 
(West Bengal Act 1 of 1954), and have submitted a copy of their said order to the State Government for issue of a 
Notification under sub-paragraph (2) of paragraph 3 of Schedule B to the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Rules, 
1954 ; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred by sub-paragraph (2) of paragraph 3 of the Schedule B to the 
West Bengal Estates Acquisition Rules, 1954, the Governor is pleased heroby to adopt the said units as the unite of 
survey and record and as constituting villages.

No. 437-Ex.—29th March 1974.—In exercise of the powers conferred by 
section 86 of the Benyal Excise Act, 1909 (Bengal Act V of 1909) and in 
supersession of rules 176, 177 and 177A of the rules published with 
notification No. 601-SR, dated the 30th March 1915, as subsequently 
amended, the Governor is pleased hereby to make the following rules, 
namely :— 


The West Bengal Excise (Rectified Spirit and Denatured Spirit Licence Fee) 
Rules, 1974. 


1. These rules may be called the West Bengal Excise (Rectified Spirit 
and Denatured Spirit Ticense Fee) Rules, 1974. 


2. The expressions used in these rules shall have the same meaning aa 
in the Bengal Excise Act, 1909 and in the rules made thereunder. 


3. The fee for a license for the retail sale of rectified spirit for medicinal, 
industrial or scientific purposes shall be Rs.200.00 per annum, and shall be 
paid in advance. 


4. The holder of a license for the wholesale sale of denatured spirit 
shall pay in advance a license fee on the basis of the quantity of denatured 
spirit sold during the previous twelve months at the rate mentioned against 
it in the following table, namely :— 


Table

10,000 bulk litres provided that any amount of fifty 
paise or more shall be reckoned as a whole rupee and 


any amount below fifty paise shall be ignored. 


Eeplanation: In the case of a new license, the license fee shall be 
levied with reference to such quantity as may be estimated by the Collector 
as likely to be sold under the license during the period for which it is 
granted. 


5. The holder of a license for the retail sale of denatured spirit shall 
pay in advance a license fee on the basis of the quantity of denatured 
spirit sold during the previous twelve months at the rate mentioned against

6. The holder of a license for the possession of denatured spirit ‘for
